chunks.t: Candidate Lifecycle Report in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Candidate Lifecycle Report helps you track the complete journey/lifecycle of candidates in your Recruit CRM database over a selected time period. It provides visibility into every stage transition a candidate has gone through, making it easier to analyze hiring progress, monitor pipeline performance, and identify trends across your recruitment process.

chunks.t: Candidate Lifecycle Report in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: The report displays candidate movement across both Hiring Stages (for candidates assigned to jobs) and Pitch Candidate Stages (for candidates pitched directly to clients). It also includes visual charts, stage-wise candidate counts, candidate-to-stage ratios, and detailed drill-down lists that can be filtered, customized, exported, or saved for future reference. • You want to track the complete lifecycle of candidates over a specific date range. • You need to analyze how many candidates progressed through each hiring or pitch stage. • You want to save frequently used report configurations for quick access in the future. Generate and Analyze the Candidate Lifecycle Report

chunks.t: Candidate Lifecycle Report in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Open the Candidate Lifecycle Report from the Reports section in Recruit CRM. Select the stages you want to include in the report from the KPI dropdown option. You can choose from: • Hiring Stages – Used to analyze candidates who have been assigned to jobs. • Pitch Candidate Stages – Used to analyze candidates who have been pitched directly to clients/contacts. Select the required date range for the report. You can choose one of the predefined ranges or specify a custom date range. Once the report is generated, you'll see: • A bar chart showing the number of candidates in each selected stage. • A summary table displaying the numerical count for every stage included in the report.

chunks.t: Candidate Lifecycle Report in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You can export the report in multiple ways: • Click Export Report to CSV below the chart to download the stage-wise summary table as a CSV file. • Click the Export icon in the top-right corner of the bar chart to download the chart as an image in PNG, JPG, or SVG format. • Click any bar in the chart to open the detailed candidate list for that stage, then select Export Report to CSV to download the detailed candidate report as a CSV file. Each bar in the chart is clickable. Click any bar to open a detailed list of the candidates associated with that stage for the selected time period. ​ • Review the candidate records for that stage. • Sort the data by clicking any column header.

chunks.t: Candidate Lifecycle Report in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: • Customize the displayed information using Edit Columns . • Apply additional filters to narrow down the results. • Perform a Boolean Search to quickly find specific records, especially when working with larger datasets. • Export the detailed candidate list to a CSV file after applying the desired filters and selecting the required columns. The Candidate Lifecycle Report also displays the Ratio of Candidates Assigned for each stage. ​ (Number of candidates in a particular stage ÷ Total number of candidates across all selected stages for the chosen time period) × 100

chunks.t: Candidate Lifecycle Report in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 📌 Note: The Candidate Lifecycle Report is based on historical stage transitions for the selected date range. As a result, the figures shown in the report may differ from the current candidate counts displayed elsewhere in Recruit CRM, such as your Dashboard statistics. Problem: The numbers in the Candidate Lifecycle Report do not match the current dashboard counts.

chunks.t: Candidate Lifecycle Report in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Likely cause: The Candidate Lifecycle Report shows historical data based on the selected time period, while the dashboard shows current, real-time counts. ​ What to check: Confirm the date range selected in the report and compare it to the time frame represented on the dashboard. ​ Resolution: Adjust the report’s date range to match the period you want to compare, and remember that the report reflects historical transitions, not only current stage assignments. Problem: A specific stage does not appear in the Candidate Lifecycle Report.

chunks.t: Candidate Lifecycle Report in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Likely cause: The stage is not selected in the stages dropdown for the report. ​ What to check: Open the Candidate Lifecycle Report and review the list of hiring stages and pitch candidate stages you have selected under the KPI section. ​ Resolution: Add the missing stage to your selection and regenerate the report. Problem: The exported CSV does not contain all the fields you expected. Likely cause: Not all desired fields were selected before exporting. ​ What to check: In the detailed list view, verify which fields are selected for export. ​ Resolution: Choose the fields again during export and generate a new CSV.

chunks.t: Candidate Lifecycle Report in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What is the difference between hiring stages and pitch candidate stages in this report? Hiring stages are used when candidates are assigned to a job, while pitch candidate stages are used when candidates are pitched directly to a client without assigning them to a job. How is the ratio of candidates assigned for each stage calculated? The ratio of assigned is the number of candidates in the particular hiring stage for the time period selected/Total number of candidates across all hiring stages for the time period selected *100. Can I edit which fields appear in the detailed candidate list?

chunks.t: Candidate Lifecycle Report in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Yes. In the detailed list view that opens when you click a bar, you can click Edit Columns and select the fields you want to display, and those fields will then appear in the list. In what formats can I export data from the Candidate Lifecycle Report? You can export the table as a CSV file and export the bar chart as a PNG, JPG, or SVG image. You can also export detailed candidate lists as CSV files.

chunks.t: Candidate Lifecycle Report in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: By using the Candidate Lifecycle Report , you can gain a clear understanding of how candidates progress through your recruitment pipeline over time. Whether you're reviewing stage transitions, analyzing hiring trends, exporting data for reporting, or drilling down into individual candidate records, this report provides the insights needed to make informed recruitment decisions and optimize your hiring process. It helps you compare multiple clients, monitor hiring activities, and analyze client-specific performance over a selected time period through interactive charts and detailed reports. • You want to evaluate the performance of one or more clients over a specific time period. • You need to compare multiple clients side by side using consistent recruitment KPIs.

chunks.t: Client Performance Report

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: Important Note: The Open API is only available to users on the "Business" plan or higher. Alternatively, organizations with formal partnerships with Recruit CRM may also qualify to access the API. Additionally, only the Account Owner can manage API keys for added security. What this feature does and when to use it? The Recruit CRM API allows external systems and applications to securely interact with Recruit CRM data using standard HTTP methods such as GET, POST, and DELETE. Using an API token for authentication, you can connect Recruit CRM with third-party tools and custom applications. • You want to connect Recruit CRM with external tools, custom applications, or reporting dashboards

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: • You are a developer implementing secure API authentication and integration workflows • You require API access to automate candidate creation, resume parsing, timesheet retrieval, or data synchronization • You want to build custom workflows and integrations using Recruit CRM data Our API Documentation is available live at https://docs.recruitcrm.io

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: While asking our API to GET/POST/DELETE the required data, one must not directly query the endpoint on the front end/webpage, as it exposes the API token. You would need to hide the Recruit CRM API token/Bearer token. This can be done by introducing a server in between or by making the API token abstract. Basically, the webpage on the front end would query a private server in between which would then query the Recruit CRM API. This is the safest way of doing this, as it would then prevent exposing the Recruit CRM API token/key publicly.

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: Also, if you encounter an error while using the API key, please ensure that you are not on a Free Trial account and generating a new API key on your end, as this may otherwise result in a 401 Authorization error ( INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS - Please Upgrade Your Plan to “Business” or “Enterprise” to gain access to the Open API). While API tokens are available across all plans for integration with Workflow Automation (accessible to all plans), access to our public API requires a Business plan or higher.

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: These restrictions are specifically designed to ensure that sensitive organizational data remains protected and API tokens are managed by trusted individuals. Recruit CRM prioritizes security by limiting API access to Account Owners, thereby maintaining data integrity. API Access: Account Owner vs. Admin Roles Even if you have an Admin role within Recruit CRM, you cannot generate or retrieve the API key unless you are also the Account Owner. This measure ensures enhanced security by limiting access to the most trusted individual in the organization. If you are an Admin user and need API access, you may: Request that the Account Owner retrieve the API key on your behalf, or

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: Ask the Account Owner to create a custom role for you with the necessary permissions to access the API token. Here are the step-by-step instructions to enable and copy your API token as the Account Owner. Scroll down and click on API to open the API section. Note: Only the Account Owner can access and manage this section to ensure compliance with security measures. Turn the toggle to the ON position to enable the API token. ​ Copy the displayed API token. Store it securely in your integration tool, backend server configuration, or secret manager. Avoid saving it in plain text files or sharing it over unsecured channels. Creating a candidate using the API endpoint

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: You can use the 'Creates a new candidate' endpoint to create a new candidate: You can also retrieve generated call transcripts via the API. In the Find Call Log via API endpoint, you can use the boolean query parameter: transcript_required . When transcript_required is set to true , you can retrieve: Transcript segments with corresponding timestamps. You can use the 'Resume Parser' API to upload a resume and automatically create or update a candidate in Recruit CRM. From the API Endpoints Documentation , select the Resume Parser endpoint, and upload the resume file in a supported format like PDF, DOC, DOCX, or RTF.

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: Once you send the request, the system will read the resume and extract basic details such as Candidate’s Name, Phone Number, Email, City, Full Address, Specialization, Work Experience Year, Work Experience Month, Current Organization, Title, Skills, Language Skills, Summary, Educational Qualification, Work and Education History and social medial URLs like Facebook URL, Twitter URL, LinkedIn URL, GitHub URL, Xing URL (if any). Duplicate handling is based on the “Allow Duplicate Candidates” setting in Admin Settings → Account Management . If this setting is on, a new candidate is always created.

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: If this setting is off, the system checks for an existing candidate and updates the record based on the parsed resume data. You can control how existing candidate data is updated using the override_data parameter. If it is set to no , only empty or missing fields are filled, and existing data remains unchanged. If it is set to yes , the existing candidate details are updated with the newly parsed information. If duplicate candidates are allowed, this setting is ignored and a new candidate is created instead. Bulk parsing or parsing multiple resumes in a single call is not supported.

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: The API endpoint ' Count candidates matching search filters' returns the count of candidates matching a set of search filters - without exposing candidate profiles or resumes. This is useful for building client-facing search experiences where you want to show how many matching candidates exist, without sharing candidate data itself. Retrieving all timesheets using the API endpoint You can retrieve a list of all timesheets from Recruit CRM using the 'Get All Timesheets' endpoint. This allows you to access the timesheet data, making it easier to integrate with external systems such as payroll or reporting tools. Fetching timesheet details using the API endpoint

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: You can fetch detailed information for a specific timesheet using the 'Get Timesheet by ID' endpoint. This enables you to access complete timesheet records, including detailed timelogs. Additionally, two response parameters, is_contractor and contractor_status, are available across the following six existing candidate endpoints: Search for Candidates, Edit Candidate, Find Candidate by Slug, Get List of candidates which are marked as off limit, Show All Candidates, and Un-assign Candidate. Problem: You cannot see the API section or API token in Admin Settings.

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: Likely cause : You are not logged in as the account owner. ​ ​ What to check : Confirm your role (account owner vs admin vs other). ​ ​ Resolution: Log in as the account owner, or ask the account owner to either retrieve the token for you or create a custom role that grants API token access. Who can manage and view the Recruit CRM API token? Only the account owner can manage and retrieve the API token by default. Admin users cannot access the token unless the account owner grants a custom role with explicit permission to access the API token. Is the API available on all Recruit CRM plans?

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: No. The API is only available to users on the Business plan or higher. Organizations with a formal partnership with Recruit CRM may also qualify for API access. Can I call the Recruit CRM API directly from my website or client-side application? No. You must not directly query the API endpoint from a front-end webpage or client-side application using the API token, because this exposes the token and can compromise your data security. Always use the API token on the server side. Where can I find the official Recruit CRM API documentation? The API documentation is available online at the Recruit CRM API documentation link: https://docs.recruitcrm.io

chunks.t: Recruit CRM API Documentation
chunks.x: Using the Recruit CRM API securely starts with ensuring only authorized users manage the API token and that it is never exposed in front-end environments. By following the role requirements, plan prerequisites, and security guidelines in this article, you can confidently enable integrations. For the full list of available endpoints, request parameters, and response formats, visit the official API documentation at docs.recruitcrm.io . chunks.t: Call Recording Laws and Consent Requirements in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: The call recording feature in Recruit CRM allows you to keep track of calls with candidates and contacts, making follow-ups easier and helping your team stay up to date. Before recording calls, it is important to understand the consent requirements that may apply based on the location of the people involved. Some countries or states require consent from more than one party before a call can be recorded.

chunks.t: Call Recording Laws and Consent Requirements in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: If a candidate or contact is associated with a region where more than one party’s consent is required, Recruit CRM automatically disables call recording. When you click the Record button, a dialog box will appear to remind you to obtain consent. You must inform the candidate/contact that you'll be recording this call, then click "I have taken consent" to continue recording the call. You plan to record calls with candidates or contacts. You need to understand when consent may be required before recording a call. You are calling candidates or contacts who may be located in different countries or states.

chunks.t: Call Recording Laws and Consent Requirements in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You want to understand why call recording may be unavailable for certain contacts or regions. In the majority of U.S. states, you'll only need consent from one of the persons participating in a call in order to record it (this is often referred to as "one-party consent"). Since you're opting to record the call you're placing, and presumably, you consent to your own recording of the call, you won't need to do anything else to comply with the laws of those types of states.

chunks.t: Call Recording Laws and Consent Requirements in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: However, approximately 13 states have chosen to require all parties' consent (sometimes called "two-party consent") in order to record the call. These states are currently California, Connecticut, Delaware*, Florida, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, Nevada, New Hampshire, Pennsylvania, Vermont*, and Washington State. For more general information on the subject, refer to Wikipedia's page on telephone recording laws on the basics of state recording laws. *Recruit CRM has chosen to include Delaware and Vermont on this list because they're tricky cases:

chunks.t: Call Recording Laws and Consent Requirements in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Delaware has some conflicting laws about how many parties need to consent, and Vermont doesn't have specific laws on the subject but, does have some relevant court cases. Several laws govern the practice of recording calls in the United Kingdom (U.K.). Unless you can guarantee that the call won't be shared with any third parties and is being recorded to either gather evidence, ensure regulatory compliance, or prevent crime, it's best to think of the U.K. as an "all-parties' consent" jurisdiction. Read more about the U.K.'s approach to call recording by referring to Wikipedia's page on telephone recording laws , Ofcom's page for the regulations , or VanillaIP's quick summary on the subject.

chunks.t: Call Recording Laws and Consent Requirements in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Irish law is clear: to record calls, you must obtain consent, so Ireland joins the U.K. and 13 U.S. states as an "all-parties' consent" jurisdiction. Irish law makes clear that the purpose of the recording should be explained in detail, so the parties participating can give informed consent. Read more about Ireland's approach to call recording at the end of the Data Protection Commissioner's FAQ page. Like Ireland, Canada has established a single set of rules for call recording, built into its electronic privacy law (PIPEDA).

chunks.t: Call Recording Laws and Consent Requirements in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Joining the other countries and states mentioned above, Canada has adopted an "all-parties consent" approach: to record a call, you need to obtain informed consent by notifying others on the call (1) that you intend to record the conversation, (2) any purposes the recording will be used for, and (3) that the call may only be recorded with each person's consent. Read more about Canada's approach to call recording by referring to the Privacy Commissioner's Guidelines for Recording Customer Calls.

chunks.t: Call Recording Laws and Consent Requirements in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: While this article has chosen to highlight certain countries above, it's by no means an exhaustive list. Since Recruit CRM doesn't know and can't enforce all international calling legal restrictions, Recruit CRM opts to display this consent message for all international calls except for Sweden and New Zealand. Before making a call to a new country, Recruit CRM recommends making sure that you and your legal team have an understanding of any regulations there, and always obtain consent if you're in doubt.

chunks.t: Call Recording Laws and Consent Requirements in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: The countries above were chosen for informational purposes; Recruit CRM doesn't guarantee that you can use the system to call any or all of these countries. This article has provided information about the law designed to help Recruit CRM's users better understand the legal issues surrounding call recording. Legal information is not the same as legal advice, the application of the law to an individual's specific circumstances.

chunks.t: Call Recording Laws and Consent Requirements in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Recruit CRM insists that you consult a lawyer if you want professional assurance that our information, and your interpretation of it, is accurate. You may not rely upon this information as legal advice nor as a recommendation or endorsement of any particular legal understanding, and you should instead regard this article as intended for informational purposes only. Using call recording in Recruit CRM can make follow-ups and team collaboration easier, but it must always be done in line with applicable call recording laws and consent requirements. chunks.t: Creating Teams In Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Teams feature allows you to organize users into teams or divisions within Recruit CRM. You can assign users to one or multiple teams, configure team-based access through Custom Roles, and generate reports to track and compare the performance of individual teams. Organize users into teams, divisions, or business units. Restrict data access to specific teams using Custom Roles. Generate performance reports for individual teams. Compare the performance of multiple teams. Note: The features described in this article are available only on the Business and Enterprise plans. Navigate to Admin Settings > Users > Teams .

chunks.t: Creating Teams In Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Click on New Team in the top right corner. Enter a name for the team and select the users you want to add to the team. Note: A user can belong to multiple teams simultaneously. Recruit CRM allows you to create Custom Roles with Team Only permissions, ensuring users can access only the records that belong to their team. For example, if you have two teams of Recruiters and you wish to give the users on each team access to only the candidate database of their respective teams, you can create a custom role with 'Team Only' view & edit permissions for the candidate module. Similarly, for each action and module, you can set 'Team Only' permission:

chunks.t: Creating Teams In Recruit CRM

chunks.t: Integrating your Recruit CRM "Jobs Page" with Wix
chunks.x: What does this feature do & when to use it? The Recruit CRM Website Integration feature provides an HTML embed option with a source link for your public job page. When you add this link into a Wix “Embed a Widget” block as a website address, your Recruit CRM jobs appears within your Wix jobs page. This lets candidates view and apply for jobs directly on your site, while Recruit CRM continues to handle the job listings and applications in the background. You need access to your Wix account and permission to edit the website. You need access to your Recruit CRM account and Admin Settings. You should already have a jobs page created in Wix, or be ready to create one.

chunks.t: Integrating your Recruit CRM "Jobs Page" with Wix
chunks.x: You will use the Website Integration option from Recruit CRM and embed it as a widget in Wix. On the top, beside your website name, click the Site Actions dropdown and select Edit Site to open the website builder. ​ In the website builder, click the Pages tab (the first tab on the left-hand side). ​ Select the jobs page you have already created. ​ If you do not yet have a jobs page, create a new page that will be used to display your jobs. Get the Recruit CRM Website Integration link: Open a new browser window or tab and log in to your Recruit CRM account. ​ Scroll down and click Public Job Page Settings . ​

chunks.t: Integrating your Recruit CRM "Jobs Page" with Wix
chunks.x: Under Option 2 - Website Integration , locate the HTML code that is provided. From this HTML code, select only the source link (the URL), and not the entire HTML code. ​ Please ensure you do not select the inverted quotes but only the source link. (Click on the above image and zoom in to see what has been selected in blue as that is the only text you need to copy) Go back to your Wix website editor page. ​ In the left-hand panel, click the + Add icon (the third icon on the left). ​ Select Embed , then click Embed a Widget . ​ Switch to the Website Address radio button so that Wix expects a URL instead of raw code. ​

chunks.t: Integrating your Recruit CRM "Jobs Page" with Wix
chunks.x: Paste the source link you copied from Recruit CRM into the text box as the website address. ​ Close the text box to return to the page layout. Click on the HTML page element you just added on your Wix page. ​ Click the Stretch button that appears above the element. ​ Turn on the toggle switch labeled Stretch to Full Width . ​ Drag the page box to the top of your jobs page and adjust its size and position until the appearance matches your design preferences. ​ Click the Preview button in Wix to see how the jobs page will look before publishing. ​ If needed, go back from Preview, make further layout or appearance adjustments, and then publish your site once you are satisfied.

Resolution: Copy just the URL from the Website Integration option again, ensure the inverted quotes are not included, and paste it into the Website Address field in Wix. chunks.t: Setting up calling in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM's Calling feature, powered by Twilio , lets you call candidates and contacts directly from within the platform, eliminating the need to switch to an external calling application. • You want to call candidates or contacts directly from Recruit CRM. • You need to use the built-in native dialer available on the Pro Plan and above.

chunks.t: Setting up calling in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: The Calling feature helps streamline your communication workflow by allowing you to place calls, optionally record conversations, and store call logs and notes within the candidate or contact record, ensuring all communication history remains centralized and easily accessible.The calling/auto-dialer feature is available on the Pro plan and above. The calling/auto-dialer feature is available on the Pro plan and above. Due to local guidelines, Twilio will no longer allow domestic outbound calls between +91 (Indian) numbers. International calls placed from Indian numbers will still be supported.

chunks.t: Setting up calling in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Based on Twilio guidelines, the phone number verification method has been updated. To continue using calling services, please verify your phone number using the new verification process added here . 📞 How to set up calling integration in Recruit CRM? There are two ways to add the calling number to the system: Navigate to your Profile section in Recruit CRM. Under the Phone field, enter the phone number you want to use for making calls. Save your profile to ensure the phone number is stored successfully. Once the phone number is added in Recruit CRM, open the candidate/contact profile. chunks.t: Setting up calling in Recruit CRM

You will receive an incoming call from Twilio to the number you added to verify the number. After answering the call, open the dialer section on your phone and enter the 6-digit code shown on the pop-up in Recruit CRM. Once added, the number will be verified. Click on the candidate's/contact's phone number and, in the pop-up window, add the phone number (if not added from the Profile Settings ).

chunks.t: Setting up calling in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Once added, click on 'Proceed', the system will show a pop-up containing the 6-digit verification code. You will receive an incoming call from Twilio to the number you have added. chunks.t: Setting up calling in Recruit CRM

chunks.t: Setting up calling in Recruit CRM

chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Transferring account ownership in Recruit CRM allows the current Account Owner to assign ownership of the account to another user. Since the Account Owner has access to billing, account settings, user management, and other account-level controls, transferring ownership ensures that the right person has administrative control of the account. Use this feature when account responsibilities need to be reassigned, ownership needs to be transferred to another administrator, or the current Account Owner is no longer responsible for managing the account.

chunks.t: Changing Recruit CRM Account Ownership

Under Account information, locate the Account Owner field and click the Edit (pencil) icon next to the owner's name. Select the Admin role user you would like to make the new Account Owner from the dropdown. Click Submit to transfer account ownership. Ask the new Account Owner to log out of Recruit CRM and log back in to access their updated permissions. Problem: I cannot select a user for account ownership transfer. Likely cause: The selected user does not have the Admin role. What to check: Verify that the user has been assigned the Admin role.

chunks.t: Changing Recruit CRM Account Ownership
chunks.x: Resolution: Update the user's role to Admin and then retry the ownership transfer. 1. Who can transfer Recruit CRM account ownership? Only the current Account Owner can transfer ownership of the account. No. Account ownership can only be transferred to a user with the Admin role. Here's how you can change the user role . Transferring account ownership ensures that the appropriate user has full administrative control over your Recruit CRM account. chunks.t: Troubleshooting Speed Issues with Recruit CRM.
chunks.x: Perform the following troubleshooting steps when: Recruit CRM pages are taking a long time to load. You are not able to click on a button in Recruit CRM. Parts of the Recruit CRM interface stop responding. Recruit CRM data does not appear or only loads partially. 1. Right-click anywhere on the Recruit CRM page and select the option labeled “Inspect” from the context menu. ​ 2.In the developer tools panel that appears, click on the tab labeled “Application.” ​ 3. In the left-hand panel inside the Application tab, locate and click on “Storage.” In the main area on the right side, find the “Clear site data” button and click the “Clear site data” button.

chunks.t: Troubleshooting Speed Issues with Recruit CRM.
chunks.x: 4. Reload or refresh the Recruit CRM page in your browser. Launch the "Terminal" app on your Mac system. You can open it using Command + Space and type "Terminal" in the search bar Once the Terminal is open, enter the following command ​ sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder You'll be asked to enter the password, it is the same password that you use to login to your computer This will flush the DNS cache. You can now visit app.recruitcrm.io to get the latest DNS information. First, you need to click on the start button and select the CMD (command prompt) tool. This will launch a command prompt window. Inside it, you need to enter the following text: ​ ipconfig /flushdns

chunks.t: Troubleshooting Speed Issues with Recruit CRM.
chunks.x: Hit the Enter button to execute the command and Windows will flush the DNS cache. You can now resume visiting app.recruitcrm.io to fetch the updated DNS information. First, you need to enter the following address in your browser’s address bar and press enter on your keyboard. ​ chrome://net-internals/#dns This will load Chrome’s net internal settings page. From here you need to click on the ‘Clear host cache' button, and Chrome will clear up its DNS cache Do I need any special permissions to follow these steps? You only need access to your own browser and the ability to open the developer tools using the Inspect option. Do I need to reload the page after clearing site data?

chunks.t: Troubleshooting Speed Issues with Recruit CRM.
chunks.x: Yes. After you click the Clear site data button, you should reload or refresh the Recruit CRM website so it can load fresh data. Clearing application storage through your browser’s developer tools is a quick way to resolve many speed and responsiveness issues in Recruit CRM. chunks.t: Connecting Your Email (Gmail) To Recruit CRM Using Nylas
chunks.x: What does this feature do & when to use it? Connecting your email to Recruit CRM using Nylas.com lets you send and receive emails from within Recruit CRM while keeping your mailbox in sync with your actual email provider. The mailbox in Recruit CRM acts as a mirror of your real mailbox, including folders and emails. You can connect up to two email accounts (on supported plans such as Business and above), choose a default sending address, and switch between connected mailboxes as needed. Recruit CRM has partnered with Nylas.com to power our email services. Initial folder syncing can take up to ten minutes, and older emails may take two to three hours to sync fully when you first connect.

chunks.t: Connecting Your Email (Gmail) To Recruit CRM Using Nylas
chunks.x: Email settings should be configured to comply with updated email protection policies from providers like Google and Yahoo, including SPF, DKIM, DMARC, easy unsubscription, and maintaining a low spam rate. How to Connect your Gmail to Recruit CRM? 📧 Go to your profile section in Recruit CRM and open the email settings. ​ In the email settings, locate and click the option to connect your email accounts. ​ On the login page, enter the email address you want to connect to Recruit CRM. ​ Click the “Sign in with Google” option if you are connecting a Gmail account. ​ Authenticate with your email credentials as prompted. ​

chunks.t: Connecting Your Email (Gmail) To Recruit CRM Using Nylas
chunks.x: When asked, allow all requested permissions so Nylas and Recruit CRM can access and sync your mailbox. ​ Confirm your permissions and continue until the account verification completes. How to Access and Use Your Mailbox in Recruit CRM 🎯 Once connected, open your mailbox from the menu bar on the left side of Recruit CRM. ​ Review your mailbox folders and emails, which will mirror your Google or other connected email provider, including existing folders and messages. ​ If you have connected more than one email account, use the mailbox switcher to change between the mailboxes of the connected accounts. ​

chunks.t: Connecting Your Email (Gmail) To Recruit CRM Using Nylas

This is just a one-time activity when you connect your email to Recruit CRM using Nylas for the first time. You can choose to expand or collapse the Folders & Labels section in the Mailbox. chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Resume/CV Formatting feature allows you to customize resumes with your organization's branding before sharing them with clients. You can add headers, footers, cover letters, and watermarks while also redacting sensitive candidate information. Hide sensitive candidate information before sharing resumes. Create client-ready resumes in just a few clicks. Resume/CV Formatting, including Text Redaction and the ability to add custom Headers, Footers, Cover Letters, and Watermarks, is available on the Business plan and above . When converting DOC files to PDF, minor formatting differences may occur.

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting
chunks.x: You can generate a formatted resume from either the Candidate Details page or by opening the candidate's existing resume. Open the Generate Formatted Resume window using either of the following methods: From the Candidate Details page, click the three-dot menu and select Generate Formatted Resume. Open the candidate's existing Resume and click Generate Formatted Resume . Under Templates, add or select the Header, Footer, Cover Letter, and Watermark you want to apply to the formatted resume. Use the Text Redaction feature to remove sensitive information, such as names, email addresses, phone numbers, or addresses. You can either:

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting
chunks.x: Enter keywords in the Text Redaction field and click Apply Redaction to remove matching text. Use the highlighter tool to manually select specific sections of the resume. Simply click and drag over the text or area you want to hide and click Apply Redaction . After making the required changes, click Save . You can optionally rename the file before saving. The formatted resume is automatically saved in the candidate's Files section. If you've created file-type custom fields, select the required field under Select Custom Field To Save File before saving.

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting

chunks.t: Tasks, Meetings, and the Task Queue in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Tasks and Meetings Page: From one place, you can view, filter, sort, and manage tasks and meetings, process pending work using the Task Queue , perform bulk actions such as updating, completing, deleting, or exporting records, and keep track of overdue tasks. You want to view and manage all your tasks and meetings from a single location. You need to work through pending tasks efficiently using the Task Queue . You want to filter and sort tasks or meetings to focus on your priorities for the day. You need to perform bulk actions, such as marking tasks as completed, updating, deleting, or exporting multiple records at once.

chunks.t: Tasks, Meetings, and the Task Queue in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You want to monitor and manage overdue tasks to ensure nothing is missed. Managing tasks and meetings efficiently plays an important role in staying on top of your daily workload. The following sections explain how to use the Tasks and Meetings page to organize and complete your work more effectively. Step-by-step instructions to navigate the Tasks and Meetings Page From the left navigation panel, click Tasks and Meetings . Use the dropdown in the top right corner to switch between the Tasks and Meetings views. ​ Use the Quick View section to switch between All Tasks , Completed Tasks , and Incomplete Tasks . ​

chunks.t: Tasks, Meetings, and the Task Queue in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You can choose between All Tasks, Completed Tasks, and Incomplete Tasks from the Quick View section. When you use the Tasks page for the first time, the system sets the Quick View to Incomplete tasks, with the Owner filter set to you, and the Due date filter set to today. If you change any filter, including the Quick View selection, that choice persists the next time you open the section, even after you log out and log back in. You can filter tasks based on the Owner, Collaborators, Status, Entity, Associations, Due Date, Added By, Added on, Related To, Updated By, and Updated On parameters.

chunks.t: How to Edit Standard Default Email Templates in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What does this feature do & when to use it? When you perform certain actions within Recruit CRM the system triggers a standard email template to help you finish your communication. These standard email templates can be customized to suit your needs. They help you quickly send emails without writing each message from scratch. You can customize these templates so the content matches your communication style, while still using the same trigger points and online links provided by the system. For setting up your email, refer to these articles: This article will help you connect your Gmail to Recruit CRM This article will help you connect your Outlook/Office365 to Recruit CRM

chunks.t: How to Edit Standard Default Email Templates in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: This article will help you connect your Email to Recruit CRM through the IMAP settings The following events trigger a pop-up of the Standard email Templates - ​ Meeting Confirmation Template Request Updated Profile ​ Submit Candidates - Online list ​ Pitch candidates to Contact ​ Submit Candidates - Email with Attachments and Candidate Grid Click on the mailbox icon in the main navigation to open the mailbox area. ​ In the mailbox area, click on Standard Email Templates to open the list of default templates. ​ On the Standard Email Templates page, locate the template you want to edit. ​ Click the pencil or edit icon next to that template to open it for editing. ​

chunks.t: How to Edit Standard Default Email Templates in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: In the template editor, update the subject line and body text as needed so they match your preferred wording and tone. You can also add attachments while editing Standard Email Templates. Any attachment configured in the Standard Email Template will automatically be included in the email whenever the template is used. Carefully review the content for any system codes, especially items like {URL} . Wherever you see code such as {URL} in the default template, do not change or delete it, because it is a unique online link to the data being sent to your candidates and contacts. ​

chunks.t: How to Edit Standard Default Email Templates in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: After updating the rest of the content, save the template so your changes apply the next time the related action is triggered. Editing standard default email templates in Recruit CRM lets you keep automated communications professional and on-brand while preserving the system-generated links that make them work. chunks.t: Deactivating an existing user & inviting a new user to your current plan
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM allows you to deactivate an existing user, invite a new teammate to use the same paid seat, and transfer record ownership when team members leave or change roles. Deactivating a user removes their access to the system but does not remove the paid license associated with your subscription. This ensures a smooth transition while preserving your existing plan and account configuration. Replace a departing teammate with a new user. Manage user transitions without losing data. Please note : Deactivating a user does not imply removing the paid seat/license from your subscription charges.​

chunks.t: Deactivating an existing user & inviting a new user to your current plan
chunks.x: Instead, the license becomes available and can be reassigned to another teammate. Please note that your subscription charges are based on the number of paid licenses in your account, not the number of active users. As a result, you will continue to be billed for any unused licenses that remain in your subscription. If you no longer need a vacant license, you can reduce the number of paid licenses in your subscription separately. Locate the user you want to deactivate and click the Edit (pencil) on the far right of the user's row. In the user pop-up, click Deactivate (bottom left) to remove their access to Recruit CRM.

chunks.t: Deactivating an existing user & inviting a new user to your current plan
chunks.x: If you do not want to reduce the license, untick the 'Deactivate user and reduce license' checkbox and click the 'Yes Deactivate' option. If the 'Deactivate user and reduce license' checkbox is not ticked, once you have successfully deactivated the old user, you can invite a new user on the same seat, without making changes to your current plan. Click the Invite Teammates button in the top-right corner of the page. Enter the new teammate's email address and select the appropriate role. Click Send Invitation to invite the user to your Recruit CRM account. The user will receive an email invitation to join Recruit CRM.

chunks.t: Deactivating an existing user & inviting a new user to your current plan
chunks.x: If you wish to transfer the ownership of records of the user that has left to the new user or an existing user, follow the steps below once the new user has joined your team: Go to " Admin Settings " and click on Users Search for the deactivated user whose records you want to transfer, or filter the list to display deactivated users. Once located, click the Edit (pencil) icon. Click Transfer to begin the ownership transfer process. Select the user who should become the new owner of the records from the Transfer ownership To drop-down and click on Submit. Confirm the transfer and wait for the success message to appear. Problem: I cannot invite a new user after deactivating an existing one.

chunks.t: Deactivating an existing user & inviting a new user to your current plan
chunks.x: Likely cause: The user may not have been fully deactivated, or no vacant seat is currently available. What to check: Verify that the original user shows as deactivated and confirm the number of available licenses in your account. Resolution: Complete the deactivation process or free up an additional license before sending the invitation. Problem: The new teammate cannot see records owned by the previous user. Likely cause: Record ownership has not yet been transferred. What to check: Verify who owns the affected records. Resolution: Transfer record ownership from the deactivated user to the appropriate teammate. 1. Does deactivating a user remove the paid license?

chunks.t: Deactivating an existing user & inviting a new user to your current plan
chunks.x: Not always. The license will only be reduced if the "Deactivate user and reduce license" checkbox remains selected during deactivation. To keep the license for reuse, uncheck the box before confirming. 2. Can I invite a new user without upgrading my plan? Yes. You can invite a new user without upgrading your plan, provided you have an available license that can be assigned to them. 3. Can I transfer records from a deactivated user? Yes. Record ownership can be transferred to another active user after the original user has been deactivated.

chunks.t: Creating CV/Resume Formatting Templates
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Resume Formatting feature allows you to create reusable Header, Footer, Cover Letter, and Watermark templates that can be applied to resumes and CVs before sharing them with clients. These templates help you maintain consistent branding by automatically adding elements such as company logos, colors, company information, cover letters, and watermarks without the need for manual editing each time. • You want to standardize the appearance of resumes sent to clients. • You are tired of manually reformatting resumes before sharing them. • You want consistent branding across all formatted CVs and resumes.

chunks.t: Creating CV/Resume Formatting Templates
chunks.x: • You need different formatting templates for different clients, industries, or job types. • You want to include a cover letter as the first page of a formatted resume. • You want to add a watermark to protect or brand candidate resumes. Once created, these templates can be mixed and matched during the resume formatting process, allowing you to quickly generate professionally branded resumes while maintaining flexibility for different client requirements. Go to “ Admin Settings ” and click on “ Resume Formatting Settings ” under CRM Process Customization.

chunks.t: Creating CV/Resume Formatting Templates
chunks.x: 2. You will now see the options: Header templates , Footer templates , Cover letter templates , and Watermark templates . You can now create customized templates for each of these. Header templates appear at the top of a formatted resume or CV, while footer templates appear at the bottom. These templates can be used to add branding elements such as logos, recruiter information, colors, and candidate details, helping you create a consistent and professional presentation. In the Header template section, click the New Header button. Enter a name in the Template Name field to help you identify the template later. ​ • Both the Cover Page and All Resume Pages ​

chunks.t: Creating CV/Resume Formatting Templates
chunks.x: Upload your company logo using the Upload Header Logo option. ​ Choose whether you want candidate details to be displayed in the header by configuring the Candidate Information option. ​ Under Recruiter Information , add the placeholders you would like to display, such as: Customize the template further by selecting your preferred background color and title color . You can check the preview of how the header will appear from the Preview section at the bottom. Click Submit to save the template once you are done.

chunks.t: Creating CV/Resume Formatting Templates
chunks.x: In the Footer Templates section , follow a similar process to create a footer template. Configure the desired footer content, branding elements, placeholders, and styling options, then click Submit to save the template. ​ 📌 Tip: If you would like your teammates to use the same header or footer templates, enable the Share with Teammates toggle before saving. Cover Letter templates allow you to include a customized cover letter along with a candidate's formatted resume or CV. You can create multiple cover letter templates for different clients, industries, or submission requirements and select the appropriate one when formatting resumes.

chunks.t: Creating CV/Resume Formatting Templates
chunks.x: Navigate to the Cover Letter Templates section and click New Cover Letter . Enter a suitable name in the Template Name field to help you identify the template later. ​ In the editor, add the content of your cover letter by either: • Typing the content directly into the editor, or • Pasting your own HTML code into the Source section if you have a pre-designed layout. ​ Use Candidate Placeholders within the cover letter body to automatically populate candidate information from their profile. ​ Customize the cover letter as needed by adding: • Other formatting elements available in the editor Once you're satisfied with the design and content, click Submit to save the template.

chunks.t: Creating CV/Resume Formatting Templates
chunks.x: 📌 Note: When a cover letter template is applied during resume formatting, it is automatically added as the first page of the formatted resume or CV. ​ Watermark templates allow you to further brand your formatted resumes and CVs by displaying custom text and an optional logo across the document. ​ Navigate to the Watermark Templates section and click New Watermark . In the pop-up window, enter a suitable name in the Template Name field. ​ Choose where you would like the watermark to appear: • Both the Cover Page and All Resume Pages ​ In the Watermark Text field, enter the text you want displayed, such as your company name or other branding text.

chunks.t: Creating CV/Resume Formatting Templates

Once you are satisfied with the design, click Submit to save the watermark template. To delete a CV/Resume formatting template, go to the CV/Resume Formatting Templates section and locate the template you want to remove.

Problem: Watermark is not visible or is too faint

chunks.t: Creating CV/Resume Formatting Templates
chunks.x: Likely cause : Opacity or text color makes the watermark hard to see. ​ What to check : Open the watermark template and review the opacity , text color , and font size settings. ​ Resolution: Increase the opacity, adjust the color to a more visible shade, and modify font size as needed, then save and preview the watermark again. Problem: Cover letter does not appear as the first page

chunks.t: Creating CV/Resume Formatting Templates
chunks.x: Likely cause : The cover letter was not attached when formatting the resume. ​ What to check : Confirm that a cover letter template was selected when generating the formatted CV. ​ Resolution : Reformat the resume and ensure the appropriate cover letter template is added; it will then appear on the first page of the CV file. Can I create multiple templates for headers, footers, cover letters, and watermarks? Yes. You can create multiple templates of each type and use them as needed for different clients or roles. Where will the cover letter appear in the formatted CV? When added, the cover letter is placed on the first page of the CV file. Can I use HTML to design my cover letter?

chunks.t: Creating CV/Resume Formatting Templates
chunks.x: Yes. In the cover letter editor, you can paste HTML code into the Source section to control layout and styling. Can I automatically include candidate information in templates? Yes. You can use candidate placeholders in the cover letter body and select candidate information options in the header template to auto-populate data from candidate profiles. How do I share templates with my teammates? Use the Share with Teammates toggle in the template settings. When this toggle is turned on, templates are shared with teammates.

chunks.t: Creating CV/Resume Formatting Templates
chunks.x: By setting up header, footer, cover letter, and watermark templates in Resume Formatting Settings, you can standardize and brand every CV or resume you send with minimal effort. If you need further assistance using these templates in your day-to-day workflow, contact Recruit CRM support for guidance. Parsing resumes and creating candidate/contact records from your mailbox in Recruit CRM.

chunks.t: Customizing your "Pitch Candidate" Pipeline
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Pitch Candidate Pipeline in Recruit CRM lets you define and manage stages for candidates you have pitched to contacts. Once configured, each pitched candidate can be assigned to one of these stages. As you receive feedback (such as positive response, rejection, or no reply), you can update the candidate’s stage and monitor how your pitching activities are performing over time. 1. Go to Admin Settings > Pitch Candidate Pipeline 2. On this page, you can now click on Customize . 3. Click on Add Stage to create your own stage. A new stage entry will appear in your pipeline list where you can define its name.

chunks.t: Customizing your "Pitch Candidate" Pipeline
chunks.x: Please note: You can have up to 20 stages in your pitch candidate pipeline. This includes a 1 default stage set up by Recruit CRM and 19 customizable stages. Note: To use these stages, go to the Pitch Candidates to Clients article and check how you can change these stages on a candidate . Now that you have set up the "Pitch Candidates to Contacts" Stages, you can change the stage on candidates and track your progress based on the responses you receive from contacts. What happens if I forget to click Save after adding stages?

chunks.t: Customizing your "Pitch Candidate" Pipeline
chunks.x: If you do not click Save , your changes will not be applied. The pipeline will remain in its previous state, and your new or modified stages will not be available when updating pitch candidate stages. By customizing your Pitch Candidate Pipeline in Recruit CRM, you create a clear, trackable process for every candidate you pitch to contacts, from initial outreach to final decision. Pitch Candidate(s) to Contact(s)in Recruit CRM (New UI)

You can also track the source of the candidates who apply through the Job Application URL/Talent Pool Page by tweaking the URL a little! For example, if you want to track candidates who have applied through LinkedIn a simple change in the job URL will help you keep track of your LinkedIn applicants. To do this, just copy the URL of the job you want to post on LinkedIn: And then add, ?source=LinkedIn after the URL as seen in the image below: If this sounds confusing, here’s a video for you:

chunks.t: Track the Source of Applicants from Multiple Platforms Using the Job Application URL/Talent Pool Page.

When a Candidate then applies through this link, the Source field for candidates will appear as "LinkedIn" inside your Recruit CRM database. Similarly, you can do this to track applicants from other platforms as well, just by adding the name of the platform after “?source=” in the URL. Since this source added gets captured under the source field, you can also run a filter to track applicants coming from a specific source using Advanced Search . ​ Note: Please make sure to add the query with the word "source" in the lower case. For example, if you want to track candidates who have applied through LinkedIn:
