chunks.t: Updating or Changing Your Recruit CRM Subscription/Account Plan
chunks.x: Recruit CRM's subscription management lets you update your plan, and seat configuration as your business needs change. Whether you're upgrading from Pro to Business or to Enterprise , switching from monthly to annual billing, or using a combination of both, these settings can be managed directly from your account. ​ Please note: On the Pro Plan , only the Account Owner can make subscription changes. On the Business and Enterprise plans, other users can be granted this permission through Custom Roles . The sections below cover the most common subscription changes and explain how to complete each one. Switching Between the Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans

chunks.t: Updating or Changing Your Recruit CRM Subscription/Account Plan
chunks.x: From the left navigation panel, select Plans . Review your current subscription plan and the available Pro , Business , and Enterprise plans. If required, use the toggle at the top of the page to switch between Monthly and Annual billing to compare the available pricing and plans. Select the plan you want to switch to and follow the on-screen prompts to complete the change. Charges for the new plan are calculated on a pro rata basis for the remaining days in your current billing cycle. The full cost of the new plan is charged when your subscription renews in the next billing cycle. Please note: If you downgrade your subscription:

chunks.t: Updating or Changing Your Recruit CRM Subscription/Account Plan
chunks.x: Business → Pro: You must remove any teams , custom roles , and custom fields exceeding the 15 custom field limit supported by the Pro Plan. You must also reduce your Sequences and XML Feeds, Custom Hiring Pipelines to 1 each , as the Pro Plan supports only 1 Sequence , 1 XML Feed and 1 Custom Hiring Pipeline . If your account exceeds the new 10,000 records per user limit, purchase Additional Records Limit add-ons or delete excess records. ​ ​ Enterprise → Business: You must adjust your records to match the 20,000 records per user limit on the Business Plan. If your account exceeds the new limit, purchase Additional Records Limit add-ons or delete excess records. ​ ​ Enterprise → Pro: You must remove the unsupported teams , custom roles , custom fields exceeding the 15 custom field limit, extra custom hiring pipelines (Pro Plan supports 1 custom hiring pipeline ), extra Sequences (Pro Plan supports 1 sequence ), and reduce your XML Feeds to 1 , as the Pro Plan supports only 1 XML Feed . If your account exceeds the new 10,000 records per user limit, purchase Additional Records Limit add-ons or delete excess records.

chunks.t: Updating or Changing Your Recruit CRM Subscription/Account Plan
chunks.x: Recruit CRM will prompt you to complete these changes before the downgrade can be applied. From the left navigation panel, make sure you are on the View Current Plan tab, then select Edit Current Plan . Choose Annual as your preferred billing cycle. Review the updated pricing and billing details. Confirm the change to update your subscription. If you want to change your subscription from annual to monthly billing, contact the Recruit CRM Support team using either of the following methods: Email the Support team at support@recruitcrm.io .

chunks.t: Updating or Changing Your Recruit CRM Subscription/Account Plan
chunks.x: Include your account details and mention that you would like to switch from annual to monthly billing. The Support team will guide you through the process and make the necessary changes. Please note: Your request must be submitted before your annual subscription renewal date . Once your annual subscription has renewed and payment has been processed, the billing cycle cannot be changed until the next renewal period. Switch some of your seats to annual billing Just like the option to switch between Monthly and Annual, you can now choose to add some of the seats to Annual while keeping some in Monthly.

chunks.t: Updating or Changing Your Recruit CRM Subscription/Account Plan
chunks.x: Login to your Recruit CRM account > Admin Settings > Plans & Billing > View Current Plan > Click on Edit Current Plan: Once on the page, ensure that the billing plan is selected to Annual (right-hand side), and choose the division of the seats between Monthly and Annual : Once you have selected the seats and divided them between Monthly and Annual , click on the review order to move on to the next page and pay for the upgrade. After each of the steps mentioned, here's how you can make a payment: Scroll to the bottom of the page and click on the Review order option to check the amount and proceed further with the payment.

chunks.t: Updating or Changing Your Recruit CRM Subscription/Account Plan
chunks.x: On the next page, you'd be asked to put in a card detail if you do not have a card on file, or change it if you wish to; and proceed further with making a payment with the charge being applied on the current transaction being made (as shown in the below image). Click on the Update Plan and Pay button once confirmed. Q1. Can I move from annual to monthly billing by myself? No. To move from an annual billing plan to a monthly billing plan, you must contact Recruit CRM support via chatbot or email. The request must be made before your annual subscription renewal date.

chunks.t: Updating or Changing Your Recruit CRM Subscription/Account Plan
chunks.x: Updating your Recruit CRM subscription plan, whether changing plan levels, or splitting seats between monthly and annual is managed from your account with clear prompts and pro-rata billing. If anything is unclear or you need help with a specific change, reach out through the in-app chat box and the support team will guide you through the process. Canceling your subscription and permanently deactivating the Recruit CRM account Adding more licenses to your Recruit CRM account

chunks.t: Pitch Candidate(s) to Contact(s)
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM lets you pitch or market candidates discreetly to multiple hiring managers/contacts without needing to assign them to a job role. You can use this feature when: You want to market a strong candidate profile to multiple clients without linking them to a specific job. You need to track which candidates were shared with which contacts for reporting or follow-up. You want to send candidate CVs and summaries as structured emails directly from Recruit CRM. The candidate won't receive an email when you send their application to a contact.

chunks.t: Pitch Candidate(s) to Contact(s)
chunks.x: This way, you can record if you shared Candidate CVs with your clients, even if the candidate isn't assigned to any specific job. Make sure your email is connected inside Recruit CRM, so you can send emails directly from Recruit CRM. Step-by-step instructions on Pitching a single candidate 1. Go to the relevant candidate’s profile. 2. Click the three-dot (ellipsis) button and select ' Pitch Candidate To Contact' . Alternatively, scroll to the middle of the candidate profile and click the Contacts Pitched widget to begin the pitch process.

chunks.t: Pitch Candidate(s) to Contact(s)
chunks.x: 3. Now you will be redirected to a page to select the contacts you want to pitch this candidate with and click on the Select fields and email contacts option (or you can mark the candidate as pitched if you have already pitched outside of Recruit CRM): 4. Select the candidate fields (including file/document fields) you wish to share with the contact, and then click on the " Generate Email" button: ​ In the File Columns section, you'll be able to select the option "Summary". The Candidate Summary will be converted into a .pdf file and attached to the pitch email. The file name generated will follow numeric order, to prevent sharing the name of the pitched record.

chunks.t: Pitch Candidate(s) to Contact(s)
chunks.x: 5. You can now see an email is generated with the fields you selected, ready to be sent to the contacts you selected individually (Recruit CRM sends an individual email to each contact listed in the To field so that recipients are not aware the email is being sent to multiple contacts): ​ Pitching multiple candidates from the list view This can also be done with multiple candidates from the list view by just selecting candidates & clicking on the "Pitch Candidate(s)" button that appears. Note: You can pitch a maximum of 20 candidates at a time. Once you have pitched the candidate(s), you will be able to track this pitch on both the candidates' & contacts' profiles.

chunks.t: Pitch Candidate(s) to Contact(s)
chunks.x: On the candidate's profile, you will find the "Contact(s) pitched" widget which has a timestamp with the name of the user who made the pitch to keep you organized. Similarly, from contact profiles: On the contact's profile, you will find the "Candidate(s) pitched" widget. Click here to know more about Pitch Candidate Pipeline Track and Update Pitches from Contact Profiles Once you receive a status update from the contact about a candidate, click on the pitch stage value and select a new stage (for example, Pitched ) from the options you have customized in your system. You can add a Remark or Feedback for future reference. Don't forget to hit Submit :)

chunks.t: Pitch Candidate(s) to Contact(s)
chunks.x: How to view a list of all the candidates I have pitched in Recruit CRM? Recruit CRM enables you to view all the candidates pitched by any team members by generating a report. This report provides a clear list based on their specific activities as a user. Access the Reports Section > Team Performance Report . Choose the team members in the report filters, and the time period. Select the KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) as stages from your Pitch Candidate pipeline , such as "Candidate Pitched - Pitched". Click on the option to generate the report . Once the report is displayed, you will see a bar graph summarizing your pitching activity. ​

chunks.t: Pitch Candidate(s) to Contact(s)
chunks.x: Click on the bar graph. This will lead you to a detailed list of all candidates the selected team members have pitched. Click here to learn more on generating a Team Performance Report Can I pitch candidates without assigning them to a job? Yes. Recruit CRM lets you pitch a candidate or market candidates discreetly to multiple hiring managers or contacts without needing to assign them to a job role. Can I record a pitch that was sent outside of Recruit CRM? Yes. When selecting contacts during the pitching process you can choose to Mark the candidate as pitched if you have already pitched outside of Recruit CRM. This records the pitch without sending a new email.

chunks.t: Pitch Candidate(s) to Contact(s)
chunks.x: By following the steps above, you can pitch single or multiple candidates. Please feel free to reach out if you have any further questions via the chatbot. Pitch Candidate(s) to Contact(s)in Recruit CRM (New UI)

chunks.t: How to Set Up Parent and Child Company Relationships in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What does this feature do & when to use it? The parent–child company relationship feature in Recruit CRM lets you link companies together as parent and subsidiary (child) records. Set one company as the primary parent company. Link other companies as secondary or subsidiary (child) companies. Create these links one by one from the company profile. Create these links in bulk while importing companies using a CSV or XLS file. Identify whether the company you are viewing has a parent company. View all contacts grouped together for related parent and subsidiary companies. See subsidiary or child companies listed on the parent company profile page.

chunks.t: How to Set Up Parent and Child Company Relationships in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: This helps you manage complex client organizations where multiple entities belong to the same group. Make sure you have access to the company’s details view so you can open the company profile and use the three dots menu. Prepare your CSV or XLS file carefully if you plan to link parent and child companies during import. The file should contain a column that clearly lists the parent company for each subsidiary. Ensure that the parent company names in your sheet match the company names you intend to use as parents in Recruit CRM, so the mapping to the “parent company name” field works correctly. Method 1: Link parent and child companies from the company profile:

chunks.t: How to Set Up Parent and Child Company Relationships in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: On the company details view, click the three-dot icon (more options menu). ​ From the menu that appears, choose the option to link the company to its parent or child company. ​ After you have completed the linking on those companies, you will see whether the company is related to a parent company when you view its profile. ​ Method 2: Link parent and child companies during import: Prepare your CSV or XLS file with all the companies you want to import, including a column that contains the parent company for each subsidiary company. ​ Start the company import process in Recruit CRM and upload your CSV or XLS file. ​

chunks.t: How to Set Up Parent and Child Company Relationships in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: During the import mapping step, map each column in your sheet to its respective field in Recruit CRM. ​ Specifically, map the column in your sheet that contains the parent company to the “parent company name” field in Recruit CRM. ​ Complete the import so that Recruit CRM can create the companies and link them as parent and child based on the mapped parent company name column. ​ Once you have assigned a parent or subsidiary company through this import process, you can view all contacts grouped together in the “Group Contacts” section on the company profile. ​

chunks.t: How to Set Up Parent and Child Company Relationships in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: On the parent company profile page, you will be able to see the subsidiary or child companies listed, confirming the parent–child relationships you set up. ​ Conclusion: The parent–child company relationship feature in Recruit CRM helps you organize and manage complex company structures by connecting parent organizations with their subsidiaries. Whether added individually or through bulk imports, these links make it easier to track related companies, view grouped contacts, and maintain a clear overview of business relationships within an organization. Bulk Importing Records into Recruit CRM (New UI)

chunks.t: Job-Associated fields and files
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Job-associated fields let you tailor the application process to the specific requirements of each job opening. Recruit CRM streamlines the process of managing candidate information by allowing you to customize fields based on the different job roles the candidate is being considered for. Job-associated files let you add, store, and share files that are specific to each job a candidate is associated with. This allows you to manage different resumes, cover letters, portfolios, or other documents for the same candidate across multiple roles. Together, these features streamline how you collect, store, and share candidate information that varies by job.

chunks.t: Job-Associated fields and files
chunks.x: You need to ask job-specific questions on the job application form. You want to store different resumes, cover letters, or portfolios for each job a candidate applies to. You can easily add and share job-specific fields for candidates, and ensure you gather the most relevant information for each position. 1. Navigate to your Admin Settings -> Job Application Form Fields Settings 2. Scroll down to the “Job Associated Files” section and click on 'Add Field': 3. Enter the field name and select its type from the following options: 'Text', 'Long Text', 'Dropdown', 'Multiselect', 'Number', or 'Checkbox'. 4. Click on the green 'Save Field' button to add the field.

chunks.t: Job-Associated fields and files
chunks.x: Recruit CRM lets you add 5 custom job-associated fields apart from the 5 default 'File' type job-associated fields in the system. How to make job-associated fields visible on the job application form? 1. Once you add the fields, turn the visibility 'ON' of the desired fields to make them visible on your job application form. Additionally, you can mark fields as 'Required' to make them mandatory for applicants to fill out. 2. Click the green 'Save' button to save your changes: 3. Upon saving the changes, the desired fields will become visible on the job application forms as well, ensuring that applicants can easily access and fill them out as required.

chunks.t: Job-Associated fields and files
chunks.x: Any changes you make in the Job application form settings will apply to all the job application forms. However, you can also customize these fields uniquely for each job application form. Accessing job-specific details submitted by candidates 📄 On the job details page, within the "Candidate Pipeline" tab, click on the "Job Specific Details" button in the candidate details section to access job-related information for each candidate. You'll be able to access the job-associated fields that you've added, enabling you to upload files, add values to those fields, and view previous values added by yourself or submitted by candidates via the job application form.

chunks.t: Job-Associated fields and files
chunks.x: Furthermore, you'll also be able to review the candidate questions that the candidate has submitted for that specific job. You might need different information from a candidate such as a different Cover Letter or Resume based on the different job roles they're being considered for. Recruit CRM makes it easy to add, store, and share job-specific files for Candidates. If one of your candidates wants to apply to 2 different jobs, say a Marketing role and a Sales role, with 2 job-specific Resumes. The candidates can now submit different CVs/ Portfolios/ Cover letters/ Other files for different jobs from the job application form.

chunks.t: Job-Associated fields and files
chunks.x: 1. If you are on the Candidate’s profile, you can find the “View Files” option under the Assigned Jobs tab. (as shown in the image below): 2. On the Job profile, you’ll find the “Job Specific Details” option under Candidate Pipeline: Once you click on the “Job Specific Details” button under each Job assignment, you’ll have the option to add/ store 5 standard files such as Formatted Resume, Cover Letter, Portfolio and an additional 2 other files for each job. These can also be Resumes formatted and Cover Letters created within Recruit CRM. This article will give you more information: Resume/ CV Formatting There are two ways in which you can add a candidate file associated with the job:

chunks.t: Job-Associated fields and files
chunks.x: 1. You can click on the “Upload file” option and upload a brand new file into the system OR 2. You can use the “Select file” option to choose an existing file from within the files section of the Candidate. How to share job-associated fields with clients? ✅ While submitting candidates to clients, you can share the fields/files associated with the particular job. To do that, click on the "Fields Shared with Clients" button and select the fields/files that you want to share. Click here to learn more about the Submit Candidates to Contact feature!

chunks.t: Job-Associated fields and files
chunks.x: On the Assigned Candidates list within a job, you have the flexibility to display job-associated fields in the List view, run Advanced searches based on these fields, and seamlessly export them along with the candidate data. Problem: New job-associated field does not appear on the job application form Likely cause : The field’s visibility is turned off or changes were not saved. In Job Application Form Field Settings , confirm the field is listed under Job Associated Fields . Verify the Visibility toggle is turned on for that field. Confirm you clicked the green Save button after making changes.

chunks.t: Job-Associated fields and files
chunks.x: Turn visibility on for the field, click Save , and refresh or reopen the job application form to verify the field now appears. Problem: Cannot add more job associated fields Likely cause : You have reached the limit of custom job associated fields. Count how many custom job associated fields are already created. Since Recruit CRM allows five custom job associated fields (in addition to five default file-type job associated fields), remove or repurpose existing custom fields if you need to create new ones. Can a candidate upload different resumes for different jobs?

chunks.t: Job-Associated fields and files
chunks.x: Yes. Using job-associated files, a candidate can submit different resumes, cover letters, portfolios, or other files for each job they apply to. Can I choose which job-specific fields and files to share with clients? Yes. When submitting candidates to clients, click Field Share with Clients and select which job-associated fields and job-associated files you want to share.

chunks.t: Job-Associated fields and files
chunks.x: Job-associated fields and files in Recruit CRM give you the flexibility to collect, store, and share candidate information that's specific to each job opening. Whether you're capturing job-specific answers through the application form, managing role-specific resumes and documents, or sharing relevant details with clients, these features help you keep candidate data organized and relevant across every position they're considered for. Bulk export files for candidates in Recruit CRM (New UI)

chunks.t: Associate notes, call logs, tasks, or meetings
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Create Associations feature allows you to link a note, call log, task, or meeting to multiple records, such as candidates, contacts, companies, jobs, and deals. This eliminates the need to duplicate activities across records. Keep related records updated with the same information. Avoid creating duplicate notes, tasks, meetings, or call logs. View the same activity across all associated records. While creating a Note , Call Log , Task , or Meeting , click Create Associations . Use the search bar to find and select the records you want to associate with the activity. You can link candidates, contacts, companies, jobs, and deals.

chunks.t: Associate notes, call logs, tasks, or meetings
chunks.x: Finally hit the Add button to save the changes. Once it's created, the associated records will be displayed under Associations . The same note, call log, task, or meeting will also appear on every associated record. For example, if you create a note on a contact's profile and associate it with a candidate, the note will automatically be visible on both records without needing to create it again. If you link them it will automatically update the Updated On field of this action on the linked record as well. If a record is deleted, all the Notes/Call logs/Tasks/Meetings added to that specific record will also be deleted.

chunks.t: Associate notes, call logs, tasks, or meetings
chunks.x: When Notes/Call logs/Tasks/Meetings on a record is associated with any other record(s) under “Create Associations”, and if this primary record is deleted, all the linked associations will also be deleted. Problem: I can't find a record while creating an association. Likely Cause: The record may not exist or may not match your search criteria. What to Check: Verify that the record has already been created and confirm you're searching with the correct name. Resolution : Create the record first if it doesn't exist, or refine your search to locate it. What happens if a linked record is deleted?

chunks.t: Associate notes, call logs, tasks, or meetings
chunks.x: If a record is deleted, all the Notes/Call logs/Tasks/Meetings added to that specific record will also be deleted. When Notes/Call logs/Tasks/Meetings on a record is associated with any other record(s) under “Create Associations”, and if this primary record is deleted, all the linked associations will also be deleted. The Create Associations feature helps you keep related records connected by allowing a single note, call log, task, or meeting to appear across multiple records. This improves collaboration, reduces duplicate work, and ensures everyone has access to the same activity history. chunks.t: Enable the 'unsubscribe/opt-out from email' link for emails sent to candidates/contacts
chunks.x: Recruit CRM gives you the option to include an unsubscribe link within your email that allows candidates/contacts to opt out of further emails from you, helping you build the right contact list and protect your email marketing strategy. You can add an unsubscribe link to your emails, manually opt records out, and later opt them back in if needed. You send bulk or individual marketing or outreach emails from Recruit CRM, and you need to comply with email marketing regulations and respect unsubscribe requests. You want to improve email engagement by maintaining a clean, consent-based contact list. Email opt-out behavior is based on the email address, not just the individual record.

chunks.t: Enable the 'unsubscribe/opt-out from email' link for emails sent to candidates/contacts
chunks.x: Opting out/unsubscribing means that all the records linked to that specific email ID will no longer receive your email communication. Bulk opt-out is not supported; you can only opt out records individually. Account Owners can customize or translate the opt-out button text under Admin Settings → Email Opt Out Settings. ​ How to include the unsubscribe link in the emails sent to candidates and contacts You can include an unsubscribe link in both individual and bulk (mass) emails sent via Recruit CRM. 1. Open the candidate or contact details page and click their email address to open the email composer. 2. Enter the email body and subject line.

chunks.t: Enable the 'unsubscribe/opt-out from email' link for emails sent to candidates/contacts
chunks.x: 3. In the top-right corner of the email composer, locate the Include opt-out/unsubscribe link checkbox and check this box to add an unsubscribe link to the email. When this checkbox is selected, an unsubscribe/opt-out link is automatically added to the email. The candidate/contact can simply click and unsubscribe from your emails: Recognize Unsubscribed/Opted-Out Profiles Once a candidate or contact clicks the unsubscribe link and opts out, their Recruit CRM profile is updated with a specific label indicating they have opted out or unsubscribed. All candidates or contacts marked as opted out or unsubscribed are automatically skipped when sending bulk or mass emails.

chunks.t: Enable the 'unsubscribe/opt-out from email' link for emails sent to candidates/contacts
chunks.x: You do not need to manually exclude them while selecting records for bulk emails. Manually Opt a Candidate or Contact Out of Emails Apart from the self-service unsubscribe link, you can manually remove a candidate or contact from your email list. 1. Open the candidate or contact’s profile. 2. Click the Opt Out of Email icon or option. 3. In the confirmation pop-up, click the Yes, Opt Them Out (green) button. The profile will now be marked as opted out, and they will no longer receive emails from you. Re-Enable Email for an Unsubscribed or Opted-Out Record If you need to start sending emails again to a candidate or contact who previously unsubscribed or was opted out:

chunks.t: Enable the 'unsubscribe/opt-out from email' link for emails sent to candidates/contacts
chunks.x: 1. Open the candidate or contact’s profile. 2. Locate the Opted out of all emails tag/button and click on 'Remove opt out from all emails' 3. When the confirmation pop-up appears, click Yes, Opt Them In . After this, the unsubscribe/opt-out status is removed, and you can send emails to this candidate or contact them again. Show and Use the Opt-Out Column on the Contact List To easily see which candidates/contacts have opted out: 1. Go to the Candidates/Contact List page and click on the pencil icon at the top right corner. 3. Ensure the Opt-Out column is turned on (visible). 4. chunks.t: Time To Hire Report
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Time to Hire Report helps you measure the efficiency of your hiring process by showing how long it takes to fill jobs and how much time candidates spend at each stage of your hiring pipeline. Using this report, you can measure the average time it takes for the entire hiring process for different jobs! Time to Hire Report measures the time between the creation of a job to when the first candidate is placed and the average time to hire for all placements for the job. You can also measure the average time for each hiring stage in your hiring pipeline.

chunks.t: Time To Hire Report
chunks.x: These metrics will not only help you get an overview of the time to hire for individual jobs, but you can also compare the time taken to hire for different jobs and how long a candidate has spent in each hiring stage. The report presents the data through an interactive bar chart and a detailed table , allowing you to compare hiring timelines across selected jobs and hiring stages. You can click most bars in the chart to view the underlying candidate records, and export both the charts and report data for further analysis or sharing. Generate and Analyze the Time to Hire Report Navigate to the Reports section from the left-hand navigation menu and open the Time to Hire Report . ​

chunks.t: Time To Hire Report
chunks.x: Choose the job or jobs you want to include in the report. • Use the Quick View filters to narrow down the list of jobs. • Perform the Add Filter or the Boolean Search to find specific jobs based on your search criteria. Once you've identified the required jobs, select them using the corresponding checkboxes, then click Select Jobs to confirm your selection. Open the KPI dropdown and select the hiring stages you want to analyze in the report. These stages are used to calculate the average time candidates spend at each stage of your hiring pipeline. ​

chunks.t: Time To Hire Report
chunks.x: If you want to reuse the same report configuration in the future, click Save and Generate Report . This saves the report settings while generating the report immediately. ​ Once the report is generated, you'll see: ​ 1. A bar chart displaying the average time taken for candidates to move through each selected hiring stage. All bars in the chart are clickable. Click any bar to view the list of candidates associated with that hiring stage for the selected jobs. ​ • Review the underlying candidate records. • Sort the data by clicking any column header. • Customize the displayed information using Edit Columns . • Apply additional filters to narrow down the results.

chunks.t: Time To Hire Report
chunks.x: • Perform a Boolean Search to quickly locate specific candidates. • Export the filtered candidate list as a CSV file. ​ 📌 Please note: One of the bars in the chart represents an aggregate metric and is therefore not clickable . ​ 2. A detailed table below the chart displaying both the average time and the actual time taken for each hiring stage across the selected jobs, allowing you to compare hiring timelines and identify stages that may be causing delays. ​ You can export the report in multiple ways: • Click the Export icon in the top-right corner of the bar chart to download the chart as a PNG, JPG, or SVG image.

chunks.t: Time To Hire Report
chunks.x: • Click Export Report to CSV in the table section to download the detailed Time to Hire report as a CSV file. • Click any bar in the chart to open the detailed candidate list for that KPI, then click Export Report to CSV to download the detailed report as a CSV file. ​ Here is how the two metrics on the Time to Hire Report are calculated: 1. Time for the first candidate to reach a specific stage = Date of specific Hiring Stage (Stage Date) - Date on which job was created 2. Average time for all candidates to reach a specific stage = Total time taken / Number of candidates in that Hiring Stage

chunks.t: Time To Hire Report
chunks.x: Total Time = [Date of Specific Hiring Stage (Stage Date) of first candidate - Date of Job Created] +[Date of Specific Hiring Stage (Stage Date) of second candidate - Date of Job Created] Problem: A hiring stage you expect to see is missing from the report Likely cause: The stage was not selected as a KPI when configuring the report. What to check: In the Time to Hire Report setup, review which KPIs (hiring stages) are selected. Resolution: Re-run the report and ensure the required hiring stages are selected in the KPI list before generating. Likely cause: You may not be clicking the correct menu icons on the graph or table.

chunks.t: Time To Hire Report
chunks.x: What to check: For the graph, look for the three lines icon on the top right corner. For the table, look for the Export Report to CSV button at the top corner of the table. Resolution: Click the appropriate icon and select the desired export format (PNG, JPG, SVG for graphs). How is “time for the first candidate to reach a specific stage” calculated? Time for the first candidate to reach a specific stage is calculated as: Date of specific hiring stage (stage date) − Date the job was created. This shows how long it took from job creation until the first candidate reached that stage. How is the “average time for all candidates to reach a specific stage” calculated?

chunks.t: Time To Hire Report
chunks.x: Average time for all candidates to reach a specific stage is: Total time taken ÷ Number of candidates in that hiring stage. The total time is the sum of each candidate’s time to reach that stage. How is “total time” defined in this report? Total time is calculated by adding together - [Date of Specific Hiring Stage (Stage Date) of first candidate - Date of Job Created] +[Date of Specific Hiring Stage (Stage Date) of second candidate - Date of Job Created] What does the Time to Hire Report measure at the job level? The time from job creation to when the first candidate is placed in that job. The average time to hire for all placements in that job.

chunks.t: Time To Hire Report
chunks.x: The average time spent in each hiring stage for that job. Can I save and reuse a Time to Hire Report setup? Yes. When generating the report, you can choose Save and Generate Report . This saves the report configuration, and you can later view and edit all saved reports instead of reconfiguring from scratch.

chunks.x: Recruit CRM's Texting feature, powered by Twilio, allows you to send and receive SMS messages with candidates and contacts directly from within Recruit CRM. You can manage one-to-one or bulk SMS outreach, use reusable SMS templates with placeholders, view conversation history from the record, and monitor SMS usage and costs, all without leaving the platform. Step-by-step guide to set up texting in Recruit CRM Before you can send or receive SMS messages, you must purchase calling and texting credits for your Recruit CRM account. Go to Admin Settings in Recruit CRM and scroll down and open Phone Calling & SMS Settings . ​ Navigate to the Account Credits & Usage section.

chunks.t: Texting & WhatsApp Messaging Candidates/Contacts in RecruitCRM

chunks.t: Texting & WhatsApp Messaging Candidates/Contacts in RecruitCRM
chunks.x: SMS cost is calculated after the message is delivered , based on the number of segments used. This includes messages with emojis , non-GSM characters , and regular English text . Because the cost depends on segments, the final amount charged may differ slightly from the "expected" SMS cost you see before sending the message. ​ You can learn more about how segments are calculated from this Twilio Article on Segments. To estimate the number of segments in your message, you can also use the Twilio Segment Calculator . Carrier charges are also calculated per segment .

chunks.t: Texting & WhatsApp Messaging Candidates/Contacts in RecruitCRM

For other delivery statuses - sent, delivered, undelivered, or delivery unknown - we charge the normal full cost: ​ Total cost = 25% of [message cost + carrier cost] A charge of $0.05 per unique recipient will be deducted immediately when a message is sent to a unique recipient for the first time in a calendar month. chunks.t: How to Whitelist an IP address on Recruit CRM?
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? IP whitelisting in Recruit CRM lets you specify a list of trusted IP addresses that are allowed to access your Recruit CRM account to help protect your organization’s data from unauthorized access. Recruit CRM checks the IP address of each login attempt. If the IP address is in your trusted list, the user can log in (subject to their normal credentials). If the IP address is not in the trusted list, the user will see an IP restriction error and will not be able to log in. You can use this feature when you want to: Allow logins only from your office network or company VPN. Prevent unauthorized access from unknown or public networks.

chunks.t: How to Whitelist an IP address on Recruit CRM?
chunks.x: Strengthen compliance with internal security policies that require IP-based access control. This feature is available only on the Business Plan and Enterprise plan. Only the Account Owner and users on the Custom roles with permissions to access 'Account' settings in the Admin Settings have access to this feature. The IP address restriction is applicable for all users except the Account Owner. But if you do not wish to have the IP restriction for certain users on your team, you can create a custom role and disable the IP Restriction for just the users on this role.

chunks.t: How to Whitelist an IP address on Recruit CRM?
chunks.x: You can create the custom roles from Admin Settings > Users > Roles & Permissions . Here is a quick article on creating custom roles: Creating Teams & User Roles in Recruit CRM . 1. Go to Admin Settings and open Account under Account Management. 2. On the Account Management page, scroll down until you see the IP Whitelisting section and you'll see the box where you can add the trusted IP addresses. The system will automatically show your current IP address there, so you can easily add it to your trusted list. 3. You can enter the trusted IP addresses in the box and once complete, click outside the text box to save the IP restriction settings.

chunks.t: How to Whitelist an IP address on Recruit CRM?
chunks.x: After you have set this up, users will be restricted from logging in from IP addresses that have not been whitelisted. If a user tries to log in, from an IP address that is not marked as trusted, they will get the following error: Problem: User cannot log in and sees an IP restriction error Likely cause : The user is trying to access Recruit CRM from an IP address that is not whitelisted. Confirm the user’s current IP address (ask them to share their IP). Compare the user’s IP address with the list of trusted IP addresses in Admin Settings > Account > IP Whitelisting. Check whether the user is assigned to a custom role with IP restriction disabled.

chunks.t: How to Whitelist an IP address on Recruit CRM?
chunks.x: Add the user’s IP address to the trusted IP list, or Ask the user to connect via a whitelisted network (for example, office or VPN), or Assign the user to a custom role where IP restriction is disabled, if appropriate. IP whitelisting in Recruit CRM helps control which IP addresses are allowed to access your account to improve data security and manage login access for your teams. chunks.t: Deals by Teammates/Team
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Deals by Teammates/Teams report provides a comprehensive view of your deal pipeline, helping you monitor revenue opportunities and track how deals are progressing across different deal stages. It enables you to compare the performance of individual teammates and teams by analyzing deal counts, deal values, weighted deal values, and stage distribution over a selected time period. • You want to see how many deals each teammate or team is managing across different deal stages. • You need to monitor the value and progress of revenue opportunities in your deal pipeline. • You want to compare deal performance between individual teammates and teams.

chunks.t: Deals by Teammates/Team
chunks.x: • You need to export deal data or charts for reporting, presentations, or further analysis. Generate and Analyze the Deals by Teammates/Teams Report 1. Open the Deals by Teammates and Teams Report Navigate to the Reports section from the left-hand navigation menu. Open the Deals Report , then select Deals by Teammates/Teams . Choose the team members you want to include in the report from the user dropdown. If you want to view the combined performance of all selected users, select Total Deal Statistics . Alternatively, select individual team members to generate recruiter-specific reports.

chunks.t: Deals by Teammates/Team
chunks.x: If you're on the Business Plan or above , you can also select one or more Teams along with the team members to generate team-level reports. Open the Deal Stages (KPI) dropdown and select the deal stages or metrics you want to include in the report. ​ Choose the required date range for the report. You can select one of the predefined ranges or specify a Custom Date Range by choosing the desired start and end dates. You can also choose whether the report should be based on the deal's: • Added On date – The date the deal was created in Recruit CRM. • Close Date – The date the deal was marked as closed.

chunks.t: Deals by Teammates/Team
chunks.x: If you plan to reuse the same report configuration in the future, click Save and Generate Report to save the report settings while generating the report immediately. Once the report is generated, you'll see interactive charts displaying the selected deal statistics. The report provides two different ways to analyze your deal pipeline: • Numbers – Displays a bar chart showing the number of deals in each deal stage for the selected team members or teams during the chosen date range. • Value – Displays the percentage distribution of the total deal value across the different deal stages. ​ Click any bar to open a detailed list of the deals associated with that stage for the selected time period.

chunks.t: Deals by Teammates/Team
chunks.x: • Sort the data by clicking any column header. • Customize the displayed information using Edit Columns . • Apply additional filters to narrow down the results. • Perform a Boolean Search to quickly locate specific deals. • Export the filtered deal list as a CSV file. Review Deal Value and Weighted Deal Value: Below the bar chart, you'll find two donut charts that provide additional insights into your deal pipeline. This chart shows the percentage distribution of the total deal value across each deal stage.

chunks.t: Deals by Teammates/Team
chunks.x: For example, if there are six deals in the In Progress stage, the total value of those six deals is added together, divided by the total value of deals across all stages, and then converted into a percentage. This chart displays the percentage distribution based on each deal's weighted value rather than its actual value. It calculates the total weighted value of deals in each stage, divides it by the weighted value of deals across all stages, and converts the result into percentages. ​

chunks.t: Deals by Teammates/Team
chunks.x: The bar chart displays historical data , showing every deal stage a deal passed through during the selected date range. As a result, a deal may appear in multiple stages if it moved through them within that period. The Deals by Value and Deals by Weighted Value donut charts display live data , meaning each deal is counted only in its current stage at the time the report is generated. You can export the report in multiple ways: • Click Export Report to CSV to download the detailed report data as a CSV file. • Click the Export icon in the top-right corner of any chart to download it as a PNG, JPG, or SVG image.

chunks.t: Deals by Teammates/Team
chunks.x: • Click any bar in the chart to open the detailed candidate list for that stage, then select Export Report to CSV to download the detailed candidate report as a CSV file. Problem: The Teams option is not available in the report Likely cause : The account is not on the Business Plan or higher. What to check : Confirm the current subscription plan. Resolution: Upgrade to the Business Plan or above to access team-level reporting. Problem: The numbers in the bar graph do not match the donut charts Likely cause : The bar graph shows historical data, while the donut charts show live data. What to check : Confirm whether you are expecting historical stage movement or current stage distribution.

chunks.t: Deals by Teammates/Team
chunks.x: Resolution : Use the bar graph when analyzing all stages deals passed through in the selected timeframe, and use the donut charts when you need current-stage snapshots. Problem: Deals are missing from the report for the expected period Likely c ause : The wrong date filter (added on vs close date) or date range is selected. What to check : Verify whether the filter is set to “added on date” or “close date,” and confirm the chosen date range. Resolution : Adjust the date type and range to match how you want to filter deals (by creation or by closure). Problem: Cannot see specific fields in the detailed deal view Likely cause: The required columns are not enabled in the detailed view.

chunks.t: Deals by Teammates/Team
chunks.x: What to check: In the detailed deals view, open the column settings from the top right corner. Resolution: Edit the columns and select the specific deal details you want to display, then re-run or refresh the view. What does the Deals by Teammates and Teams report show? It shows the number and value of deals in different deal stages for selected team members and, on Business Plan and above, for teams, along with historical bar graphs, live donut charts, and a detailed table. Who can use the Teams part of the report? Only users on the Business Plan and above can use the Teams report functionality. What is the difference between deals by value and deals by weighted value?

chunks.t: Deals by Teammates/Team
chunks.x: Deals by value show the percentage share of total deal value per stage. Deals by weighted value add the weighted deal value of deals in a stage, divide it by the total weighted deal value across all stages, and then convert that into a percentage. How are percentages calculated in the value chart? For example, if there are six deals in the “In Progress” stage, the system adds the deal value of those six deals, divides that sum by the total deal value of deals across all stages, and converts the result into a percentage. Can I export charts and tables from this report?

chunks.t: Deals by Teammates/Team
chunks.x: Yes. You can export bar and donut charts as PNG, JPG, or SVG from the top-right corner of each chart, and you can export detailed tables and deal lists as CSV using the Export to CSV button. The Deals by Teammates and Teams report in Recruit CRM gives you clear visibility into deal volume, value, and stage distribution across your users and teams, with flexible filters and export options for deeper analysis.

chunks.t: Integrating Recruit CRM with your LogicMelon account
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM has partnered with LogicMelon to make job posting easier for you! ​ With a few simple steps, you can integrate your LogicMelon account with Recruit CRM and use their multiposting feature to distribute your job posts across multiple job boards. The interface allows you to post jobs to multiple boards, directly to your company website, and across all your social media networks at the same time. You must be on the Recruit CRM Business plan or Enterprise plan to use the LogicMelon integration. You must have your LogicMelon username, password, and API key available.

You can: Create a PDF or Word (.docx) report with candidates you select from the job pipeline. Customize sections such as the Executive Search Title (cover page), Candidate List, Candidate Profile, custom pages, and Team. Insert placeholders for job, candidate, company, contact, user, and job statistics data. Control formatting, section order, and visibility of individual sections. Decide whether empty placeholders show fallback text or appear as blank spaces.

chunks.t: How to generate an executive search report in Recruit CRM?
chunks.x: The revamped version provides enhanced formatting options, improved placeholder management, and better section organization, so reports are more flexible and client-ready. You need permission to use the “Submit to Client” action for that job. To configure candidate summary templates and placeholder behavior, you need access to Admin Settings. chunks.t: How to generate an executive search report in Recruit CRM?

chunks.t: How to generate an executive search report in Recruit CRM?

chunks.t: Email Scheduling in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Email Scheduling in Recruit CRM lets you compose an email now and schedule it to be sent automatically at a specific future date and time. Recruit CRM will deliver the email exactly as scheduled, even if you are offline. This feature allows you to plan and automate your communication, ensuring your emails are delivered exactly when you want them to be. Send emails to candidates or clients at a specific time. 1. Open the email composer from either the candidate/contact list view or the detailed profile view in Recruit CRM. You cannot bulk-select candidates/contacts and schedule emails. To send a scheduled email to multiple recipients, manually enter each email address in the To field.

chunks.t: Email Scheduling in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Please note that you can add up to 10 recipients per email at a time, and this feature is available on all plans. 2. Write your email as usual, then click the clock icon next to the Send button. This option is labelled Send Later and opens the scheduling window. 3. Select the date and time you want the email to be sent based on your time zone and hit the schedule button. When scheduling an email, you can select from which connected email you wish to send the email: ​ NOTE: 2 email connection is only available for users in the Business Plan. Save your settings to schedule the email. Recruit CRM will automatically send the email at the selected time, even if you are offline.

chunks.t: Email Scheduling in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: It's worth noting that you need to select a date and time at least 15 minutes ahead of the current time. For example, if the current time is 1:43 PM, selecting 1:45 PM will not allow you to schedule the email. Make sure to set the time for 1:58 PM or later to ensure your email is properly scheduled. All the emails you have scheduled will appear in your mailbox under the " Scheduled Emails " tab. Please note that you'll be able to view only your own scheduled emails, not those of your team members. If a scheduled email fails to send, you can easily reschedule it from the "Scheduled Emails" section in your mailbox, ensuring your important messages still reach their intended recipients.

chunks.t: Email Scheduling in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Here are some important limits to keep in mind when scheduling emails: 1. Per Slot Limit: Each user can schedule up to 20 emails within any 5-minute slot. Note that if there are 3 recipients in an email, it will be counted as 3 separate emails, since our bulk email functionality sends individual emails to each recipient. 2. Daily Limit: Users can schedule up to 100 emails per day, based on the GMT zone over 24 hours. 3. Recipient Limit: You can add a maximum of 10 recipients per email. Problem: I can’t select the time I want; the system won’t let me schedule. Likely cause: The selected time is too close to the current time.

chunks.t: Email Scheduling in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What to check: Confirm the time you’re choosing is at least 15 minutes ahead of the current time. Resolution path: Adjust the scheduled time to be 15 minutes or more in the future (for example, from 1:45 PM to 1:58 PM or later) and try scheduling again. Problem: My scheduled email did not send at the planned time. Likely cause: The send may have failed due to email provider issues or temporary connectivity problems. What to check: Go to your mailbox and open the Scheduled Emails tab to see the status of the email. Resolution path: If the email shows as failed, open it from the Scheduled Emails section and reschedule it for a new time.

chunks.t: Email Scheduling in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 🎥 Here's a tutorial on how to schedule emails in Recruit CRM Can I schedule emails to multiple candidates at once using bulk select? No. You cannot bulk-select candidates or contacts to schedule a single email to all of them. You must manually enter each recipient’s email address in the To field, and you can add up to 10 recipients per scheduled email. What happens if I add multiple recipients to one scheduled email? Each recipient is counted as a separate email , because Recruit CRM’s bulk email functionality sends individual emails to each recipient. For example, one email with 3 recipients counts as 3 emails towards your per-slot and daily limits.

chunks.t: Email Scheduling in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Email Scheduling in Recruit CRM allows you to send candidate and client emails automatically at the time you choose. It helps you stay organized and maintain timely communication with less manual effort. By following the steps in this guide, you can easily schedule and manage your emails with confidence. chunks.t: Notes Restriction in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM allows users to add notes to records such as candidates, companies, contacts, jobs, and deals. The actions users can perform on notes such as adding, viewing, editing, or deleting, depend on their assigned role or custom role permissions. Control who can add, view, edit, or delete notes. Manage note permissions based on user roles. Configure note access using Custom Roles. Note: Note permissions work differently depending on whether your organization is on the Pro Plan or the Business Plan .

chunks.t: Notes Restriction in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: On the Pro Plan, the " Role " of the user would determine whether they can view, edit or delete the notes. The basic logic that applies to restrictions around notes is that when you are able to view a record, you can add notes to it. But you cannot delete a note unless you are the Admin or the Account Owner. Following are the 4 default roles and the restrictions that they have around notes: Account Owner: An account owner has access to the entire database. So they can add, view, edit, and delete any note associated with any record. Admin: The admin can also add, view edit, and delete any note associated with any record.

chunks.t: Notes Restriction in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Team Member: A team member can only add, edit, and view all the notes but cannot delete any notes from the database. Restricted Team Member: A restricted team member can only add and edit notes on the records that they have added to the system or made collaborators on. They won't be able to delete any notes P.S. It's set up like this to avoid data loss that happens due to the deletion of notes. 2. Notes permissions on the Business Plan

chunks.t: Notes Restriction in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: On the Business Plan, the determining factor to add, view, edit, or delete the notes depends upon the permission of the role the user is assigned. Apart from the four default user roles, on the Business Plan, you can create new roles with custom access to the database. The permissions configured for each entity determine what actions users can perform on notes associated with that entity. For example, if a user has permission to: They can view and edit all notes under the candidates, but cannot delete notes that are added on candidates that are not owned by them. The same permissions apply to notes associated with the following entities: Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Jobs, Deals.

chunks.t: Notes Restriction in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: In cases, where the note is added to a candidate who is owned by the user and associated with records that are not owned by them, they can still delete the notes from all the records as they have the delete permission for the candidate record, which was the primary record where the note was added. Likely Cause: The user's role or Custom Role does not include permission to delete notes. What to Check: Verify the user's assigned role. If you're on the Business Plan, review the Delete permission configured for the relevant entity in the user's Custom Role. Resolution: Update the user's role or modify the Custom Role permissions if the user should be allowed to delete notes.

chunks.t: Notes Restriction in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 1. Can Team Members delete notes on the Pro Plan? No. Only Account Owners and Admins can delete notes on the Pro Plan. 2. Can I customize note permissions on the Business Plan? Yes. Note permissions are determined by the Custom Role permissions configured for each entity. 3. Why can a user delete a note associated with multiple records? The permission is determined by the ownership of the primary record where the note was originally created. Recruit CRM provides flexible note permissions based on user roles and Custom Roles, allowing administrators to control who can add, view, edit, and delete notes while protecting important information from accidental deletion.

chunks.t: Customize Your Hiring Pipeline And Create Multiple Hiring Pipelines
chunks.x: What does this feature do & when to use it? The multiple hiring pipeline feature in Recruit CRM lets you: Maintain a master hiring pipeline that contains all stages you might use across jobs. Create custom hiring pipelines that use selected stages from the master pipeline. This supports flexible, role-specific workflows while preserving consistent tracking, automation, and reporting. You can use this when: You hire for different types of roles and need separate hiring pipelines for each. You need to control which stages clients can see and use when reviewing submitted candidates. Pro plan users can have one master (default) hiring pipeline and create one custom hiring pipeline.

chunks.t: Customize Your Hiring Pipeline And Create Multiple Hiring Pipelines
chunks.x: Business plan users can create multiple custom hiring pipelines. Only users in admin or account owner roles can customize the hiring pipeline. Users on the Business plan and above can also create custom roles with access to the hiring pipeline. Recruit CRM includes default stages that are system-locked across both the master hiring pipeline and all custom hiring pipelines. These locked stages include: Assigned, Applied, Placed (final stage in the pipeline).

chunks.t: Customize Your Hiring Pipeline And Create Multiple Hiring Pipelines
chunks.x: Locked stages cannot be edited, renamed, reordered, or removed in any pipeline.They are locked because the platform relies on them for core system functions such as application tracking, workflow automation, and consistent reporting across all jobs. Maintaining these stages ensures data accuracy and prevents workflow inconsistencies. All stages you want to use in any custom hiring pipeline must first be added to the master hiring pipeline. How to Customize the Master Hiring Pipeline 💫 Under CRM Process, click Hiring Pipeline. ​ Click the Edit button at the top right to start adding or changing hiring stages. ​ Click the blue Add Stage button to add a new hiring stage. ​

chunks.t: Customize Your Hiring Pipeline And Create Multiple Hiring Pipelines
chunks.x: Type the name of the new hiring stage in the field provided. To reorder a stage, click and drag the small equal-to icon next to the hiring stage to its new position in the pipeline. ​ You will also see a checkbox with the option "Let clients use" next to each hiring stage. If you have ticked the checkbox then, once you share your online " Submit Candidate " link, your clients will be able to move the candidates across the hiring stages you have ticked ​ To remove a hiring stage, click the X icon on the right of that stage. ​ After all additions, removals, and changes are complete, click Submit to save the updated master hiring pipeline. How to Create a Custom Hiring Pipeline? 👷

chunks.t: Customize Your Hiring Pipeline And Create Multiple Hiring Pipelines
chunks.x: Make sure all the hiring stages you need are already added to the master hiring pipeline. ​ Click the green Create New Hiring Pipeline button. ​ Enter a name for the new custom hiring pipeline. ​ Use the green Visibility toggle next to each stage to turn visibility on for stages you want to include in this custom pipeline, and off for stages you want to exclude. ​ Reorder the visible hiring stages by dragging them into the desired sequence in the pipeline. Once all changes are made, click Submit to save the new custom hiring pipeline. ​ After saving, you can mark this custom pipeline as the default pipeline if desired. ​ How to Choose the Hiring Pipeline for Each Job? 💼

chunks.t: Customize Your Hiring Pipeline And Create Multiple Hiring Pipelines
chunks.x: When adding a new job, the hiring pipeline marked as default will be selected automatically. ​ For existing jobs, click on the pencil icon to open the job in edit mode to change the hiring pipeline. ​ Within the job edit view, locate the hiring pipeline option. ​ When editing a job, note that the pipeline currently marked as default will still appear as the default choice and then Save to update the job. ​ Handling warnings when changing pipelines on existing jobs While selecting a new pipeline when editing a Job the system will give you a warning if some of the candidates in the job are in hiring stages that are not available in the new pipeline selected:

chunks.t: Customize Your Hiring Pipeline And Create Multiple Hiring Pipelines
chunks.x: You can then move the candidates to one of the stages available in the new pipeline selected and then make the changes. Problem: Clients cannot move candidates between certain stages Likely cause: The Let Clients Use checkbox is not enabled for those stages. What to check: In the master hiring pipeline, review the Let Clients Use setting for each relevant stage. Resolution: Tick the Let Clients Use checkbox for the stages you want clients to manage, then save the pipeline. Problem: Cannot create more than one custom hiring pipeline Likely cause: Account is on the Pro plan, which allows only one custom pipeline in addition to the master pipeline.

chunks.t: Customize Your Hiring Pipeline And Create Multiple Hiring Pipelines
chunks.x: What to check: Confirm the current plan (Pro or Business). Resolution: On Pro, manage within the one allowed custom pipeline. To create multiple custom pipelines, upgrade to the Business plan. Who can customize the hiring pipeline in Recruit CRM? Only users in admin or account owner roles can customize the hiring pipeline. On the Business plan and above, custom roles with access to the hiring pipeline can also be created. What is the difference between the master hiring pipeline and custom hiring pipelines?

chunks.t: Customize Your Hiring Pipeline And Create Multiple Hiring Pipelines
chunks.x: The master hiring pipeline contains all possible hiring stages and is the source for stages used in custom hiring pipelines. Custom hiring pipelines are built by turning visibility on or off for selected stages from the master pipeline and reordering them as needed. Why are some stages like Assigned, Applied, and Placed locked? These stages are system-locked because the platform relies on them for core system functions such as application tracking, workflow automation, and consistent reporting across all jobs. They cannot be edited, renamed, reordered, or removed.

chunks.t: Customize Your Hiring Pipeline And Create Multiple Hiring Pipelines
chunks.x: By configuring your master hiring pipeline and setting up custom hiring pipelines, you can tailor Recruit CRM to match different hiring workflows while keeping core tracking and reporting consistent. chunks.t: Creating title and candidate profile templates for executive search reports
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Generating a complete search report for your client for executive or C-suite roles is made simple with Recruit CRM's " Executive Search Report " feature. Create pre-designed templates for your Executive Search Report to make your work faster and easier. Customize title pages, candidate profiles, and candidate summaries. Reuse report templates across multiple executive searches. This feature is available on the Business plan and above. You must be an Account Owner, Admin, or have access to Admin Settings to create and manage Executive Search Report templates. How to create an Executive Search Report template?

chunks.t: Creating title and candidate profile templates for executive search reports
chunks.x: Navigate to Admin Settings → CRM Process Customization → Executive Search Report Settings . Click Create Executive Search Report Template. Enter a name for your template in the Template Name field. Then, customize the Executive Search Title section by editing the content, adding a header or logo, formatting the layout, and using placeholders to automatically populate information from Jobs , Companies , Contacts , and Users (Recruiters) . Customize the Candidate List section as required.

chunks.t: Creating title and candidate profile templates for executive search reports
chunks.x: Customize the Candidate Profile section by formatting the layout, right-clicking the table to add rows, columns, or cells, and using candidate placeholders. All candidate fields will be available as placeholders here. The Candidate Summary, Work History, and Education History placeholders automatically populate candidate details. You can also choose which work and education history fields to display, with work_history_1 / education_history_1 being the most recent and work_history_10 / education_history_10 the oldest. Similarly, you can customize the Team section:

chunks.t: Creating title and candidate profile templates for executive search reports
chunks.x: Add Custom Pages if you want to include additional information in the report. You can add placeholders for Jobs , Contacts , Companies , Users , and Job Statistics , and reorder custom pages as needed. Executive Search Report templates help you create professional, branded reports for executive hiring by allowing you to customize every section, automatically populate data using placeholders, and reuse templates across multiple searches. chunks.t: Integrating Totaljobs with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use this? Integrate your Recruit CRM account with Totaljobs , one of the UK's largest job boards and automate the process of posting open jobs from within Recruit CRM to your Totaljobs feed. This removes the need to manually recreate job listings on Total Jobs and keeps your external job board feed aligned with jobs in Recruit CRM. You want to post open jobs from Recruit CRM directly to your Total Jobs feed. You want a simple, two-step setup for job board posting. You must be an Account Owner in Recruit CRM to set up the Total Jobs integration. You need an active Total Jobs account with a valid username and password registered with Total Jobs.

chunks.t: Integrating Totaljobs with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: How to integrate Recruit CRM with TotalJobs 1. Go to Admin Settings > External Job Boards 2. Locate Total Jobs in the list of external job boards and click Connect . In the connection window, enter the username and password you have registered with Total Jobs. 3. Click Save to complete and activate the integration between Recruit CRM and Total Jobs. Conditions for a job to be posted on job boards While creating the job or while editing it, please populate all the required fields. If all the required fields are not populated, the job won't be posted to any job board.

chunks.t: Integrating Totaljobs with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 1. You have to make sure you have selected the "Post on Job Boards" box inside Job Fields in Admin settings . This will post your open jobs not only to the free job boards but also to other external job boards (such as Total Jobs) too. If you turn ON this setting in Recruit CRM, it will automatically post all your open jobs on our partner job boards for free :) ( You can see all the job boards here ) 2. While creating a new job or editing an old one that you want to post on Total Jobs, you need to fill in all the fields that are required to post jobs on the job boards. The required fields and specifications are: - There should be a Job description for the Job

chunks.t: Integrating Totaljobs with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: - The City, State, and Country fields must be filled in. - Enable job application box should be checked - Notes for candidates should be filled in Once you fill in all the necessary details and hit "Save Job", the job will automatically be posted to Total Jobs. Problem: Jobs are not appearing on Total Jobs after integration. Likely cause: One or more posting requirements for external job boards in Recruit CRM are not satisfied. ​ What to check: Confirm that the job is open in Recruit CRM. Check that the job meets all external job board requirements mentioned in Recruit CRM.

chunks.t: Integrating Totaljobs with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Verify that the Total Jobs integration shows as connected in the External Job Boards section. ​ Resolution: Update the job so it satisfies all external job board requirements, then allow time for the posting to process. If the issue persists, verify your Total Jobs username and password in the integration settings and re-save the connection. Problem: Error when saving Total Jobs credentials. Likely cause: Incorrect Total Jobs username or password. ​ What to check: Try logging directly into your Total Jobs account with the same credentials.

chunks.t: Integrating Totaljobs with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Check for typos, extra spaces, or outdated login details. ​ Resolution: Correct your credentials in Total Jobs if needed, then re-enter the same working username and password in the Recruit CRM integration and click Save . What do I need from Total Jobs to connect it with Recruit CRM? You need the username and password that you have registered with Total Jobs. Are all jobs in Recruit CRM posted to Total Jobs automatically? Jobs are only posted to external job boards such as Total Jobs if the requirements specified in Recruit CRM for external job board posting are satisfied.

chunks.t: Integrating Totaljobs with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Integrating Total Jobs with Recruit CRM lets you quickly publish open jobs from one central system while relying on Recruit CRM’s external job board rules to control what gets posted. chunks.t: Custom Roles - Access Control & Permissions In Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What does this feature do & when to use it? Custom roles in Recruit CRM let you define exactly what actions users in a role can take and what data they can see. You can configure permissions separately for each module, including whether users can view, create, edit, delete, change ownership, or manage files. These roles can be edited or updated at any time to adjust the level of access or control you want to provide. Eg. For a team manager, you can create a custom role to grant them access to generate specific reports to analyze the performance of their team.

chunks.t: Custom Roles - Access Control & Permissions In Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You can also create and manage Teams within Recruit CRM and create custom roles for each team based on their responsibilities or job functions. Click here to learn how to create Teams in Recruit CRM You want to restrict what different users can view, create, edit, or delete in Recruit CRM. You need team managers to access specific reports without giving them full admin rights. This feature is available only on the Business and Enterprise plans. By default, only the Account Owner can create custom roles. Which modules each role needs access to (for example: Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Jobs, Deals, Placements, Invoices, Email Templates).

chunks.t: Custom Roles - Access Control & Permissions In Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Whether users in a role should access all records, only team records, only their own records, or none for each module. Which users need access to specific admin settings or bulk actions (like export to CSV). To create a new custom role, go to Admin Settings > Users and switch to the Roles & Permissions tab from the tab options at the top. Click on the +New Role button in the top right corner to create a new custom role. ​ Type the name of the role in the role name field and then configure permissions as per your requirements. ​ For each module (such as Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Jobs, Deals, Placements, Invoices, Email Templates), select the appropriate permissions to allow users to:

chunks.t: Custom Roles - Access Control & Permissions In Recruit CRM
chunks.x: For each module, choose one of the four access levels: Everything : The user can view, edit, and delete all records in that module across the database. Team only : The user can view, edit, and delete only those records that belong to their team or themselves. Owned only : The user can view, edit, and delete only the records they personally own. Nothing : The user cannot view, edit, or delete any records in that module. ​

chunks.t: Custom Roles - Access Control & Permissions In Recruit CRM
chunks.x: These permissions will also impact the user's ability to see, create, edit and delete Notes, Call Logs, Tasks and Meetings inside each entity. ​ E.g. If a user has permission to edit only candidates they own, they won't be able to edit the notes inside a candidate that belongs to someone else, even if the note was added by the user themselves. ❌ If a record from a specific entity (candidates, companies, etc.) doesn't have an owner, the user will not be able to edit or delete the Notes, Call Logs, Tasks or Meetings. In the Report Visibility section, turn the toggles on or off to control which reports the role can see. ​ For the Team Performance report, choose whether users in this role see:

chunks.t: Custom Roles - Access Control & Permissions In Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Configure bulk actions and admin permissions In the Permissions area, set controls for bulk actions such as export to CSV : Only users with the permission to export to CSV will be able to export data from your database. ​ Choose whether users in this role have access to Admin Settings : No access at all to the admin settings; or Access to specific modules in the admin panel, such as data customization for an administrator-type role, while restricting other modules. After assigning all required permissions, click the Save Role button at the bottom of the page to save your new custom role. On the Roles and Permissions page, locate the role you want to copy. ​

chunks.t: Custom Roles - Access Control & Permissions In Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Click on the three dots next to that existing role to open the role options menu. ​ Use the clone option in this menu to duplicate the existing role and then adjust permissions as needed. ​ Problem: A user on the custom role cannot edit notes, call logs, tasks, or meetings on certain records. Likely cause: Their module access is set to Owned only or Team only , and they do not own the record (or the record has no owner). ​ What to check: The user’s role settings for the relevant module (for example, Candidates or Companies). Whether the record has an owner and whether that owner matches the user or their team. ​ Resolution:

chunks.t: Custom Roles - Access Control & Permissions In Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Adjust the user’s role permissions to a broader access level if appropriate (for example, from Owned only to Team only or Everything ). Assign a correct owner to records that currently have no owner. Problem: A user cannot see or access a particular module (for example, Deals or Invoices). Likely cause: The role for that user has the module set to Nothing or only limited permissions. ​ What to check: The role’s permissions for that specific module, including view rights. ​ Resolution: Update the role to grant at least view access for that module if the user needs it. Problem: A user is unable to export data to CSV.

chunks.t: Custom Roles - Access Control & Permissions In Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Likely cause: The user’s role does not include permission to export to CSV. ​ What to check: The bulk action and export-related settings in the role’s Permissions area. ​ Resolution: Enable the export to CSV permission for that role if exporting is required for their work. ​ Problem: A user cannot access admin settings. Likely cause: The role is configured with no access to admin settings. ​ What to check: The Permissions section for admin access within the role. ​ Resolution: Grant access to the specific admin modules that the user needs (for example, data customization), while keeping other modules restricted. Q1: Who can create custom roles in Recruit CRM?

chunks.t: Custom Roles - Access Control & Permissions In Recruit CRM
chunks.x: By default, only the account owner can create custom roles. Q2: Can I edit a custom role after creating it? Yes. You can edit or update custom roles at any time to adjust the level of access or control you want to provide. Only custom roles can be customized. Default roles cannot be modified in the same way. Custom roles, access control, and permissions in Recruit CRM give you precise control over what each user can see and do, helping you align access with responsibilities and protect your data.
