chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Deals by Revenue report provides a comprehensive view of your deals and the revenue they generate across different deal stages and time periods. It helps you monitor revenue performance, compare results across teammates or teams, identify revenue trends over time, and gain deeper insights into your deal pipeline through interactive charts and detailed reports. • You want to track the total revenue generated across selected deal stages. • You need to compare deal revenue performance between teammates or teams. • You want to analyze revenue trends by week, month, or year .

chunks.t: Deals by Revenue Report
chunks.x: • You need to export revenue reports or charts for further analysis or presentations. • You want to schedule revenue reports to be automatically generated and shared with selected teammates. The report summarizes deal revenue by team member or team , displays revenue trends over your selected time period, and provides both visual charts and detailed deal records. You can drill down into the underlying deals, apply additional filters, customize the displayed columns, export report data in multiple formats, or schedule reports for automatic delivery to keep your team informed. Generate and Analyze the Deals by Revenue Report Navigate to the Reports section from the left-hand navigation menu.

chunks.t: Deals by Revenue Report
chunks.x: Open the Deals Report , then select Deals by Revenue . ​ Choose the deal stages you want to include in the report. ​ Choose the time period for the report. You can select one of the predefined ranges, such as Today, Yesterday, This Week, Last Week, This Month, or Last Quarter , or specify a Custom Date Range by selecting the required start and end dates. ​ After selecting the deal stages and date range, click Generate Report to create the report. After the report is generated, you can further customize how the data is displayed. Use the Show By option to group the report by: You can also choose whether the report should be based on the deal's:

chunks.t: Deals by Revenue Report
chunks.x: • Added On date – The date the deal was created in Recruit CRM. • Close Date – The date the deal was marked as closed. ​ The generated report provides a breakdown of deal revenue for the selected stages, grouped by team members and teams , along with the total deal amount for each time period. ​ The data is organized based on the selected Show By interval (Week, Month, or Year), making it easier to analyze revenue trends over time. • A bar chart displaying historical deal data, showing every stage that deals moved through during the selected time period. • A comprehensive table showing stage-wise performance for each team and teammate included in the report.

chunks.t: Deals by Revenue Report
chunks.x: Each bar in the chart is clickable, click any bar to view the detailed list of deals associated with that stage and time period. ​ • Sort the data by clicking any column header. • Customize the displayed information using Edit Columns . • Apply additional filters to narrow down the results. • Perform a Boolean Search to quickly locate specific deals. • Export the filtered deal list as a CSV file. You can export the report in multiple ways: • Click Export Report to CSV above the table to download the summary table as a CSV file. • Click the Export icon in the top-right corner of the bar chart to download the chart as an image in PNG, JPG, or SVG format.

chunks.t: Deals by Revenue Report
chunks.x: • Click any bar in the chart to open the detailed candidate list for that KPI, then click Export Report to CSV to download the detailed report as a CSV file. ​ You can schedule the Deals by Revenue report to be generated automatically and delivered to selected teammates at your preferred intervals. To learn how to configure scheduled reports, click here Please note that the bar graph will display historical data, showing all the stages the deals have been in that particular time frame. Problem: The Deals by Revenue report is empty or shows fewer deals than expected.

chunks.t: Deals by Revenue Report
chunks.x: Likely cause: Deal stages or timeframes are too narrowly selected, or date filters (added on vs. closed date) do not match your expectations. ​ What to check: Confirm that the correct deal stages are selected before generating the report. Verify the timeframe covers the dates when the deals were added or closed. Check whether the filter is set to added on date or closed date and whether this aligns with what you want to measure. Resolution: Adjust the selected stages, timeframe, and date reference, then click Generate Report again. Problem: You cannot see all the columns or stages you need in the detailed list view.

chunks.t: Deals by Revenue Report
chunks.x: Likely cause: The default column layout does not include all desired fields or stages. ​ What to check: Open the column editing option in the detailed list view. Check which columns are currently selected and their order. Resolution: Edit the columns to add the needed deal stages and reorder them so key information appears where you expect. Q1: What is the difference between the Deals by Revenue and Deals by Teammates reports?

chunks.t: Deals by Revenue Report
chunks.x: The Deals by Revenue report focuses on deal amounts and accumulated revenue across stages and timeframes, while the Deals by Teammates report focuses on performance grouped primarily by teammate. In the Deals by Revenue report, you still see breakdowns by teams or teammates, but the core metric is revenue. Q2: Can I change how the Deals by Revenue report groups data over time? Yes. You can use the “Show by” options to group and display data by week, month, or year. The report will then store and present data according to the interval you select. Q3: What is the difference between filtering by added on date and closed date?

chunks.t: Deals by Revenue Report
chunks.x: Filtering by added on date uses the date the deal was added to the system, helping you analyze new pipeline creation. Filtering by closed date uses the date the deal was closed in the application, helping you analyze revenue conversion in a specific period. Q4: Can I drill down into the deals behind a specific bar in the chart? Yes. All bars in the Deals by Revenue report are clickable and open a detailed list view of the deals represented in that bar. From there, you can search, filter, adjust columns, and export the data. Q5: In which formats can I export the Deals by Revenue report?

chunks.t: Deals by Revenue Report
chunks.x: You can export the bar chart as PNG, JPG, or SVG image files. The detailed list of deals can be exported as a CSV file for further analysis. The Deals by Revenue report gives you a clear, flexible view of your deal amounts and revenue across stages and timeframes, with options to drill down, export, and schedule insights for your team. Use the filters, visualizations, and exports described here to keep your pipeline performance transparent and your revenue tracking accurate.

chunks.t: Scheduling Reports
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Schedule Report feature lets you automate the delivery of your saved reports to yourself and your teammates via email. Instead of manually generating and sharing reports, you can schedule them to be sent automatically at your preferred frequency, ensuring everyone receives the latest insights without any additional effort. • You want reports to be emailed to you or your teammates automatically. • You need reports delivered on a regular schedule, such as daily , weekly , or monthly . • You want to share report insights with individual teammates or entire teams without manually exporting and sending them.

chunks.t: Scheduling Reports
chunks.x: • You need to manage multiple scheduled deliveries for the same saved report. When creating a schedule, you can choose the report frequency, start and end dates, recipients, and the export format ( CSV or XLS ). Once configured, Recruit CRM automatically generates and emails the report according to your schedule, helping you stay informed while saving time on repetitive reporting tasks. Navigate to the Reports section and open the report you want to schedule. Configure the report using the required filters and click Generate Report . ​ Learn how to generate reports in Recruit CRM After the report is generated, click Schedule Report . ​ Set up how and when you want the report to be delivered.

chunks.t: Scheduling Reports
chunks.x: • Frequency – Choose how often the report should be sent ( Daily , Weekly , or Monthly ). • Schedule Name – Enter a name to help you identify the scheduled report later. • Start Date & Time – Select when the schedule should begin. • End Condition – Choose one of the following options: End after a specified number of occurrences. Continue indefinitely without an end date. Select the users who should receive the scheduled report via their registered email addresses. Enter the details for the email that will accompany the report. • File Format – Choose whether the report should be attached as a CSV or XLS file. ​ After reviewing your settings, click Save Schedule to create the scheduled report.

chunks.t: Scheduling Reports
chunks.x: You can view and manage all scheduled reports from the Saved and Scheduled Reports tab. ​ • View all your saved and scheduled reports. • Click the green Schedule label to view the schedule details and delivery history once reports have started sending. • Turn an existing schedule On or Off using the schedule toggle. • Create an additional schedule by clicking Add New Schedule . A saved report can have multiple schedules, allowing you to send the same report at different times or to different recipients. 1. Open the Saved and Scheduled Reports tab. 2. Locate the saved report and click the Calendar icon in the Actions column. 3. Click the ellipsis (⋯) menu and select Edit Schedule .

chunks.t: Scheduling Reports
chunks.x: 5. Configure the schedule by selecting the frequency, start and end conditions, recipients, email details, and preferred file format. 6. Click Save Schedule to add the new schedule. 📌 Please note: A user can generate and save multiple reports but can only add two schedules to each of the saved reports. ​ Problem: Recipients are not receiving scheduled reports by email Likely cause : The intended users were not added as recipients. Review the schedule configuration and confirm the correct users and/or teams are selected as recipients. Confirm that the users have active, registered email addresses in Recruit CRM.

chunks.t: Scheduling Reports
chunks.x: Resolution : Update the schedule to include the correct users or teams and ensure their email details are accurate. Problem: Scheduled report stops sending earlier than expected Likely cause: The schedule was configured with an end date or a limited number of repetitions. Open the schedule settings and review the ending options (specific date, repetitions, or run indefinitely). Resolution: Adjust the ending option to extend the schedule or set it to run indefinitely if you want ongoing delivery. Problem: The report arrives, but the format is not what the recipient expects Likely cause: The wrong file type (CSV or XLS) was selected when creating the schedule.

chunks.t: Scheduling Reports
chunks.x: Review the schedule configuration and verify which file format is selected. Resolution : Edit the schedule and change the report file type to the preferred format (CSV or XLS), then save the updated schedule. Q1: Can I schedule any report from the Reports section? You can schedule the delivery of reports that you can generate and save from the Reports section, using the Schedule Report button available after the report is generated. Q2: How many schedules can I add to a single saved report? A user can generate and save multiple reports, but can only add two schedules to each of the saved reports. Q3: What file formats are available for scheduled reports?

chunks.t: Scheduling Reports
chunks.x: You can choose between CSV and XLS as the file type for scheduled reports. Scheduled reports are sent by email to the users and teams you select as recipients in the schedule configuration, using their registered email addresses in Recruit CRM. Q5: Where can I see and manage all my scheduled reports? You can keep track of all your scheduled reports under the Saved and Scheduled Reports tab, where you can monitor schedules, view history, add new schedules, and turn existing schedules on or off.

chunks.t: Scheduling Reports
chunks.x: Automating report delivery with the Schedule Report feature in Recruit CRM helps you and your teammates stay informed without manual effort. Configure your schedules, recipients, and formats once, and the system will keep your reports flowing reliably to the right inboxes. Scheduling Reports for Your Dashboard in Advanced Analytics

chunks.t: Invite your Clients to the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Hiring Manager Portal (HMP) allows your clients to securely access the jobs, candidate pipelines, and timesheets you've shared with them. You can invite clients directly from Recruit CRM or from within the Hiring Manager Portal itself. Invite a single client to the Hiring Manager Portal. Invite multiple contacts from the same company at once. Send invitations directly from the Hiring Manager Portal. Share recruitment updates securely with your clients. Please note: There are no email domain restrictions when inviting clients. Invitations can be sent to any valid email address, including personal email providers such as Gmail or Rediffmail.

chunks.t: Invite your Clients to the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: Invite clients to the Hiring Manager Portal Recruit CRM offers three different ways to invite clients to the Hiring Manager Portal. 1. Invite a client from the Contact Details page Use this method when you want to invite a single contact. Click the three-dot menu and select Enable Portal . Confirm the action when prompted. An invitation email will be sent to the contact. Before sending the invitation, Recruit CRM validates the contact's email address. If no email address is available, you'll be prompted to add one before continuing.

chunks.t: Invite your Clients to the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: If the email address is already associated with an existing Hiring Manager Portal account (either within your Recruit CRM account or another agency's account), the invitation cannot be sent. Once the invitation is sent, an Invite Sent tag appears on the contact. After the client completes the signup process, the tag automatically changes to Client Portal Enabled . You can hover over the tag to see who sent the invitation and when.

chunks.t: Invite your Clients to the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: Please Note: When enabling portal access for the first time, if the contact is associated with multiple companies, you'll be prompted to choose the company for which you'd like to enable portal access. The client will then be linked to that company's Hiring Manager Portal. 2. Invite multiple clients from the Company Details page Use this method when you want to invite several contacts from the same company. Click the three-dot me nu and select Enable Portal . A dropdown will appear listing the contacts in that company who can still be invited. Select the contacts you want to invite.

chunks.t: Invite your Clients to the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: Only contacts who have not yet been invited or have not yet activated their portal account are available for selection. Contacts who already have an invitation pending, an active portal account, or belong to a subsidiary or group company won't appear in the list. If every eligible contact already has portal access, the Enable Portal option will be disabled, along with a tooltip explaining why. Review any validation messages and make the required corrections before sending the invitations. Each selected contact will receive a separate email at their respective email address. 3. Invite clients from the Hiring Manager Portal

chunks.t: Invite your Clients to the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: Sign in to the Hiring Manager Portal and click the Hiring Managers icon from the left navigation menu. Click Invite Hiring Manager and enter the client's email address, and click Send Invite . Pro Tip: Use Add Another Email to invite multiple users at the same time. The client will receive an invitation email containing a signup link. After clicking the link, the client can complete the signup process using the same email address that received the invitation. Share jobs with your Hiring Managers through the HMP so they can review candidates and collaborate with your team. Learn How to Share Jobs with Your Hiring Manager

chunks.t: Invite your Clients to the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: Click on the three-dot menu or on the "client Portal Enabled" tag and select the option to disable the portal. A warning modal will appear. Once confirmed, an email is sent to the client, the portal tag is updated across all records associated with that email, and the contact can no longer log in. Please note: If you enable portal access again later, a new invitation email will automatically be sent to the client. Problem: The Enable Portal option is disabled for a company. Likely Cause: All eligible contacts within the company already have invitations pending or active portal accounts. What to Check: Review the contacts associated with the company.

chunks.t: Invite your Clients to the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: Resolution: No further invitations are required unless you add a new eligible contact. 1. How many times can I send an invite to the same contact? You can send the invite up to 3 times a day from the Contact Details page. If you change the contact's email, the limit resets and the 'Invite Sent' tag is removed. 2. Another agency has the same contact. What happens? Whichever agency successfully sends the invite first, owns the portal relationship for that email. If you try to invite a contact whose email already has a portal account on another agency, you will see a message that a portal account already exists, and the invite will not be sent.

chunks.t: Invite your Clients to the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: 3. Two of my contact records have the same email. Will both update? Yes. When the client signs up, all contact records with that email address are linked to the same portal account and will show the 'Client Portal Enabled' tag. 4. I changed a contact's email after the invite was sent but before they signed up. What happens? The client can still sign up using the original invite link, but because the email on the record no longer matches, the 'Client Portal Enabled' tag will not appear on the updated record, and timesheets for that contact will no longer be visible. The sender's name and timestamp are visible to your team on hover.

chunks.t: Basic elements of Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: New to automation? Let's take this one step at a time. Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM connects to apps to build recipes, with each connection reusable across multiple recipes. Think of a connection like a key that allows it to unlock and communicate with another tool or app (like Recruit CRM, Outlook, Slack, etc). It's a way for Workflow Automation to securely access and retrieve information from the connected tool.

chunks.t: Basic elements of Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Now, imagine a recipe as a set of instructions or a cooking recipe. It's a series of steps that guides the workflow on what to do with the information it gets from Recruit CRM (or any other connected tool). Recipes allow you to create automated workflows, like moving data from one tool to another without manual effort. So, in simple terms, a connection is like the key to open the door to another tool, and a recipe is the set of instructions for what to do once that door is open! Triggers serve as events or conditions that kickstart the execution of a workflow. They determine when the automation begins by responding to changes or activities within connected applications.

chunks.t: Basic elements of Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Trigger events are activated within specific apps (like Recruit CRM, Gmail, etc.) upon the occurrence of certain events, such as the addition or update of a candidate or the receipt of an email. Additionally, triggers can be initiated by actions like adding a new line to a file, scheduled occurrences, or firing at predetermined times or intervals. Actions represent the specific steps or tasks performed in response to a trigger. These are the operations that interact with connected applications and manipulate data. Actions encapsulate the specific functionalities and operations required to achieve the desired outcome of the workflow.

chunks.t: Basic elements of Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: For example, in the context of a recruitment workflow, an Action could involve creating a Deal when triggered by the creation of a Job in Recruit CRM. The Action step defines the details of this creation process, specifying the fields to be filled, data mappings, and any other relevant parameters. Assets within Workflow Automation are a comprehensive list encompassing all the Connections and Recipes associated with your account. These pivotal elements form the foundation of your workflow structure, providing the necessary components to drive automation.

chunks.t: Basic elements of Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: When you navigate to the Assets tab, you'll find a comprehensive overview of every recipe and connection that you and your team have created. This organized hub allows you to efficiently manage and access all the automation components. Whether you are working on intricate workflows or establishing connections with external applications, the Assets tab provides a consolidated space for overseeing and editing all the essential elements of your automation ecosystem.

chunks.t: Basic elements of Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: A project serves as a repository for your integration assets. Within a project, you can organize and store a cohesive set of assets related to your integrations, encompassing recipes, connections, and sub-folders. Projects help users maintain a logical and organized workflow within their work environment. Organize the projects in your workspace by department, use case, or project. For example:

chunks.t: Basic elements of Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Jobs represent the instances or executions of your workflows or recipes. When you trigger a recipe, whether manually or through an automated event, a job is initiated to execute that particular recipe. Jobs serve as tangible records of the workflow execution, capturing details such as start time, end time, and any associated outcomes. Every time a recipe runs, it generates a job that can be tracked and reviewed in the Jobs tab. This allows users to monitor the status, details, and results of each workflow execution. Whether a job is completed successfully or encounters errors, the Jobs section provides valuable insights into the performance and outcomes of your automation processes.

chunks.t: Basic elements of Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: A task represents a singular unit of work carried out whenever a recipe undertakes an action demanding computing resources. Each time a recipe utilizes an action offered by a connector, it registers as one task. A job within a recipe may encompass numerous tasks, with the total tasks executed in a job being contingent on the data associated with the trigger event and the logic embedded in the recipe. Task counting: The following table shows a breakdown of how tasks are counted with the different recipe steps: Search/Create/Update/Get/Upsert/Lookup etc. The Task is incremented by 1 for each of these Actions The Task is incremented by 1 for every Action in the loop

chunks.t: Basic elements of Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Control statement (If, Error monitor, stop) Note: All users, regardless of their plan, receive 50 free tasks per month to test and explore automation features. The free tasks are account-specific and not user-specific. Workflow Automation is an Enterprise plan feature which can also be added at an additional cost to Pro or Business plan subscriptions. chunks.t: Converting CSV files to Excel
chunks.x: We understand that sometimes our clients require their Recruit CRM data in Excel format rather than CSV. In this article, we will guide you through the straightforward steps to seamlessly convert CSV files into Excel, ensuring a smooth transition for enhanced data management and analysis. Converting CSV and XLS files online 🧞‍♂️ Option 1: CSV to Excel using the “From Text/ Data” Option 1. Open Microsoft Excel, and start a Blank workbook.

chunks.t: Converting CSV files to Excel
chunks.x: 2. Once the new spreadsheet is open, select Data from the ribbon, and then click on the From Text/ CSV button on the upper-left-hand side of the window. An Import Data pop-up box will appear. From there, select the CSV file you want to import and click on Import: 3. A new tab will appear, asking you to define certain parameters within the imported data, like File Origin , Delimiter , and Data Type Detection . Under delimiter select the delimiter used in your CSV file; It is best to choose comma by default. Once everything’s set, click on Load: 4. Once you click on Load, excel will load your data from the CSV file into a formatted table:

chunks.t: Converting CSV files to Excel
chunks.x: 5. After this you can save your file by clicking the File and then Save As and Excel will save your file as an xls or Excel file: Option 2: CSV to Excel using the “Text to Column” Option 1. Open Microsoft Excel, and start a Blank workbook. 2. Click on File , go to the "Open" tab of the left bar, and choose Browse from the Open side-pane to display all the files from your device. Choose the CSV file you want to convert and click on Open:

chunks.t: Converting CSV files to Excel
chunks.x: Once Excel has opened your CSV file, you’ll notice that your data is separated into the appropriate rows. However, it’s not separated into the appropriate columns. Instead, the data is saved in the first column of each row. Luckily, you can automatically sort the data by using the Text to Column option. 3. Go to the Data tab in the ribbon. Select the rows of data that you want to convert, and click on the Convert to Text option located in the Data Tools field. This will open a Convert Text to Column Wizard that will guide you through the process.

chunks.t: Converting CSV files to Excel
chunks.x: 4. Under the Original data type , choose Delimited , and click Next . In the next section, check the box next to the type of delimiter your CSV file uses (our example uses a comma). The Data Preview field will allow you to see the data being assigned to corresponding columns. Click Next , choose the spreadsheet destination, and click Finish . Your data is now separated into the corresponding columns: 5. Click on the File tab and select the Save option. When the Save dialog box appears, give your file a name, and choose Excel Workbook in the Save as type drop-down menu: Option 3: CSV to Excel using Google Sheets option

chunks.t: Converting CSV files to Excel
chunks.x: 1. Log into Google Sheets using your Google credentials. If you don’t own a Google account, you might have to create one. After you’ve logged in, select the Blank option to create a new spreadsheet. Once the new spreadsheet is open, click on the File menu in the upper right corner of the page, and select Import :

chunks.t: Converting CSV files to Excel
chunks.x: 2. This will open up an Import file dialog box. Click on the Upload tab, and either drag and drop your file or click on the Select a file from your device button to locate the file and upload it. Google Sheets will ask you about the import location and separator (delimiter type) it should use to derive data. You can leave the delimiter selection drop-down at Detect Automatically and click on Import data : 3. Google Sheets will automatically separate the data into its appropriate cells. Now you can save the file. 4. Once you’ve made the necessary changes, if any, go to File , and choose Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) from the Download drop-down menu:

chunks.t: Converting CSV files to Excel
chunks.x: Importing CSV files in Excel to convert them into XLS files in Mac is pretty similar to the options we have for Windows. 1. Once you have downloaded the CSV into your device, you need to open a blank Excel spreadsheet. Select File > Import : Delimiters: Comma (no other options should be checked). In the Data Preview window, select all columns. If you select all of the columns, you'll see a label above each column in the preview that says Text : 5. Excel will ask you where you want to put the data. choose Existing sheet and select OK . That's it 😄 You have successfully converted your CSV file into an Excel sheet! chunks.t: Connecting Recruit CRM & other apps with Workflow Automation
chunks.x: Connect your Recruit CRM account with Workflow Automation You can connect your Recruit CRM account in two ways: through the connection wizard or in the recipe editor. A. Connecting through the connection wizard The same process can be followed to connect 3rd party apps with Workflow Automation. Head over to Workflow Automation & Integration from your Admin Settings . Go to the Workflows module and click on Create >> Connection. Search Recruit CRM on the search bar and select the app. Enter the Connection Name, Location, and API Token to set up your Recruit CRM connection. Once connected you can use this connection to create your Recipes. ​ B. Connecting through the recipe editor

chunks.t: Connecting Recruit CRM & other apps with Workflow Automation
chunks.x: Head over to Workflow Automation & Integration from your Admin Settings . Give your recipe a name, and the location (folder) where you want it to be saved, and pick your starting point as “Trigger from an app” to start building the recipe. Search for Recruit CRM in the app directory and select it as the trigger app for your recipe. Choose the trigger and connect your account by entering the API token. Once connected, you’ll be able to use the same connection every time you create a recipe. Click here to find your Recruit CRM API Key

chunks.t: Connecting Recruit CRM & other apps with Workflow Automation
chunks.x: Specify the trigger event that will initiate the workflow. For example, in Recruit CRM, you can choose to trigger the recipe when a new candidate is added, a job is updated, or any other supported trigger event. Once your trigger is set up, you can add various actions that should follow the trigger event. These actions can include updating candidate records, sending notifications, or creating tasks within Recruit CRM or other apps. ​ Connect third-party apps with Workflow Automation The below steps will help you connect your third-party applications such as Outlook, Gmail, Google Sheets, or any other apps. 1. chunks.t: Signing up on the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Hiring Manager Portal (HMP) provides Hiring Managers with secure access to the jobs, candidate pipelines, and timesheets shared with them by their recruiting agency. Hiring Managers can be invited either by the agency through Recruit CRM or by another Hiring Manager from within the portal. Invite Hiring Managers to the Hiring Manager Portal. Complete the Hiring Manager signup process. Access shared jobs and candidate pipelines. View and approve timesheets shared by your recruiter. Please note: Hiring Managers can be invited using any valid email address . There are no email domain restrictions.

chunks.t: Signing up on the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: Sign in to the Hiring Manager Portal and click the Hiring Managers icon from the left navigation menu. Click Invite Hiring Manager and enter the client's email address, and click Send Invite. Pro Tip: Use Add Another Email to invite multiple users at the same time. The client will receive an invitation email containing a signup link. After clicking the link, the client can complete the signup process using the same email address that received the invitation. Your email address and company will already be populated and cannot be changed during signup. Your account is created immediately, and no additional email verification is required.

chunks.t: Signing up on the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: After signing in, you can update your own profile information at any time. Click your Profile from the upper-right corner. Update your details and save the changes. You can also choose how time is displayed in the Client Portal. Under Time Format , select either the 12-hour or 24-hour format and click Save Profile. All timesheets will be displayed using the selected time format. If you change your email address to one that matches an existing Contact in Recruit CRM, the Client Portal Enabled tag will automatically appear on that contact record. Any jobs, candidates, or timesheets previously shared with your old email address will no longer be available.

chunks.t: Signing up on the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: You can only edit your own profile. Each Hiring Manager is responsible for managing their own account. After signing in, you'll land on the Timesheets tab by default. Timesheets will appear only when all of the following conditions are met: Your portal email matches a Contact record in Recruit CRM. That Contact is associated with the relevant Contract or Contract-to-Permanent job. The Online Candidate list Link for that job has been enabled. When all three conditions are met, timesheets become available automatically. If the Online Link is later disabled, the timesheets are removed immediately. Open the Online Candidate List link shared with you and click ' View in Portal '.

chunks.t: Signing up on the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: From there, open the Jobs tab on the portal. Your shared jobs will now be visible. Problem: I can't see any timesheets after signing up. Likely Cause: Your portal account hasn't been linked to the appropriate contact record, or the Online Link for the job hasn't been enabled. What to Check: Verify that your portal email matches the contact record associated with the relevant job and that the Online Link has been enabled. Resolution: Please contact your recruiting partner to ensure your email is linked to the correct contact record and that the Online Link is enabled. Once both requirements are met, your timesheets will automatically appear in the portal.

chunks.t: Signing up on the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: 1. Do I need a company email address to sign up? No. The email domain restriction has been removed. You can sign up with any valid email address, even with Google.com , rediffmail.com , etc. 2. Can I change my email or company name while signing up? No. These two fields are pre-filled based on the invite and are locked during sign-up. You can update your other details freely. 3. I clicked 'View in Portal,' but I do not see jobs. Where are my jobs? When you click 'View in Portal' from the Online Candidate List link, you might on the Timesheets tab first. To see the jobs shared with you, go to the Jobs tab on the portal. The shared jobs will then be visible.

chunks.t: Signing up on the Hiring Manager Portal
chunks.x: 4. I was invited but haven't signed up yet, and I clicked 'View in Portal'. What happens? You will be taken to the Sign In page rather than the Sign Up page. New accounts can only be created through an invite, so ask your Agency Recruiter or existing Hiring Manager on the Portal- to Invite you as well. 5. Will I have to verify my email after signing up? No. Email verification has been removed. Your account is active as soon as you complete the sign-up form.

chunks.t: Deleting emails from Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What does this feature do & when to use it? Recruit CRM has partnered with Nylas.com to power our email services. Recruit CRM displays the same emails that exist in your email provider’s mailbox, across all folders (Inbox, Sent, Trash/Bin, Junk, etc.). When an email is permanently deleted from your native mailbox, it is also removed from Recruit CRM and will no longer appear there. Your email account must be connected to Recruit CRM. You must have access to your native mailbox (for example, Gmail, Outlook, or another email provider). You need permission in your email provider to delete and permanently remove emails from all folders, including Trash, Bin, or Junk.

chunks.t: Deleting emails from Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 📧 How to delete emails from Recruit CRM? Open your native mailbox (for example, Gmail or Outlook) where the email account connected to Recruit CRM is hosted. ​ Locate the email you want to remove from Recruit CRM in your Inbox, Sent, or any other folder. ​ Delete the email from that folder using your email provider’s standard delete option. ​ Go to your email provider’s Trash, Bin, or Junk folder (the folder name depends on your email service). ​ Find the same email in Trash/Bin/Junk and delete it again so it is permanently removed from your mailbox. ​

chunks.t: Deleting emails from Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Wait for the sync between your mailbox and Recruit CRM to complete; once the email is permanently deleted from your native mailbox, it will no longer be visible in Recruit CRM. ​ As Recruit CRM mirrors your entire mailbox, the " All Emails " tab comprises the emails present in all the different folders in your native mailbox, including the bin. Thus, to ensure the emails do not show up in Recruit CRM, you have to delete them permanently. ​ Problem: An email still appears in Recruit CRM after I deleted it from my inbox. Likely cause: The email is still present in your Trash, Bin, or Junk folder in your native mailbox.

chunks.t: Deleting emails from Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Open your email provider and check the Trash, Bin, and Junk folders for the same email. Permanently delete the email from these folders. Wait for the mailbox to sync with Recruit CRM and refresh the All Emails view. Can I delete emails directly from Recruit CRM? No. Because Recruit CRM mirrors your mailbox, you must delete emails directly from your native mailbox (such as Gmail or Outlook). Once deleted there (including from Trash/Bin/Junk), they will disappear from Recruit CRM. To delete emails from Recruit CRM, always remove them permanently from your native mailbox, including any Trash/Bin/Junk folders, so they no longer appear in the mirrored All Emails view.

chunks.t: How Recruit CRM's Data Migration Service Works
chunks.x: Recruit CRM's Data Migration service helps transfer your existing database from another ATS or CRM into your Recruit CRM account. The migration process includes extracting your exported data, analyzing and filtering records, mapping fields to Recruit CRM, cleaning and transforming the data where required, testing the import in a test environment, and finally uploading the verified data into your live account. Throughout the process, Recruit CRM's dedicated data migration team works to ensure an accurate, efficient, and hassle-free migration while helping you start with a clean and well-structured database. You are moving from another ATS or CRM into Recruit CRM.

chunks.t: How Recruit CRM's Data Migration Service Works
chunks.x: You want Recruit CRM's data migration team to migrate your existing database. You want to understand the migration process, timelines, and responsibilities. You want to reduce migration costs by cleaning or filtering your records before migration. ​ Step-by-step instructions on how the Data Migration is carried out Step 1: Request and share your data export: Request a complete data export from your previous ATS/CRM provider. Once you receive the exported data, share it with Recruit CRM's Data Migration team through your Customer Success Manager. After receiving the files, the Data Migration team will extract the data and upload it into their internal systems for further processing.

chunks.t: How Recruit CRM's Data Migration Service Works
chunks.x: Step 2: Count analysis and initial filtering: Once the exported data has been imported into the team's local database, an initial analysis of the data is performed. During this stage, the team verifies the total record count for: The team can also apply filters to remove outdated or unnecessary records based on criteria such as: Other filters agreed upon during the migration planning process This helps create a cleaner, more functional database by excluding records that are no longer required. ​ Example: If 5,000 candidates have not been contacted since 2021 and you only want recently updated candidate profiles, those older records can be excluded from the migration.

chunks.t: How Recruit CRM's Data Migration Service Works
chunks.x: Once the analysis is complete, the team shares the record counts with you for verification. Once the counts are confirmed to be accurate, we proceed to raise an invoice for the data migration service. If any discrepancies or special conditions are identified, the team performs another round of analysis to resolve them before moving forward. Note: Filtering the data is a good way of reducing the data migration cost since it's calculated on the total number of records in the database.

chunks.t: How Recruit CRM's Data Migration Service Works
chunks.x: The next crucial step is to analyze and extract the required data from the source and map it with the equivalent columns in Recruit CRM in a spreadsheet. This process is important to determine what columns will be imported into the system and avoid unnecessary data being mapped into Recruit CRM's database. Note: actual field mapping varies by source system and is confirmed with you during Step 3. The completed field mapping document is then shared with you for review and confirmation. Once you approve the mapping, the Data Migration team begins the data cleaning process.

chunks.t: How Recruit CRM's Data Migration Service Works
chunks.x: From this point onward, your involvement in the data migration process is complete. The Data Migration team takes care of the remaining steps until the migration is successfully completed. Step 4: Data cleaning and transformation: In data cleaning, we will transform the data according to data analysis and Recruit CRM's database structure. Step 5: Test the data in a test environment: Before importing your data into your Recruit CRM account, the cleaned CSV files are first uploaded into a test environment. The data structure matches Recruit CRM's requirements. The data imports successfully without any technical issues.

chunks.t: How Recruit CRM's Data Migration Service Works
chunks.x: Any issues identified during testing are resolved before the final migration begins. Step 6: Upload the verified data to your Recruit CRM account: Once the test import is successful, the same verified data is uploaded into your live Recruit CRM account. After the upload is complete, the data migration process is finished. Your Customer Success Manager or the Data Migration team will notify you once the migration has been successfully completed. Congratulations! Your data migration to Recruit CRM is now complete. ​ If you prefer not to use Recruit CRM's paid Data Migration service, you can import your data yourself by: Uploading spreadsheets directly into Recruit CRM.

chunks.t: How Recruit CRM's Data Migration Service Works
chunks.x: Importing candidate information using the Resume Parser. These self-service options allow you to migrate your database independently whenever needed. chunks.t: Import Mapping Template in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What does this feature do & when to use it? Import mapping templates let you save the way you map your CSV or XLS columns to Recruit CRM fields during an import. Once saved, you can apply the same template to future imports so the fields are mapped automatically. This removes the need to repeat the manual mapping process for files with the same structure. You can use this when: You frequently import CSV or XLS files with the same column structure. You want to avoid manually mapping each column to a Recruit CRM field on every import. You need consistent, repeatable field mapping across multiple imports. You want to reduce mapping mistakes during candidate data imports.

chunks.t: Import Mapping Template in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Ensure you have a CSV or XLS file ready to upload. Confirm that your file has clear column names that can be used for mapping. Be aware that if you choose the option to include the first header row of the CSV or XLS file in a way that removes column names for mapping, you will not be able to save a template. Only the creator of a mapping template can edit or delete that template. Upload your CSV or XLS file and proceed to the field mapping stage of the import. ​ Map each column in your file to the correct Recruit CRM field. ​ After completing the mapping process, click the Save Mapping button to store your current field mappings as a template. ​

chunks.t: Import Mapping Template in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Confirm the save action as prompted so that the mapping fields are stored as a template. You can also choose to share it with your teammates by enabling the Share with all teammates toggle. ​ This lets you select the same mapping each time you upload a similar file, eliminating the need to manually map fields every time. Hover your cursor over the template you want to manage. ​ When you hover, you will see options to edit or delete the template. ​ Click the pencil icon to edit the existing mapping template. ​ Click the trash icon to delete the template if you no longer need it. ​ Only the creator of a template can delete or edit that template. ​

chunks.t: Import Mapping Template in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: If there are columns in your data sheet that you do not wish to import, you can skip them by selecting Don’t import this column from the dropdown for that column. Once a field is mapped, it will no longer be available in the dropdown for mapping again. Make sure the field type in Recruit CRM matches the type of value in the column you are mapping. For example, if you are trying to map the column “Work Experience”, you need to find a field that accepts numeric values viz the Number field. If you’ve mapped it to a field that is a text field, then the values for the column Work Experience will not be imported to Recruit CRM.

chunks.t: Import Mapping Template in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: If a column in your spreadsheet does not match any existing field in Recruit CRM, you will need to create a custom field before importing so that the data can be stored correctly. Do I need to create a mapping template every time I import a file? No. You only need to create a template once for each file structure. After that, you can select the saved template on future imports with the same column layout. What happens if I change the column names in my CSV or XLS file? If column names change, the template may no longer correctly identify which columns to map, and some fields may not map as expected. Keep your column names consistent when reusing templates.

chunks.t: Add your own custom industries for companies
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM offers a feature that allows users to customize default industry fields for companies. You have the flexibility to add as many custom industries as you'd like to align with your diverse work portfolio! You can also delete custom industry options you no longer need, while keeping the built-in default options intact. You need industry options that are not available in the default Company Industry list. You work across niche or specialized markets and want the industry field to reflect them. You need to clean up or remove outdated custom industry options. Simply follow these steps to create custom industries for companies:

chunks.t: Add your own custom industries for companies
chunks.x: While creating a new company or editing an existing one in Recruit CRM, you'll have the option to fill in the company's industry field. Locate the Company Industry field, and you can choose from a default list of industries or create your own custom industry. If the industry you need is not in the default list, type the desired industry name into the search box of the Company Industry field. Click the Add button that appears to create this as a new custom industry option. Once added, you will find it from the User Added section within the Company Industry field. After selecting the custom industry, click the Submit button to save the company with that custom industry selected.

chunks.t: Add your own custom industries for companies
chunks.x: You can also add a new custom industry directly from the "Company Industry" field on the company main profile page: Go to a company record and edit the company. Click on the Company Industry drop-down field to view all available options, including any you have added. Find the custom industry option you want to remove. Click the small trash bin icon next to that custom industry option to delete it. After clicking on it, you'll receive a confirmation message indicating that you've successfully deleted the custom industry option: You can also delete the custom company industry from the company details page: Please note that the default industry options cannot be deleted.

chunks.t: Add your own custom industries for companies
chunks.x: Problem: Cannot find a newly added custom industry Likely cause: The custom industry was not saved or not selected from the User Added section. Open the Company Industry field and look under the User Added section. Confirm that you clicked the Add button after typing the new industry name. If the custom industry is not listed, type the name again and click the Add button, then select it from the User Added section and save the company. Problem: Unable to delete an industry option Likely cause: You are trying to delete a default industry option. Look for the trash bin icon next to the industry option. Default industry options do not show a trash bin icon and cannot be removed.

chunks.t: Add your own custom industries for companies
chunks.x: Only delete options that display the trash bin icon. If you do not see the icon, the option is a default industry and cannot be deleted Yes. You can add as many custom industries as you would like to align with your diverse work portfolio. Custom company industries in Recruit CRM give you the flexibility to match the Company Industry field to your real markets and internal terminology. By adding, selecting, and deleting custom options directly from the Company Industry field, you can keep your data accurate, relevant, and easy for your team to work with. chunks.t: Advertise your jobs through Recruit CRM's Job Marketplace
chunks.x: It's always a struggle to find the right job boards to post your jobs and ensure you get the right applications to fill positions quickly. Recruit CRM helps you streamline your job posting process and publish job ads in an easy and targeted way. You can have access to more than 3,000 channels to advertise and market your jobs. Job advertising is available for all accounts with a paid Recruit CRM subscription. If you’re on the free plan (in the beta phase), you won’t be able to post jobs, but you can still explore the job board marketplace. Once you upgrade to a paid plan, you’ll experience a 3-day verification period . ​ Let's see how you can do this!

chunks.t: Advertise your jobs through Recruit CRM's Job Marketplace
chunks.x: Only the account owners, admins, and users on custom roles have permission to advertise jobs. 1. Open the job you wish to sponsor and click on the blue button at the top to advertise the job. ​ 2. A pop-up will appear prompting you to fill in the basic information for the job campaign. Search for an existing job in your database Give your job advertising a name for future tracking P.S. The job function, location, and industry tag will only be used to offer you job board recommendations. Jobs that have the status : "on hold", "closed" or "canceled" cannot be advertised.

chunks.t: Advertise your jobs through Recruit CRM's Job Marketplace
chunks.x: 3. After filling in the details, you'll be redirected to a page where you can manage your existing contracts or buy job campaigns. Click on the second tab to access the Job Board Marketplace. ​ 4. Here you'll have a list with more than 3000 job board options to choose from, including LinkedIn, Monster, Facebook, SEEK and many more! SEEK is available on the Job Board Marketplace! You can now publish your jobs directly to SEEK through the Recruit CRM Marketplace. Simply navigate to the Job Board Marketplace section, select SEEK, and follow the prompts to post your job. You can also sort the options from newest to oldest and apply filters based on the location, industry and job function:

chunks.t: Advertise your jobs through Recruit CRM's Job Marketplace

After choosing the job board(s) you wish to advertise in, click on "Add to Campaign" to proceed. ​ While advertising you can select all the required job boards in your cart and proceed to post the job i.e, you can post to multiple job boards in a single campaign. You can click on "More Information" to learn more about the job board and the advertising details (cost, campaign processing time, location, duration, etc). 6. On the right side of the screen you'll be able to see your bill summary. Select "Continue to Review Details" to go ahead with the purchase. ​ You can remove the job boards selected by clicking on "Remove from Campaign".

chunks.t: Advertise your jobs through Recruit CRM's Job Marketplace

chunks.t: Deals in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? A Deal in Recruit CRM represents any opportunity your team is actively pursuing to generate revenue. This could include consulting projects, pitching candidates to clients, or facilitating candidate placements. The Deals section helps you track these opportunities from start to finish by organizing them into customizable stages, monitoring progress, forecasting revenue, and collaborating with teammates. You want to track and manage revenue opportunities such as consulting projects, candidate pitches, and placements. You need to organize opportunities into customizable deal stages to monitor progress and forecast revenue.

chunks.t: Deals in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You want to link deals with candidates, contacts, companies, and jobs for a complete view of each opportunity. You need to collaborate with teammates using deal splits and generate reports based on deal performance, revenue, and team contributions. You want to archive, restore, or clone deals as your sales pipeline evolves. The deal's currency is the same as the account's currency. Only the Account owner has the option to change the Account currency; follow along to know how this can be done - ​ 1. Go to Admin Settings . 2. Open the Account option to change the account currency, which will also change the deal currency. There are several ways by which you can add a deal in Recruit CRM:

chunks.t: Deals in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Navigate to the Deals section and click the Add Deal button. Enter the required deal details. If needed, select a Deal Type and fill in any custom deal fields relevant to your workflow. Note: The Deal Type field is an optional field, and it can also be hidden from the add form/edit form if not needed for your workflow. Additionally, if you have specific requirements, you can include custom 'Deal' fields to store additional details as needed. Click here to learn how to add custom fields for deals! Scroll to the bottom of the job form and enable the Create New Deal checkbox. Complete the remaining job details and submit the form. A new deal will be created and linked to the job automatically.

chunks.t: Deals in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Within the Candidate/Contact/Job/Company's details page Open the details page of a candidate, contact, job, or company. Navigate to the Related Deals tab to view all associated deals. Click the option to Add Deal to create and link a new deal directly from the record. Click the Global Add (+) icon at the top of Recruit CRM and select Deal . Enter the required deal details and click Submit to create the deal. Deal stages represent various phases of a deal's progression. Each stage is assigned a specific percentage value, which determines the proportion of revenue earned as the deal advances. You can customize the deal stages and create a deal pipeline as per your requirements.

chunks.t: Deals in Recruit CRM

Once you've entered the required information, confirm the update to save the new stage. Change a deal stage from the deal profile You can also update a deal stage directly from an individual deal profile.

chunks.t: Deals in Recruit CRM

chunks.t: Single Sign-On (SSO) Setup in Recruit CRM with Google, Azure, and Okta
chunks.x: What does this feature do & when to use it? Recruit CRM’s Single Sign-On (SSO) integration lets users access their Recruit CRM account using their existing login credentials from an external identity provider that supports the OpenID Connect (OIDC) protocol. Instead of managing separate Recruit CRM passwords, users authenticate once with an IDP such as Google, Microsoft Azure, or Okta. Recruit CRM then trusts that authentication and grants access to the corresponding user account. Use Single Sign-On in Recruit CRM when you want to: Centralize user authentication through an identity provider like Google, Microsoft Azure, or Okta.

chunks.t: Single Sign-On (SSO) Setup in Recruit CRM with Google, Azure, and Okta
chunks.x: Enforce consistent security policies from your IDP across Recruit CRM access. Control which users can log in to Recruit CRM via IDP group membership. SSO is available only on the Business and Enterprise plans. Only users with access to Admin Settings and Account Management can configure SSO. You must have an existing identity provider (IDP) that supports OpenID Connect (OIDC), such as Google, Microsoft Azure, or Okta. You will need to create or configure an OIDC application in your IDP and obtain the credentials required by Recruit CRM. Enabling SSO will disable multi-factor authentication (MFA/2FA) if it is currently enabled on the account.

Recruit CRM supports identity providers that use the OpenID Connect (OIDC) protocol, including Google , Microsoft Azure , and Okta . What happens to MFA/2FA when I enable SSO? When you enable SSO in Recruit CRM, any existing MFA/2FA configuration in Recruit CRM is disabled. If you require multi-factor authentication, you should enforce it at the identity provider level. Can users still log in with email and password after SSO is enabled?

chunks.t: Single Sign-On (SSO) Setup in Recruit CRM with Google, Azure, and Okta
chunks.x: Yes, but only if you enable the option to permit login using email and password . If this option is unchecked, users must log in via SSO. The account owner can always log in with email and password regardless of this setting. Single Sign-On in Recruit CRM lets you centralize authentication, simplify user logins, and control access through your existing identity provider. Once configured, you can manage who can sign in via IDP groups while keeping the account owner’s email and password access as a secure fallback. chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? AI sequence generation in Recruit CRM lets you create complete, multi-step outreach sequences for candidates or contacts without drafting each step manually. You describe your goal, target audience, desired tone, and any specific requirements in a single prompt, and the AI generates a ready-to-review sequence of up to six steps.

chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: Each sequence can include email steps, SMS steps (if applicable), task steps, and, where the LinkedIn add-on is enabled, LinkedIn steps as well. You can regenerate the full sequence or individual steps, edit any generated content, and add further steps manually before saving and enrolling records. You can use this feature when: You want to quickly create a structured outreach sequence for candidates or contacts. You need a multi-step, multi-channel workflow that includes emails, tasks, and LinkedIn actions. You want AI to draft the initial sequence steps so you can review, refine, and deploy them faster.

chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: Important Note: We use ChatGPT to power the AI sequence generation, which is still undergoing improvements. As a result, the AI-generated content may sometimes be inaccurate or misleading. Please ensure you always double-check the results for accuracy. Navigate to the Sequences page in Recruit CRM from the Admin Settings. Choose whether you are creating a sequence for Candidates or Contacts . Click Create Sequence Using AI to open the AI prompt interface. The quality of the AI-generated sequence depends directly on the quality of your prompt. A detailed, specific prompt produces a more accurate and personalized result than a short or vague one.

chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: Your prompt should include as many of the following as relevant: Goal and use case: What is this sequence trying to achieve? For example, outreach for a new job opening, follow-up after a career fair, or a product demo invitation. Target audience: Who will receive this sequence? For example, mid-level software engineers, HR managers at enterprise companies, or passive candidates in a specific industry. Desired tone: How should the messages feel? For example, professional, warm and conversational, concise and direct, or persuasive.

chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: Language: Specify the language if you need the sequence in a language other than English. If your prompt is written in Spanish, the sequence will be generated in Spanish. Specific requirements: Any particular points to include, links to mention, actions to prompt, or content to avoid. The more detail you provide, the more accurately the AI can tailor the sequence to your needs. If you prefer to speak rather than type, click the microphone icon to dictate your prompt using voice input. Always skim the transcribed text before clicking Send to catch any speech recognition errors.

chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: Example prompt: "Create a five-step outreach sequence in English for passive software engineering candidates being considered for a senior backend role at a fintech startup. Use a professional but approachable tone. Include two follow-up emails, one LinkedIn connection request, and one task to call the candidate." Click Send (arrow icon) after entering or dictating your prompt. The AI will process your input and generate the sequence. Once the AI has finished generating, a sequence of up to six steps will appear. These may include email steps, task steps, and LinkedIn steps if your account has the LinkedIn add-on enabled. Review each step carefully before proceeding.

chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: 📌 Note: Six steps is the default maximum for AI generation. If your workflow requires more than six steps, add them manually after reviewing the generated output or you can mention the required steps in the prompt itself. Step 4: Regenerate the Sequence or Individual Steps If you are not satisfied with the output, you have two regeneration options: Regenerate the full sequence: Click the global Regenerate button to discard the current output and generate a completely new sequence from your prompt. ​ Regenerate a specific step: Click the Regenerate button on an individual step card to regenerate only that step while keeping the rest of the sequence intact. ​

chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: Step 5: Edit, Extend, and Finalize the Sequence. All AI-generated steps are fully editable. Before saving, you can: Click into any generated step to edit its subject line, body text, timing, or any other field. Add new steps manually by scrolling to the bottom of the sequence and selecting a step type: Email , Task , SMS or LinkedIn (where available). Reorder steps or adjust timing between steps to match your preferred cadence.

chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: ⚠️ Important: If you have already added steps manually and then choose to use Create Sequence Using AI , a warning will appear stating that the AI-generated steps will overwrite all existing manually added steps. Proceed only if you are comfortable losing those steps. There is no automatic rollback, so consider saving a copy of the sequence before making major changes. ​ Once you have reviewed and finalized all steps, click Save to store the sequence. Enroll the relevant candidates or contacts into the sequence to begin outreach.

chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: When the LinkedIn Messages Integration add-on is enabled on your account, the AI can include LinkedIn connection requests and message steps alongside email and task steps within the same generated sequence. This enables a complete multi-channel outreach workflow from a single prompt. The LinkedIn Messages Integration add-on must be active on your account for LinkedIn steps to appear in AI-generated sequences. All AI-generated LinkedIn steps are fully editable before saving, so you can adjust messaging, timing, and connection request notes to match your strategy. Click here to learn more about Email Sequencing in Recruit CRM

chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: Click here to learn more about LinkedIn message sequencing in Recruit CRM Click here to learn more about SMS Sequencing in Recruit CRM Problem - The AI-generated content doesn’t match your desired tone or audience. Likely cause : The prompt is too short or not specific enough. ​ What to check : Review your prompt to see if it clearly states goal, audience, tone, language, and any special requirements. ​ Resolution path : Update the prompt with more detail and click Send again, or use the Regenerate buttons on the sequence or individual steps. Problem - Generated content appears misleading or factually incorrect.

chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: Likely cause : Limitations of the underlying ChatGPT model. ​ What to check : Carefully review each AI-generated step for accuracy and relevance. ​ Resolution path : Manually edit the content in each step to correct inaccuracies before saving and enrolling records. Avoid using AI-generated text without human review. Yes, users can edit and customize the AI-generated sequences before finalizing them. Yes, it supports multiple languages based on user prompts. For example, if your prompt is in Spanish, the sequence steps will be generated in Spanish. Is there a limit to the use of this feature?

chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: Yes, the AI-Assist feature has monthly token limits that vary based on your plan. Token usage includes both input and output, and may vary depending on the language and content. ​ Please note that token counts may vary based on the language and content. • Free Plan – 50K tokens • Pro Plan – 5 million tokens • Business Plan – 10 million tokens • Enterprise Plan – 20 million tokens These limits apply to the following AI features: • Generate Note Summary • Generate Call Log Summary • Generate Email Template • Generate Email • Generate Email Sequence • Email Reply Suggestion • Generate Candidate Summary • Generate Job Description

chunks.t: Generate Sequence using AI
chunks.x: Note: These token limits currently do not apply to AI Sourcing and AI Boolean Search . Can I edit AI-generated steps before enrolling candidates or contacts? Yes. All AI-generated steps (emails, tasks, SMS, LinkedIn) are fully editable. You should review and adjust each step before saving the sequence and enrolling records. Using AI to generate sequences in Recruit CRM lets you quickly build structured, multi-channel outreach for candidates and contacts while keeping full control over the final content. Provide a clear prompt, review and refine each step, and then save and enroll your records to put your new sequence into action.

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Recruit CRM’s Advanced Analytics is an embedded analytics solution designed to help users create custom reports, visualize key metrics through interactive dashboards, and easily share insights with teams and external stakeholders. Advanced Analytics is an Enterprise plan feature which can also be added at an additional cost to the Pro or Business plan subscriptions. Step-by-step instructions on how to use Advanced Analytics Once you've subscribed to the Advanced Analytics add-on for your Recruit CRM account, you can start using the feature immediately from the Reports section .

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 1. You'll find a section on the Reports page called 'Advanced Analytics.' Clicking on it will take you to the Homepage , where you can find the available collections. Select the respective collection to explore it. You will have a default dashboard in the with some pre-built charts. 2. You can also personalize the default dashboard to fit your needs. Edit it to move tables, rearrange reports across different tabs, adjust visualization options, and more!

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 3. This, as an interactive dashboard, lets you visualize all the information from various statistics tables and see exactly which records (candidates, contacts, deals, jobs, call logs) the system is referencing. Simply click on the data you want to explore for a detailed view. Creating custom reports and advanced queries✏️ Create your own custom Dashboards to organize your reports To start adding and organizing reports in the same view, you first need to create a dashboard. This will allow you to add your statistics and reports, saving them in a single, interactive view where they can be easily accessed and connected with each other.

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: To create your own new dashboard, click on the "+ New" button located at the top right of your advanced analytics screen and then click on "Dashboard" . Add a name, and a description to the new collection you create, save it anywhere in your library, and then click on "Create". This will allow you to start organizing and saving your reports in any custom dashboard you create. Having explored the default and custom dashboards in Recruit CRM, you should know that you can also create custom reports, tables, and statistics, and organize them into your own personalized dashboards.

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 1. To create custom queries and reports, click the "+ New" button, then select "Question" to create a specific report. You'll then be able to select the entity you want to generate the report from: 2. Once you've selected an entity for your report, you can choose various aspects and filters related to that entity. For instance, if you select "Candidates," you can specify which candidate fields you want to include in the generated report by clicking on the little arrow next to the title of the entity:

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 3. You can apply filters to refine your report or analysis, allowing you to obtain results that are precisely tailored to your needs. For instance, you can filter records to include only those with a current salary above a certain amount. 4. You can enhance your report by summarizing the data using various metrics, such as "Average", "Max of", "Min of" or "Sum". Additionally, you have the option to group the summarized results by any field in the records, providing a clearer and more organized view of the information.

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 5. Once you've made all the necessary customizations to your report, click on "Visualize" to generate the final, customized report. This will apply all your adjustments, allowing you to see the data exactly as you've configured it. Create your own collections to save your reports📘 In the advanced analytics feature, you can create your own collections or libraries to save all the dashboards you build. This makes it easy to access and manage your work, ensuring that all your reports and dashboards are organized and stored in one convenient place.

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: To create your own collection, click on the "+ New" button located at the top right of your advanced analytics screen and then click on "Collection" . Add a name, and a description to the new collection you create, save it anywhere in your library, and then click on "Create". This will allow you to start organizing and saving your dashboards in a custom library. Actions you can perform once the report is generated 🤔

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 1. After generating the report, you can still make adjustments and refine your search. This includes applying additional filters based on entity fields, summarizing the results using metrics, and grouping data by specific fields. You can also open the search editor to modify your search criteria, refresh the results, and save the updated report to any collection or dashboard you've created.

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 2. You can also interact with each column or field in the report by clicking on the title. This allows you to apply filters to specific columns, adjust the data distribution, sort the column in ascending or descending order, or even merge it with another column. These options give you greater flexibility in customizing and analyzing your report.

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 3. You can make your report easier to read by adding extra details and turning it from a plain table into a chart or graph.. For example, instead of keeping the data in a table, you could include variables such as the number of years of experience for each record or who added the record. Then, you can transform this data into a graph (or any other option from the list of visualizations), making it more visually engaging and easier to interpret. To do this, simply click on the "Visualization" button to change how the table is displayed.

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 4. Once you've made all the changes and customizations to your report, you can save it by adding a title and description. You can store the report in any collection you've created within your account. Additionally, you have the option to add the generated graph or report to a previously created dashboard, or even the default dashboard, where you can arrange it for optimal and personalized visualization. Now that you've created all the reports you need to track your workflow in a more specific and tailored way, you can save and organize them within your dashboard.

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: The dashboard functionality allows you to further customize your reports and manage all this interactive information within a single, unified view. Explore all the features available in your dashboard to maximize its potential and learn how to efficiently manage and interact with the reports you've built. 1. You can further customize your dashboard by adding headings, creating new sections, including any new reports you've created but haven't added yet, and making a variety of other adjustments. This flexibility allows you to tailor your dashboard precisely to your needs, making it a powerful and personalized tool for managing and visualizing your data.

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 2. You can arrange and prioritize the reports in your dashboard by simply dragging and dropping them into the desired sections. Additionally, you can change the visualization options of the reports directly from the dashboard. This flexibility allows you to organize and display your reports in a way that best suits your workflow and highlights the most important information. Once your dashboards are fully created and finalized, the next step is to share them with decision-makers or anyone interested in the statistics you've compiled. This ensures that relevant stakeholders have access to the insights and data you've organized.

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: To share the dashboards you've created, click on the "Share Dashboards Link" button. Once you click on the "Share Dashboards Link" button, a new window will open displaying all the dashboards created in your account. To share a specific dashboard, simply turn on the toggle next to its name. This will generate a link that you can share with anyone. When someone clicks on the link, they will be redirected to the specific dashboard you chose to share. You can set your shared dashboard to auto-refresh, ensuring it stays up-to-date without needing to resend it every time the data changes. To enable this, select a refresh timeframe while editing the dashboard, before sharing it with others.

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Navigate to the Dashboard editing window and click on the small clock icon labeled "Auto-refresh". From there, you can select a timeframe for how often the dashboard will automatically refresh. Once you select a timeframe, a ticking clock icon will appear, indicating when the dashboard will auto-refresh. And that's it! You've successfully built detailed advanced analytics reports and created interactive dashboards using Recruit CRM and the data from your account.

chunks.t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
chunks.x: From viewing the default dashboard to building custom reports, organizing them into personalized dashboards, and sharing auto-refreshing links with stakeholders, Advanced Analytics gives you a complete toolkit for turning your account data into actionable insights. With these fundamentals in place, you're ready to build reports and dashboards tailored to your team's specific needs. If you need help at any stage, feel free to reach out to Recruit CRM support for further assistance.
