chunks.t: Search in Mailbox
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Search in Mailbox feature allows you to find emails by searching using keywords across different email parameters such as To, From, CC, BCC, Email Subject, Email Body. You can also refine your search using specific search parameters, folders, and date ranges to quickly locate the conversations you need. Search for emails containing a specific keyword. Find emails sent to or received from a particular contact/candidate. Narrow down emails by folder, such as Inbox, Sent, or Trash. 1. Navigate to Mailbox , click the search bar, and enter the keyword you want to search for.

chunks.t: Search in Mailbox
chunks.x: 2. By default, Recruit CRM searches across all of the following parameters, however, you can also select the desired ones for a more refined result: Note: Some search parameters may not be available (greyed out) due to limitations imposed by your email provider. These options will appear disabled with a tooltip explaining the limitation. 3. Finally, click Apply Search to display the matching emails. 4. To further refine your search, use the filter panel at the top of the Mailbox. 5. Select the Folder you want to search, such as Inbox , Sent , or Trash . Select a Date Range to display emails from a specific time period. 6. Click Apply to use both filters together.

chunks.t: Search in Mailbox
chunks.x: Problem: No emails are returned after searching. Likely Cause: The keyword entered may be incorrect, or the selected filters are too restrictive. What to Check: Verify that the keyword is spelled correctly. Check the selected search parameters. Confirm the selected folder and date range. Resolution: Modify the keyword or adjust the selected filters, then click Apply Search again. Yes. Select Email Subject as the search parameter before clicking Apply Search . Why are some search parameters unavailable? Some email providers do not support searching across all email fields. Unsupported parameters will automatically appear disabled. Can I search emails in the Sent or Trash folder?

chunks.t: Search in Mailbox
chunks.x: Yes. Select the required folder from the filter panel before applying your search. The Search in Mailbox feature makes it easy to find emails by combining keyword searches with advanced search parameters, folder selection, and date range filters. Using these options together helps you locate conversations quickly and manage your mailbox more efficiently. chunks.t: Requesting Updated Candidate Profiles (New UI)
chunks.x: The Profile Update Request feature in Recruit CRM lets you send candidates an email containing a secure link to a form where they can update their details and CV. Once they submit the form, their information is updated in your Recruit CRM database in real time. You can use this feature: When you want to refresh outdated candidate information or request an updated CV. When you need multiple candidates to update their profiles at once. You must have access to candidate records in Recruit CRM. Ensure your Mailbox is connected so emails can be sent from Recruit CRM. Please note that the profile update link expires after the candidate submits their updated profile.

chunks.t: Requesting Updated Candidate Profiles (New UI)
chunks.x: 1. Request an updated profile from a candidate’s detail page From the candidate’s details page, you can request an updated profile directly. On the candidate’s profile, click the Request Updated Profile button as shown in the image. ​ Once you click on it, the system triggers an email to be sent to the candidate with a URL link. This URL will lead the candidate to the profile update request form that they can fill in to submit their updated details. ​ The details then directly get updated in your system in real-time. 2. Request updated profiles for multiple candidates from the Candidates List page You can send an email to multiple candidates at the same time with the link to update profiles.

chunks.t: Requesting Updated Candidate Profiles (New UI)
chunks.x: 2. Select the candidates whose data you want to update. 3. Click on the Request Updated Profile option at the top. 4. This will trigger an email to all the selected candidates. Note: It's worth noting that each person in the To section is sent as an individual email thread so that the receiver perceives it as a personal message. The link will expire after the candidate submits the updated profile. Edit the email template for requesting updated profiles Scroll down to find the Standard Email Templates button. Click on the pencil icon on the right side of the template to edit the template.

chunks.t: Requesting Updated Candidate Profiles (New UI)
chunks.x: 1. Do not create a new template for the same as the URL for the profile update request will only be generated using the "Request Updated Profile" button and the standard email (which can be edited). 2. Do not remove {URL} from the standard email template body as it is used to trigger some pre-coded actions. You may edit the rest of the email content (subject line, message text, etc.) to match your tone and branding. Customize the profile update request form You can customize the labels and fields on the form and also make certain fields mandatory as well. Click on Profile Update Form Settings . ​

chunks.t: Requesting Updated Candidate Profiles (New UI)
chunks.x: Within the General Page Settings tab, click on the Edit button to edit the labels of buttons and links. ​ Now, switch to the Profile Update Form Field Settings tab. Within this tab, you can edit the label of the fields. Choose the fields to make them visible on the form by turning the toggle on. You can also make certain fields required by enabling the checkbox. You also have the ability to add language and the respective proficiency level to the form. You can add one or multiple default languages to the form by updating the field's value: ​ You can add languages and proficiency levels from here. ​

chunks.t: Requesting Updated Candidate Profiles (New UI)
chunks.x: Once you add it to the form, candidates will have to define a proficiency level for the default languages added. They can also edit the proficiency level for the language already added to their profile in your database. Further, in case there are no default languages added to the form, then candidates can add multiple languages and define the proficiency level for each of them. View candidates who updated their profile 3. Search for the filter called Profile Updated by Candidate On . 4. Select the date or time range you want. You will now see all candidates who updated their profile during the selected period. Problem: Candidate says the link in the email no longer works.

chunks.t: Requesting Updated Candidate Profiles (New UI)
chunks.x: Likely cause: The candidate has already submitted their updated profile, and the link has expired. What to check: Confirm whether the candidate’s record shows recent updates. Resolution path: If more changes are needed, send a new Request Updated Profile email from the candidate’s detail page or update their record manually. Problem: Certain fields never appear on the candidate’s update form. Likely cause: The fields are not set to visible in the Profile Update Form Field Settings . What to check: Go to Admin Settings → Profile Update Form Settings → Profile Update Form Field Settings and check the visibility toggles. Resolution path: Turn the relevant field toggles on and save your changes.

chunks.t: Requesting Updated Candidate Profiles (New UI)
chunks.x: Who can configure the profile update form fields and labels? Typically, users with access to Admin Settings (such as admins or account owners) can configure the Profile Update Form Settings , including labels, visibility, and required fields. How personal are the emails when sending to multiple candidates? When you send profile update requests from the Candidates List page, each person in the To section receives an individual email thread, so the email appears as a personal email. Using the Profile Update Request feature in Recruit CRM, you can quickly refresh candidate data, request updated CVs, and keep your database accurate with minimal manual effort.

chunks.t: Requesting Updated Candidate Profiles (New UI)
chunks.x: Configure the email and form once, and then use individual or bulk requests to maintain up-to-date profiles. 📹 Video tutorial on how the Profile Update feature works within Recruit CRM Social Profile Links - Candidates/Companies/Contacts(New UI)

chunks.t: How to link a candidate to their current organization (New UI)
chunks.x: What does this feature do & when to use it? The Current Organization field lets you associate a candidate with a company in your database as their current employer. This is how you can manage the relationship between candidates and their current organizations and easily update a candidate's profile after being placed in a company. You can use this when: You want to associate candidates with companies stored in your Recruit CRM database. You need to update existing candidates with their current organization. The Current Organization field will not be filled automatically for old candidates already in your database. You will need to manually update the field for those records.

chunks.t: How to link a candidate to their current organization (New UI)
chunks.x: There are multiple ways to update the Current Organization field, including from the candidate form, candidate profile, bulk actions, placement workflow, and the Chrome extension. Only the account owner can manage whether current organizations sourced from LinkedIn are added as companies via Account Settings . The Current Organization field can be added or made visible in layouts if you do not see it by default. You'll find the Current Organization field under Employment Information while adding/editing a candidate. You can search for an existing company or add a new one directly from the search: If you do not see the Current Organization field, you may need to make it visible first.

chunks.t: How to link a candidate to their current organization (New UI)
chunks.x: Click here to learn how you can make a field visible Method 2 - Add Current Organization from Candidate Profile View 2. Hover over an existing field you want to replace, then click the pencil icon to edit the layout. Next, click Replace Field . 3. From the list of available fields, select Current Organization to add it to the candidate’s profile layout. 4. Once added, you can set or update the candidate’s current organization directly in their profile.

chunks.t: How to link a candidate to their current organization (New UI)
chunks.x: For a candidate's Current Organization field, you can save it as plain text, even if a matching company record already exists - instead of it always linking to a company, by clicking on the 'Add as Text' button after entering the current organization: When you search for a company name, you'll see an 'Add as Text' option alongside 'Add as Company' if no company match is found for the entered text. You can click on the 'Add as Company' to create a new company record: Method 3 - Update Current Organization in Bulk 1. From the candidate list page, select all candidates whose current organization you want to update. 2. Click the Update Field option from the options at the top.

chunks.t: How to link a candidate to their current organization (New UI)
chunks.x: 3. In the field selection dropdown, choose Current Organization . 4. Then select the appropriate company from the dropdown list. Pro tip: Use Advanced Search to filter candidates where Current Organization is set to “Not Available,” then bulk update this field if you know their current employer. Method 4 - Update Current Organization When Placing a Candidate When you move a candidate to the Placed hiring stage, you will see an option to update their Current Organization based on the company linked to the job. Confirm this update so the candidate is automatically associated with the hiring company as their current employer. Method 5 - Use the Chrome Extension to Maintain Current Organization

chunks.t: How to link a candidate to their current organization (New UI)
chunks.x: When sourcing candidates via the Chrome extension , the candidate’s current organization will automatically be added as a new company in Recruit CRM if it does not already exist. Note: A candidate’s current organization will now always be updated with the latest data when sourcing via the Chrome Extension, even if the Override Data toggle is turned off. This ensures users never miss the most up-to-date employer information. If you don't want the candidate's current organization to be added to your database while sourcing candidates through LinkedIn, you can disable the feature in the Account Settings: Only the account owner will be able to manage the settings.

chunks.t: How to link a candidate to their current organization (New UI)
chunks.x: When a new candidate is added to the database, if the current organization is available and the same organization is present in the database, the candidate will be automatically associated with the current organization based on the company’s. ​ If we are unable to match the candidate to a company it will simply be stored as plain text. View All Candidates Employed at a Company 1. Inside a candidate’s profile, click the Current Organization field value to open that company’s profile page. 2. On the company profile, scroll down and click the Candidates Employed tab. 3. Here, you will see a list of all candidates currently working for that company.

chunks.t: How to link a candidate to their current organization (New UI)
chunks.x: From this tab, you can perform bulk actions such as assigning them to a job, updating fields, composing an email, adding a note, and more. You can also hide specific fields and run an Advanced Search within this list to refine the view. When saving a company via the Chrome extension, you will have the option to also save the associated contact as a candidate. If selected, that person will be added as a candidate in the system and automatically appear under the Candidates Employed tab for that company. Problem : The Current Organization field is not visible when adding or editing a candidate. Likely cause: The field is hidden in your layout.

chunks.t: How to link a candidate to their current organization (New UI)
chunks.x: What to check: Look for the help button in the Employment Information section and confirm field visibility settings. Resolution path: Make the Current Organization field visible in the layout, then return to the candidate form and fill it in. Can I stop new companies being created from LinkedIn sourcing? Yes. If you don't want the candidate's current organization to be added to your database while sourcing candidates through LinkedIn, you can disable the feature in the account settings. Only the account owner will be able to manage the settings.

chunks.t: How to link a candidate to their current organization (New UI)
chunks.x: Using the Current Organization field is the most reliable way to keep candidate–company relationships accurate in Recruit CRM. By combining individual updates, bulk actions, placement workflows, and the Chrome extension, you can maintain a clean, searchable database and quickly see which candidates work for which organizations. chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Query Builder in Advanced Analytics is a graphical interface that allows you to explore your data without writing SQL. In Advanced Analytics, queries and their visualizations are called "questions." Use the Query Builder whenever you need a custom view that an existing dashboard doesn't already cover, for example, checking deal values by owner, tracking candidates through pipeline stages, or spotting trends in placements over a chosen date range. Because you build the question step by step, you can start with a simple table and keep refining it until it answers the exact question you have.

chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: You can build your question using the following components: Filters – Narrow down your data based on specific conditions. Summaries – Aggregate data, such as calculating totals or averages. Custom Columns – Create new columns, like adding a Total column that sums Subtotal + Tax. Joins – Combine data from multiple tables. Sorts – Arrange data in ascending or descending order for better analysis. With these building blocks, you can filter, group, and visualize your data effectively within the Advanced Analytics interface.

chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: You can combine the query builder blocks in different order, and have multiple blocks of the same type — for example, filter, summarize, then filter the summarized results, join them with a different table, and add another summary. The next step of your query will use the result from the previous one. Step-by-step instructions on how to create and visualize a basic question in Advanced Analytics For example, we’ll work with the Deals table in the database. Start a new query builder question using table Deals from the Database as the source: In the data picker, switch to “Tables” tab, select the Deals table.

chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Once selected, Advanced Analytics will open the Query Builder, displaying Data, Filter, and Summary options. Click the Play button next to the Data section to preview the table. At every stage of your question, you can preview results as a table or create a visualization, and you can switch between the query builder, the query’s result as a chart, and the results as a table at any time. In our case, the Deals table looks like this: Deals in the table seem to have different Deal Stages. Let’s filter the data to show just the Deals in “Won” Deal Stage . In the Filter block, click "Add filter." (If no Filter block exists, click the green Filter icon below the Data block.)

chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Set the filter type to "Is" and choose "Won." Click the Play button to preview the filtered results. To see if there are any patterns in these deals, let’s see how the Deal Values are distributed by Owner Names. 1.In the gray “Summarize” block, add a “Sum” metric of Deal Value grouped by the Owner Name column. Advanced Analytics might have already added a blank Summarize block for you, but if not, you can click on the gray “Σ” icon below the Filter block to add it. 2.Click the Play button to preview the summarized data. To view the results as a chart, click on the “Visualize” button at the bottom of the query builder.

chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: That’s it! Advanced Analytics will automatically create a bar chart for you: To reorder the bars, we can sort the result of our query. Go back to the query builder by clicking on the “Show editor” button in the top right corner; Add a Sort block and sort by Sum of Deal Value. Click on the ↑ icon to change the sort order from descending to ascending. To save your question for future reference or sharing click on the “Save” button at the top right corner.

chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Advanced Analytics will ask you which collection you want to save your question in. Collections in Advanced Analytics are like folders – you can use them to organize your work. This allows you to easily access, manage, and share your visualizations later. After saving your question, you can add it to a dashboard for easier access and reporting. Click the Add to Dashboard option in the top-right corner. 3. Choose an existing dashboard or create a new dashboard. 4. Select the desired dashboard and click Save . 5. Open the dashboard to verify that the chart has been added successfully.

chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Tip: Adding questions to dashboards allows you to combine multiple charts and metrics in a single view, making it easier to monitor key recruitment performance indicators. Alternative way to add a question to a dashboard Click on the edit button on the top right. 4. Select the chart (question) that is to be added to the dashboard. 5. Place it where you want and click on Save . How to change the visualization type in Advanced Analytics? Advanced Analytics automatically selects a suitable chart type based on your data. For example, a time series will default to a line chart, while categorical summaries typically appear as bar charts. Let’s change the bar chart to a pie chart:

chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: If you are in the query builder, enter the visualization view by clicking on the “Visualize” button; Open visualization options by clicking on the “Visualization” in the bottom left corner; Select a pie chart (or another preferred chart type). 💡 Tip : Advanced Analytics has a ton of chart options, but not all chart types work with every dataset. At the top of the visualization sidebar, Advanced Analytics highlights the best options based on your data. Charts in the “Other charts” section may not be compatible. If you want to analyze seasonal trends in deal value while focusing only on existing business deals, follow these steps: Filter: Add a filter for Deal Type = Existing Business.

chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Summarize: Group the data by Close Date: Month. Sort: Add a secondary sort by Close Date (ascending). Visualize: The grouped data will automatically switch to a line chart with a date axis, showing a separate time series for each Owner. This approach helps you refine and customize your analysis for deeper insights. To view values on data points in the chart, follow these steps: Click the settings button next to the visualization. Enable the "Show values on data points" option. This will make the values visible on the chart. Similarly, you can add currency values to the data points by following these steps: Click the settings button next to the visualization.

chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Select "Currency" to apply the currency format. You can continue refining your query by adding more filters, summaries, or even joining another table . For example, we see on our line chart that there are times where the Sum of deal value has huge spikes. Let’s count these spikes per plan. Go back to the query builder by clicking on “Show editor” button in the top right corner. Add another Filter block after the Summarize block and filter for Sum of deal value over 2,000,000. Add another Summarize block after the second Filter block, and Count the rows by Owner Name. Switch views between the chart and raw table by clicking the table button at the bottom center.

chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: By layering filters and summaries , we created a complex query that counts, by Owner Name, the months where the total Deal Value exceeded 2,000,000 —all without writing SQL! Problem: If you’re unable to select a particular chart type. Likely cause: The selected visualization is not compatible with the current dataset. Some chart types require specific data structures (for example, a pie chart requires one dimension and one metric). What to check: Verify that your chart includes the required dimensions and metrics. Check whether the data has been grouped or summarized appropriately.

chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Resolution path: Use one of the recommended chart types, or modify the Summarize step so the query returns data compatible with the desired visualization. Problem: If you’re experiencing a “Something went wrong" error message. Likely cause: The query contains an invalid filter combination, depends on a modified or deleted saved question/model, or has timed out due to processing a large dataset. What to check: Review any recently added filters. Verify that the underlying data source or saved question is still available.

chunks.t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Resolution path: Remove or simplify filters one at a time to identify the issue. If the problem persists, reduce the query complexity or contact your administrator to verify the underlying data source or model. The Query Builder lets you filter, summarize, sort, and visualize data without writing SQL, turning raw tables into charts you can save and share on dashboards. Once you're comfortable combining these blocks, you can build increasingly refined questions to answer specific business needs. If you need help at any stage, feel free to reach out to Recruit CRM support for further assistance. Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? If you ever find yourself in a situation where you need to create nearly identical copies of the same dashboard, with just one different variable, there’s a better solution. Instead of creating multiple copies of the same dashboard, you can add filter or parameters. These let users change the data shown on dashboard cards themselves, without needing a separate dashboard for each variation. Step-by-step instructions on how to add a filter or parameter 1. Click the pencil icon to enter the dashboard editing mode. 2. Click the filter icon that appears in the top right to add a filter.

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: 4 . Connect your filter to dashboard cards to one or more dashboard cards on any or all tabs. Advanced Analytics will display the filter only if the filter is connected to a card on the current dashboard tab. The type of filter or parameter widget you choose will determine how the widget works, as well as which fields you’ll be able to filter your cards by: When picking a Time filter, Advanced Analytics will prompt you to pick a specific type of date picker widget:

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: Single Date and Date Range will provide a calendar widget, while the other options all provide slightly different dropdown interfaces for picking values. To get a widget that’s just like the time filter in the query builder, choose All options. You can add a time grouping filter to a dashboard to change how charts are grouped by time. For example, you may want to look at the time series charts grouped by month by default, but give people the option to view the results by other groupings: by week, by quarter, and so on. Time grouping parameter widget can only be connected to questions built with the graphical query builder .

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: This widget doesn’t filter data in the charts; the widget just changes the time granularity for any cards that have a datetime field connected to the widget. There are four types of Location filters to choose from: The ID filter provides a simple input box where you can type the ID of a Owner, deal name etc. A flexible filter type that will let you create either a dropdown menu or an input box to filter on any category field in your cards. Options include: Is . Select one or more values from a list or search box. Is not . Exclude one or more specific values. Contains . Match values that contain the entered text. Does not contain . Filter out values that contain the entered text.

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: Starts with . Match values that begin with the entered text. Ends with . Match values that end with the entered text. How to connect a filter or parameter widget to dashboard cards? Dashboard widgets apply across all dashboard tabs , though they’ll only be displayed when a tab has cards connected to the widget. Steps to connect a filter to a dashboard card: Click on the dropdown menu of the card you want to filter. Select the field that the widget should filter on. Here we’ve wired up a Date Picker filter to the “Deal Value Closed over Time” card, telling Advanced Analytics that the column to filter on should be the Deals Close Date field: How does auto-connecting filters to cards work?

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: If other cards on your dashboard have the same field as the one you selected, Advanced Analytics will automatically connect the filter to those cards, including relevant cards on other tabs. Click on the toast notification that appears when Advanced Analytics auto-connects the cards. Manually disconnect the cards by clicking the “X” next to the connected field. Wiring up dashboard filters to text cards You can even wire up filters to text cards, but only if the text card includes a variable .

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: You can tell Advanced Analytics to require a filter so that people must filter the dashboard by a certain column on a card. If you require a filter, you’ll also need to supply a default value for that filter. If your dashboard pulls a large amount of data, making it slow or difficult to interpret without filtering. If your dashboard is meant to show data for a specific customer, project, or category instead of all available data. Click the pencil icon to enter dashboard editing mode. Click directly on the filter widget you want to edit. A settings sidebar will open on the right.

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: From this filter editing view, you can wire up dashboard cards to the filter, or use the filter settings sidebar to: In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. Renaming the filter only affects the filter’s display; the label has no effect on filtering logic. In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. In the sidebar, change the Filter or parameter type dropdown. Reconnect the widget to the relevant columns on each card. If you change the type by mistake, click Cancel to exit edit mode without saving. In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar.

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: In the sidebar, use the Filter operator dropdown to select the desired operator. In dashboard edit mode, click your filter’s widget to open the settings sidebar. From the filter settings sidebar, set How should people filter on this column? : Dropdown list – Displays all possible values with checkboxes (best for predefined lists). Search box – Suggests values as users type (default for columns with <100 unique values). Input box – Allows manual text input (default for columns with >100 unique values). In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. From the sidebar, find People can pick and select 'Multiple values'. How to Change a filter’s selectable values?

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. From the sidebar, find How should users filter on this column?. Click Edit (to the right of 'Dropdown list') to specify where the values should come from: If you don't see 'Dropdown list' as an option, go to Filter widgets: Dropdown list for more info. If you don’t see “Dropdown list” as an option, go to Filter widgets: Dropdown list for more info. In dashboard edit mode, Click on the filter you want to make required. A filter sidebar should pop up on the right side. From the sidebar, choose a value from the Default value input field.

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: For example, you might want to set a default filter value like “Active”, so that when people load your dashboard, they only see data for “Active” records (not “Inactive”, “Cancelled”, etc). In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. Scroll to the Always require a value toggle and turn it on. In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. Select a card, heading, or Top of the page to make it a dashboard-wide filter. Reconnect the widget to the correct columns after moving. In dashboard edit mode, click the filter you want to edit.

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: Accidentally removed a filter? Click Cancel in the top-right to exit edit mode without saving changes. In dashboard edit mode, click on the grabber handle (six dots) on the right side of a filter widget, then drag the widget to a different position. You can also link filters so that a child filter knows to limit its choices based on the activation of a parent filter. Say you have two filters, one to filter by state, the other to filter by city. You can link the city filter to the state filter so that when someone filters by California, the city filter will “know” to only show cities in California. In this case, state is the parent filter, and city is the child filter.

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: Click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. Go to the "Linked Filters" tab and select the parent filter. In the above scenario, with a state and city filter, we’d edit the child filter, city, by clicking on the gears icon on the city filter. From the filter sidebar on the right, select the Linked filters tab. You can’t link filters that use “Custom List” or “From another model or question” as their value’s source. Once you’ve added a filter to your dashboard, just click on the filter widget to select a value and activate the filter. To stop filtering, just click the blue ‘X’.

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: Your active filter will only apply to your view of the dashboard. If someone else is viewing the same dashboard link at the same time, they won’t see your filter. 💡You can also set up a dashboard question to update a filter on click . Problem: The filter widget doesn’t appear on the dashboard at all Likely cause: The filter is not connected to any card on the current dashboard tab. A filter only appears on a tab when it is connected to at least one card on that tab. What to check: Check whether the filter is connected to at least one card on the tab where you expect it to appear.

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: Resolution path: Enter dashboard editing mode, select the filter, and connect it to at least one card on the relevant tab. Do filters automatically refresh the dashboard? By default, changing a filter value refreshes the dashboard immediately. Yes. If a dashboard is large or slow, you can disable auto-apply: Click Apply manually after setting all filters. With auto-apply turned off, each time you change a value in a filter, you’ll need to click the Apply button to refresh the dashboard with the new filter value.

chunks.t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
chunks.x: Filters and parameters let you build one flexible dashboard instead of maintaining multiple near-identical copies, dynamically changing what data or time grouping each card displays. With options like filters and default values, you can tailor a single dashboard to serve different users and use cases. If you need help at any stage, feel free to reach out to Recruit CRM support for further assistance. chunks.t: Summarize Data in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Summarizing data helps answer questions like "How much revenue was made each day last week?" by calculating averages, totals, and other key metrics. You'll reach for summarization any time you need a single number or a grouped comparison instead of raw rows. For example, total placements this quarter, average deal value by owner, or candidate counts by pipeline stage. It's the step to use when you've already got the right data in front of you and just need to roll it up into something you can read at a glance or turn into a chart. Click here to know more about how to a create chart (question)

chunks.t: Summarize Data in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Summarizing means combining data from multiple records together and producing a single number, like the “average of product ratings”. So you need to determine: The numerical metric that’s going to be used to combine value. For example, count, sum, or average The column whose values will be combined. For example, quantity, price, or rating (optionally) Breakouts . They determine the groups that the data is broken out by (or grouped ). For example, you can compute order quantity grouped/broken out by months. For example , in Advanced Analytics, you can find: Average Deal Value by Owner Name for each month:

chunks.t: Summarize Data in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: In all these cases, the metric is Average, and the column is Deal Value, but adding breakouts creates different summaries and charts. Step-by-step instructions on how to summarize data by a column in Advanced Analytics You can quickly summarize your data by clicking on a column header in a table. The available summary options depend on the column type (e.g., numerical, categorical, date). There are multiple ways to add summaries in Advanced Analytics: Click on the column header to summarize by that column. Click “Summarize” button (top-right corner) when viewing a table or chart. In the “Summarize by” block, select a metric (e.g., Sum, Count, Average).

chunks.t: Summarize Data in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: In the “Group by” block, choose how to categorize your data. Click “+” to add more breakouts (grouping levels). Add a Summarize block in the query builder and select metrics, columns, and breakouts. For more details, refer to Ask a question in the query builder . How to pick the right chart for your summaries? When you click “visualize” on a question with summaries, Advanced Analytics will automatically select a chart that it believes is the most appropriate for your result. For example, if you group by a time series column, Advanced Analytics will create a line chart. In most cases, the chart that Advanced Analytics picks will be the best option.

chunks.t: Summarize Data in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: You can change the chart type . Advanced Analytics charts have requirements on the number and the kind of breakouts you can use in summaries that feed into the chart: Displays raw or summarised query results as rows and columns, no grouping needed 1 breakout by a column with geographical data 1 breakout by a column with time series data First breakout for the X-axis (or Y-axis for row charts), second breakout for color First breakout for the X-axis, second for color, and third for the bubble size First breakout for source nodes, second breakout for target nodes; metric column determines the flow size between nodes Displays the full record for a single row, used for drilldown views

chunks.t: Summarize Data in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: 1 required breakout; optional 2nd breakout First breakout for the X-axis categories; optional second breakout creates colored series per category You can switch chart types (e.g., Pie → Bar) but some charts (e.g., Pivot Table) may have restrictions based on the number of breakouts used. If you need more complex summaries, such as calculating average or applying conditional logic, you can use Custom Expressions in Advanced Analytics. For example, summing up of deal values only when the weighted deal percentage is 33%: SumIf([Deal Value], [Weighed Deal Percentage] = 33) Check out our article on custom expressions to learn more.

chunks.t: Summarize Data in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Advanced Analytics automatically selects a granularity to group by: for example, for date columns, it will automatically group by months. groups date/time columns (e.g., by month). To change the granularity, click on the time period and select a different unit (day, week, quarter, etc.). In Advanced Analytics, you can also group by numeric variables, like Deal Value. Advanced Analytics will bin the numerical variable for you, creating range-based “categories” for grouping: If you group by a numeric variable and select "Count" as the metric, Advanced Analytics will generate a histogram (a distribution chart) of this variable. Advanced Analytics has two types of cumulative summaries:

chunks.t: Summarize Data in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: For every record, they will return the sum or count of all values up to this record in the table.These summaries work a bit differently from other summaries because the data they return depends on the order of the data in your table. Let’s say you have a table with values by month. Cumulative sum will be computed like this: But if the months ordering is changed (while values remain the same), then the cumulative sum is changed as well: Advanced Analytics “Distinct values” summary returns the number of unique values in a column. To see the distinct values themselves, you can create any summary with a breakout by that column instead. Example: Counting Distinct Deals per Owner

chunks.t: Summarize Data in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: If you want to see how many different deals each Owner has handled, use: 🔹 Distinct count of Deal Name grouped by Owner Name. This will give you a column with all the Owner Names, and a column with row counts for every Owner Name (you can hide the count column from the results): In SQL, you summarize by adding a function like COUNT into a SELECT statement — similarly to how you’d add a new column computed based on the values of other columns. In Advanced Analytics, these two operations are distinct: to add a new column, you can use a Custom column block, but to add an aggregation, you use a Summary block. Problem: If the chart is blank or empty, with no error displayed.

chunks.t: Summarize Data in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Likely cause: The query has not been summarized. Most visualizations require at least one aggregation (such as Count, Sum, or Average) and, in many cases, a grouping field. What to check: Verify that a Summarize step has been added. Ensure that at least one aggregation (for example, Count of, Sum of, or Average of) is selected. Resolution path: Add the required aggregation and grouping in the Summarize step, then rerun the query and visualize the results.

chunks.t: Summarize Data in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Summarization turns raw records into meaningful metrics by combining a numerical measure, a target column, and optional breakouts, giving you totals, averages, counts, and more. With options like custom expressions, cumulative summaries, and distinct values, you can tailor summaries to answer even complex business questions. If you need help at any stage, feel free to reach out to Recruit CRM support for further assistance Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics Finding Data, Dashboards & Charts in Advanced Analytics

chunks.t: Explore dashboards in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Step-by-step instructions on how to explore dashboards in Metabase You can find the Shared collection in the left navigation sidebar. If you need a refresher, check out the article on how to find data in Advanced Analytics . We’ll work with the Default dashboard pinned in the Shared collection. In Advanced Analytics, you can explore the numbers behind every dashboard and chart by viewing them in table format. 1.Go to the default dashboard in the Shared collection

chunks.t: Explore dashboards in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: You should see multiple tabs and cards with charts. For example, the “Candidates added per month” card shows the new candidate count for each month. The data shows an interesting seasonal pattern for candidates, so let’s explore it further! 2.Open the question “Candidates added per month” by clicking on the chart title in the dashboard. From the question view, you can add summaries and filters, but first, let’s look at the raw results behind the question. 3.See the results as a table by clicking on the table icon under the chart.

chunks.t: Explore dashboards in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Each row represents a month, and there are two columns: one for created on: month and other for count of candidates, corresponding to the series displayed on the chart. You can switch back to visualization by clicking on the chart icon next to the table icon. You can modify a chart’s visualization without affecting other users unless you overwrite the question. For example, you can switch between showing time series as a bar chart or a line chart, or maybe you just really hate pie charts (not us – we love all our charts equally). And our pies are technically donuts. Let’s make “ Candidates added per month ” into a bar chart.

chunks.t: Explore dashboards in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: 1.Open the question “Candidates added per month” from the Shared Collection. 2.Open the visualization sidebar by clicking on the “Visualization” icon in the bottom left of the chart. You’ll see that this is currently a line chart. 3.Switch to a bar chart by clicking on “Bar”. Now the series – total candidates added per month will be represented by bars. Many charts in Advanced Analytics allow you to drill down into data by simply clicking on a data point. 1.Open the default dashboard and switch to the “Deals & Companies “ tab . The “Total Deals by Deal Stage ” chart shows the number of deals for each deal stage. The Won stage has the largest number of deals.

chunks.t: Explore dashboards in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: We can dive deeper into these numbers and look at the deals that contribute to this. 2. Look at all deals in Won stage on the “Total Deals by Deal Stage” chart: This will open a table displaying all deals in the won stage. You can now look for patterns, such as which owners have the most deals at this stage. Let’s look for all Won stage deals for a specific filter. 3. How can I filter deals by a specific owner? Once you’ve drilled down to a table view, you can further refine the data: Find all records for deals with “Vivek Singhs” as Owner Name: Find the Owner Name column and click on column name. 3.Select name of the person you want to filter out by and click add filter

chunks.t: Explore dashboards in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: 4.The table will now show only deals in won stage for this owner. The active filters will be displayed above the table. 5.You can continue drilling further, for example, by clicking on a Collaborator name to filter deals for that owner and collaborator. 6 . Return to the original “Total Deals by Deal Stage” question by clicking on “Started from Total Deals by Deal Stage ” at the top left of your screen. The drill through options that you get depend on the type of chart you’re using and your data: for example, on time series charts you can select a time period to zoom in on it. You can explore the data behind the dashboards and questions on your own. For example, you can

chunks.t: Explore dashboards in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Drill down on metrics to see individual records. Problem: The dashboard or chart displays outdated data. Likely cause : The results are being served from your browser cache. What to check: Refresh the page after clearing your browser cache. Open the underlying question to verify whether it now displays the latest data. Resolution path: Clear your browser cache and reload the page. This resolves the issue in almost all cases. Problem: The numbers on the dashboard do not match the same chart when opened separately. Likely cause : Dashboard filters are being applied in addition to the chart's own filters, resulting in different values.

chunks.t: Explore dashboards in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: What to check: Check whether any dashboard filters are currently applied. Open the underlying question and compare its configured filters with the dashboard filters. Verify whether both the dashboard and the standalone question are using the same filter values. Resolution path: Clear any active dashboard filters and compare the chart again. If the values still differ, review the filters configured within the underlying question and ensure they align with the dashboard filters.

chunks.t: Explore dashboards in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Dashboards aren't just static charts, you can view the underlying data as a table, switch visualization types, and drill down into individual records to investigate the patterns behind the numbers. These exploration tools help you move from a high-level chart to specific, actionable insights without leaving Advanced Analytics. If you need help at any stage, feel free to reach out to Recruit CRM support for further assistance. chunks.t: Bulk Importing Records into Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use this feature? The bulk import feature allows you to create or update multiple records at once, helping you standardize data and reduce manual effort. You can use this feature: When you’re migrating data from another ATS/ CRM tool or from a spreadsheet. When you need to add candidates/contacts/companies at once in bulk. When you’re cleaning and re-importing data with updated information. If you have a file in XLSX format, you'll first need to convert it into XLS. ​ Here's how you can do this Before you import a file, please make sure it has column headers .

chunks.t: Bulk Importing Records into Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: If your spreadsheet has additional columns that are not available in Recruit CRM, you first need to create custom fields to map those columns into the system. Special characters like "<,>, & OR;" present in the file, crash the code for import. You need to remove these before importing the file. We do not have the option to import profile pictures into the CRM. The process to import candidates/companies/contacts is the same. Here, we have taken the example of the Candidates Entity. 1. In Recruit CRM, navigate to the ' Candidates ' entity. 2. Click the arrow icon next to the Add Candidate button and select the 'Import CSV/XLS' option.

chunks.t: Bulk Importing Records into Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: 3. Click on the Upload File button and select your file that contains the data that needs to be imported. Note: Up to 10,000 records can be imported in a single upload. To download a sample CSV file before your import so you can format your data for easier matching, click here: 5. The next step is to map file columns to Recruit CRM fields. Mapping your Recruit CRM fields with the columns in your CSV/XLS file is crucial to make sure that the information in those columns is correctly saved in Recruit CRM. 1. After the file is uploaded, the mapping template window appears.

chunks.t: Bulk Importing Records into Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: 2. On the left side, you will see the column headers from your CSV/XLS file. On the right side, you will be able to see the available Recruit CRM fields. 3. For each column, select the most accurate corresponding Recruit CRM field to ensure data is stored correctly. 6. To make this process easier for you, we've implemented a feature that covers this step by creating mapping templates. This means you won't have to map the fields manually every single time you upload a file by having your mapping track saved in a template. To save a mapping template, follow the next steps: Once all columns are mapped, you can save this configuration as a mapping template by clicking the 'Save Mapping' option.

chunks.t: Bulk Importing Records into Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: 2. Enter a name for the mapping template. If you want to share this mapping template with your teammates, turn on the sharing toggle and click the Save button to save the template. This stored template lets you apply the same field mappings to future files without redoing the mapping manually. If you select the option Include first header row of CSV or XLS file , you will not be able to save a mapping template. This setting indicates there are no column names available for mapping, so the template cannot identify which columns to associate with which fields. After confirming all mappings, click Import Candidates to proceed.

chunks.t: Bulk Importing Records into Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: 8. You will now see options to merge duplicate records during the import. Recruit CRM lets you merge duplicates based on any one of the unique parameters for each entity. Those unique identifiers are: Candidates: Email ID, LinkedIn URL, or Contact Number Contacts: Contact Number, Email ID, or LinkedIn URL. Companies: Company Name, Website URL, or LinkedIn URL 1. When you click Merge Duplicates , the system prompts you to select one unique parameter to use for detecting duplicates. During import, duplicates will be merged based on the selected parameter. 2. The 'Override Data' toggle provided below allows you to choose whether imported data should override existing records in the database.

chunks.t: Bulk Importing Records into Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: Enabling the override option ensures that duplicate records in the database are updated with the latest information from the imported spreadsheet. If information is not present in the spreadsheet, existing data will remain unaffected. When the toggle is set to 'OFF', merging duplicates won't override any existing data in Recruit CRM; instead, it will solely update the empty fields on the record with new information present in the CSV. After configuring these options, click Confirm Merge . 9. After confirming merge settings, you will see two options: Add to Hotlist or Import Now . If you do not want to add the records to a Hotlist, select No, Import Now .

chunks.t: Bulk Importing Records into Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: If you choose the “ Add to Hotlist ” option, you will see all existing Hotlists in your account and will have the option to create a new one as well. 10. Click the Import button to begin importing all records. Depending on the size of your file, the import may take a few minutes. 11. When completed, look for an Import Successful notification to confirm success. You have the flexibility to include both companies and their corresponding contacts within the same CSV/XLS sheet. This allows for the seamless import of both company details and the associated contacts working within those companies into your database in one go.

chunks.t: Bulk Importing Records into Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: When bulk importing companies, it's important to understand even if you opt for the 'Do Not Merge' option, the system automatically merges the companies from the backend based on unique parameters i.e., Name, Website URL, and LinkedIn URL. Opting for the 'Merge Duplicates' option enables you to merge the contacts being imported along with the companies, based on the unique parameters i.e. Contact number , Email ID or LinkedIn URL . Problem: Import fails or shows “Import Failed” / “Import Unsuccessful.” message. Likely cause: File formatting issues or unsupported characters. Confirm the file is CSV or XLS (not XLSX) and is under 10,000 records.

chunks.t: Bulk Importing Records into Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: Look for special characters, merged cells, or formulas in the file. Ensure the first row is a header row, not data. Clean the file (remove special characters, merged cells, and formulas). Can I import more than 10,000 records at once? No. A single import supports up to 10,000 records. For larger datasets, split your file into multiple smaller files and run separate imports. Bulk importing records from CSV or XLS into Recruit CRM lets you quickly populate and update your database while controlling field mapping and duplicate handling. By preparing your file carefully and following the steps in this guide, you can complete reliable imports that keep your data accurate and usable.

This automation also keeps all relevant team members informed in real time and reduces manual communication. Click on the Connections tab under the 'Workflows' section and click on the 'Create' button >>> 'Connection'.

chunks.t: Workflow Automation- Send channel messages in Microsoft Teams for new Recruit CRM jobs/when new candidates apply through job pages in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 3. Use the search bar to search for the Recruit CRM app and connect it by selecting it and entering the API key . chunks.t: Workflow Automation- Send channel messages in Microsoft Teams for new Recruit CRM jobs/when new candidates apply through job pages in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Once all the required apps are connected, you can select the connected account inside the related steps of the recipe from here (for new jobs created recipe) and from here (for when candidates apply for a job recipe). 📋 Overview of each step in the Recipe for new jobs created 1. Trigger: New Job Created in Recruit CRM This is the starting point of the automation. It gets triggered whenever a job is created in Recruit CRM. It helps in monitoring the following actions for errors. This makes the automation more reliable.. Post a channel message via the Teams workbot

chunks.t: Workflow Automation- Send channel messages in Microsoft Teams for new Recruit CRM jobs/when new candidates apply through job pages in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: If something fails within the Monitor block, then this step is triggered. The Retry Logic ensures that if the errors match those specified (429, 500–504), it retries the monitored actions up to 3 times. If the error continues after 3 retries, or if the error doesn’t match the handled types, the automation stops. 📋 Overview of each step in the Recipe when a candidate applies to a job 1. Trigger: Candidate applied for a job through the job pages in Recruit CRM This is the starting point of the automation. It gets triggered whenever a candidate applies for a job through the job pages in Recruit CRM.

chunks.t: Workflow Automation- Send channel messages in Microsoft Teams for new Recruit CRM jobs/when new candidates apply through job pages in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: It helps in monitoring the following actions for errors. This makes the automation more reliable. Posts a message when a candidate applies to a job. If something fails within the Monitor block, then this step is triggered. The Retry Logic ensures that if the errors match those specified (429, 500–504), it retries the monitored actions up to 3 times. If the error continues after 3 retries, or if the error doesn’t match the handled types, the automation stops. chunks.t: Commonly used API Endpoints for Careers Page (Part 1)
chunks.x: Important note when using our API endpoints While asking our API to GET/POST/DELETE the required data, one must not directly query the endpoint on the front end/webpage, as it exposes the API token. You would need to hide the Recruit CRM API token/Bearer token. This can be done by introducing a server in between or by making the API token abstract. Basically, the webpage on the front end would query a private server in between which would then query the Recruit CRM API. This is the safest way of doing this, as it would then prevent exposing the Recruit CRM API token/key publicly.

chunks.t: Commonly used API Endpoints for Careers Page (Part 1)
chunks.x: A) General data flow to fetch jobs from Recruit CRM using its API: ​ ​ 1. Show Open Jobs from Recruit CRM to Careers Page (Your Website) Use Search for Jobs Endpoint - Open Jobs Only GET https://api.recruitcrm.io/v1/jobs/search ​ This endpoint should be used to search open jobs, and the request body should contain the job_status value. In this case, the job_status value will be ‘1’ as we don’t use alphabets for job status but integers or IDs, and the same can be found here: The cURL request would look something like this:

chunks.t: Commonly used API Endpoints for Careers Page (Part 1)
chunks.x: curl --request GET \ --url 'https://api.recruitcrm.io/v1/jobs/search?job_status=1' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_API_TOKEN}' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' The response to this API request will fetch a list of all the “Open” jobs from the Recruit CRM account whose API token is given in the request.

chunks.t: See All Emails
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The See All Emails feature allows Account Owners and users with the appropriate Custom Role permissions to view other users' mailboxes directly from the Recruit CRM Mailbox. View another user's mailbox from within Recruit CRM. Monitor email conversations across your team. Search for a teammate's mailbox using their name or email address. Improve collaboration and visibility across your organization. Navigate to Mailbox and click the arrow icon next to your mailbox. Select your mailbox or choose a teammate's mailbox from the list. Use the search bar to quickly find a teammate by their name or email address, if required.

chunks.t: See All Emails
chunks.x: Note: This feature is available only for Account Owners and users assigned a Custom Role with the required permission. Custom Roles & Permissions are available on the Business Plan or higher. Navigate to User Management and open the Roles & Permissions tab . Create a new custom role by clicking New Role, or edit an existing role by clicking the three-dot menu and selecting Edit. Enable the Access to the complete Mailbox & Emails of all users permission. Scroll all the way down and click Save Role on the bottom right to apply your changes. Problem: I cannot view another user's mailbox. Likely Cause: Your account does not have permission to access other users' mailboxes.

chunks.t: See All Emails
chunks.x: What to Check: Verify whether you are an Account Owner or have been assigned a Custom Role with the All Users' Mailbox Access permission enabled. Resolution: Contact your Account Owner or admin to enable the required permission for your role. Only Account Owners and users with a Custom Role that has the All Users' Mailbox Access permission enabled can view other users' mailboxes. 2. Can I search for a teammate's mailbox? Yes. You can use the search bar in the mailbox dropdown to search for teammates by their name or email address.

chunks.t: Scheduling Reports for Your Dashboard in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Dashboard Subscriptions let you deliver a dashboard's results automatically, on a schedule, without anyone having to log in and check it manually. Use this when you have stakeholders recruiters, account managers, clients, or teammates without a Recruit CRM license — who need regular visibility into a dashboard, such as a weekly placements summary or a daily pipeline snapshot, but don't need to interact with the dashboard itself. How can I send dashboard updates via email? You can use Dashboard Subscriptions to automatically send dashboard results to people via email, even if they don’t have a license on Recruit CRM.

chunks.t: Scheduling Reports for Your Dashboard in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: Once set up, updates will be sent at your chosen frequency, and any changes to the dashboard will be reflected in future deliveries. Note: Subscriptions are private to the person who created them, a subscription you set up won't be visible to your teammates, and you won't see subscriptions they've created either. The same is true for Alerts: only the person who created an alert can see it. All scheduled subscriptions are sent according to the UTC timezone . When selecting the delivery time, please make sure to account for the difference between UTC and your local timezone. Step-by-step instructions on how to create a subscription to a dashboard 4.In the sidebar that appears, choose Email it.

chunks.t: Scheduling Reports for Your Dashboard in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: When you click on Email it option in the sidebar, and advanced analytics will give us some options: 5.Set the delivery options, including recipients and frequency. What email subscription options are available? Add subscribers: Add email addresses to register subscribers. Determine frequency and timing: Choose how often to send updates: And what time of day to send the dashboard? Send email now – Instantly send the dashboard update. Skip emails with no results – Prevents sending empty reports. Apply filters – Customize subscription filter values. How to customize filters for different subscriptions?

chunks.t: Scheduling Reports for Your Dashboard in Advanced Analytics
chunks.x: You can apply different filter values to each subscription so that different users receive tailored reports. Here is how to set filter values for a subscription: Locate the Set filter values for when this gets sent section. 3.Enter the filter values needed for this subscription. You can set values for each filter on the dashboard. If you have any dashboard filters with default values, you can override those defaults for a given subscription, or leave them as-is. This method allows you to maintain one dashboard while delivering personalized reports to different users. Attach results include dashboard data as a downloadable file. You can choose between the following file formats:

The attached files will include up to 2000 rows by default. To change this row limit on your Advanced Analytics Cloud instance, you can contact us and request a different row limit. How to add multiple subscriptions to a dashboard? Click on the ➕ (plus) icon to add a new subscription. Select the subscription you want to remove. Resolution path: Edit the subscription and set the specific filter values you want it to always use, or leave it on the dashboard's defaults if that's the intended behavior. This is a configuration choice, not a bug.

chunks.t: How does syncing your Calendar to Recruit CRM work?
chunks.x: Calendar sync in Recruit CRM lets you have all your meetings synced with your Google or Outlook calendar in just three clicks. Click here to learn about integrating your Google/Outlook Calendar When you sync your calendar to Recruit CRM, your meetings will be automatically synced in both Recruit CRM and your calendar. Meetings can be created from three different places within the Recruit CRM app. Click here to learn more about Scheduling Meetings Meetings created in Recruit CRM are automatically added to your connected Google or Microsoft Outlook calendar and vice versa. Any updates made to meetings sync both ways between Recruit CRM and your calendar. ​

chunks.t: How does syncing your Calendar to Recruit CRM work?
chunks.x: When you are viewing a candidate or contact details page, Recruit CRM automatically checks for new or updated meetings from your connected calendar. The sync runs every 15 minutes , and once completed, the latest meeting details are updated on the candidate/contact profile as well as the Meetings list page . ​ Deleting a meeting does not sync across platforms. If you delete a meeting in Recruit CRM, it will remain in your calendar, and if you delete it from your calendar, it will remain in Recruit CRM. Please note that deleting a recurring meeting from your calendar will not remove it from Recruit CRM. You will need to delete it manually in Recruit CRM.

chunks.t: How does syncing your Calendar to Recruit CRM work?
chunks.x: Tasks do not sync between Recruit CRM and your calendar. Any task created in either platform will remain available only in the platform where it was created. Click here to learn about Tasks and Meetings Problem: A meeting created in Recruit CRM is not showing in Google or Outlook. Likely cause: Calendar sync is not properly connected. What to check: Confirm your Google or Outlook calendar is connected in Recruit CRM and that sync is active. Resolution path: Reconnect your calendar, then create a new test meeting in Recruit CRM to verify it reflects in your calendar. 1. Does Recruit CRM sync both meetings and tasks with my calendar?

chunks.t: How does syncing your Calendar to Recruit CRM work?
chunks.x: No. Only meetings sync. Tasks created on your calendar won't be synced to Recruit CRM, and tasks created on Recruit CRM won't be synced to your calendar. Calendar sync in Recruit CRM helps you keep meetings aligned between Recruit CRM and your Google or Outlook calendar. By understanding how meetings, recurring events, and tasks behave with sync, you can manage your schedule across both systems. chunks.t: Entity Type Custom Fields
chunks.x: Custom Entity-Type Fields empower recruiters to tailor their CRM and ATS to fit their unique workflows by linking key records like Candidates, Jobs, Contacts, Companies, Deals, Users, and Teams. These fields streamline data management, boost visibility across connected entities, and enhance automation and reporting capabilities across platforms. This feature brings the flexibility of creating multi-select searchable fields that connect entities, ensuring data integrity, consistency, and a major productivity boost — especially when used with automation tools like API, Zapier, and Webhooks. ​ 🧩 How to create an Entity Type Custom Field

chunks.t: Entity Type Custom Fields
chunks.x: You can create and manage custom fields linking to Candidates, Contacts, Companies, Jobs, Deals, Users, and Teams. Please note that this is supported on Candidates, Jobs, Contacts, Companies, and Deals. 1. Go to Admin Settings and refer to the section 'Data Customization'. Select Candidate, Company, Contact, Deal or Job Fields: 2. Now, click on 'New Custom Field', name your field, and then on 'Field Type', choose between Candidates, Contacts, Companies, Jobs, Deals, Users, and Teams. 3. There you go! You have created your field and now can see it on the record type selected. You can also add those fields to the Profile View: Why are these fields only multi-select and not single-select?

chunks.t: Entity Type Custom Fields
chunks.x: Multi-select ensures users can associate multiple related records (e.g., multiple candidates to a job) for richer data linking and flexibility. For User and Team fields, profile viewing is restricted for privacy and security. Clicking is disabled to avoid exposing sensitive team/user info. Can I search records I don’t have access to? No, if you don't have access to view a record, you won't be able to search it. Why can’t I use placeholders with these fields? Placeholder support is intentionally excluded since entity fields are structured references rather than free-text entries. What happens if an imported value doesn't match any record?

chunks.t: Entity Type Custom Fields
chunks.x: The field is skipped to maintain data accuracy. You must ensure correct slugs, email IDs, or team names are used. Why aren’t these fields supported on the Talent Pool or Job Application settings? These fields are meant to track internal data and are ideally not to be exposed. chunks.t: Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields for Jobs
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? When you create or edit a job with the Contract or Contract-to-Permanent job type, Recruit CRM automatically displays the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields. These fields help you track contractor pay and client billing rates for contract staffing. You can choose to calculate the Bill Rate using a Fixed Rate, Margin, or Markup . Require pay and bill rates for contract jobs. Filter, import, and export jobs using these fields. Before using these fields, it's helpful to understand what each one represents. Pay Rate: The amount paid to the contractor. Bill Rate: The amount billed to your client. Margin: The percentage of the Bill Rate that represents profit.

chunks.t: Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields for Jobs
chunks.x: Markup: The percentage added to the Pay Rate to calculate the Bill Rate. Calculate Charge By: Determines whether the Bill Rate is calculated using a Fixed Rate, Margin, or Markup. ​ Markup is the percentage added to the Pay Rate to calculate the Bill Rate. For example, a $10 Pay Rate with a 50% markup results in a $15 Bill Rate. The value can be between 0% and 99% and cannot be a negative value. Margin represents the percentage of the Bill Rate that is profit. For example, a $10 Pay Rate with a 50% margin requires a $20 Bill Rate. The value can be between 0% and 10,000% and cannot be a negative value.

chunks.t: Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields for Jobs
chunks.x: Please note: These fields are conditional and only appear when the Job Type is set to Contract or Contract-to-Permanent. How to use the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields Create a new job or edit an existing one, then set the Job Type to Contract or Contract-to-Permanent. The Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields will automatically appear on the job form. ​ Select how the Bill Rate should be calculated: Fixed Rate: Enter the Pay Rate and Bill Rate directly. Margin: Enter the desired profit margin, and the system automatically calculates the Bill Rate. Markup: Enter the desired markup on the Pay Rate, and the system automatically calculates the Bill Rate.

chunks.t: Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields for Jobs
chunks.x: Admins can control the visibility of Pay Rate, Bill Rate, Margin, Markup, and Calculate Charge By navigating to Admin Settings → Data Customization → Job Fields . From here you can mark them as Required to ensure they are completed whenever applicable. Note: Existing jobs will continue to use Fixed Rate , so existing rate configurations are not changed. If Pay Rate and Bill Rate already exist, the corresponding Margin and Markup values can be calculated automatically. Where can you access the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields? Once available, the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields can be accessed throughout Recruit CRM. View the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields directly from the Jobs List Page .

Markup is the percentage added to the Pay Rate to calculate the Bill Rate. For example, a $10 Pay Rate with a 50% markup results in a $15 Bill Rate. Margin represents the percentage of the Bill Rate that is profit. For example, a $10 Pay Rate with a 50% margin requires a $20 Bill Rate. No. Existing jobs will continue to use Fixed Rate .
