chunks.t: LinkedIn Sequencing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You can send a series of scheduled LinkedIn messages to candidates and contacts using LinkedIn Sequences. This helps your team stay in touch with prospects automatically, leading to better response rates and a smoother recruitment process. To use LinkedIn steps in sequences, you'll first need to purchase the LinkedIn Messages Integration from your Plans & Billing section. LinkedIn Messages Integration is an Enterprise plan feature which can also be added at an additional cost to Pro or Business plan subscriptions. ​ Once the feature is active, LinkedIn Integration will be enabled on your account. ​ Make sure your LinkedIn account is connected here to start using LinkedIn Sequences.

chunks.t: LinkedIn Sequencing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Click here to learn more about the LinkedIn Messages Integration 1. Go to Admin Settings > CRM Process Customization > Sequences . 3. Select either "Candidates" or "Contacts" as the recipient of the sequence. 4. The next step is to name your sequence and select the LinkedIn step that needs to be executed. You can choose to either select an existing Message template or create a new one dedicated to the sequence. You can create a LinkedIn-only sequence or mix task steps with email steps and SMS steps as well, as long as you respect the limit of 40 steps in total (10 each). 5. Then, specify the number of days and the time when the sequence step should be executed.

chunks.t: LinkedIn Sequencing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: It is important to know exactly when the LinkedIn message will be sent in relation to the starting date of the sequence. To calculate this, you can use the following formula: Send Date = Start Date + Specified No. Of Days (Send SMS In) Here, "Start Date" represents the date when the sequence was initiated. "Specified Date" or "Send SMS In" is the number of days you have indicated for the message to be sent after the start of the sequence. The resulting "Send date" is the calculated date on which the message will be sent. For example : If you start the sequence on January 1st and specify that the SMS should be sent in 2 days, the Send Date would be calculated as follows:

chunks.t: LinkedIn Sequencing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Send date= January 1st + 2 days =January 3rd. You can also set the " Send Message In " days count as 0, establishing the beginning of your sequence in Day 0 . This way, the first message will be sent on the same day you enroll prospects into a sequence. 6. Add steps to the sequence as required, up to a maximum of 40 steps , which includes a maximum of 10 LinkedIn steps, 10 email steps, 10 SMS steps and 10 task steps . You can easily rearrange the sequence steps by using the drag-and-drop functionality. 7. Set a specific number of days for each step to execute, with a range of 1 to 250 calendar days or business days.

chunks.t: LinkedIn Sequencing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Tasks can be created on the same day as the sequence initiation by setting the day as "0". ​ When implementing a task on the 0th day, it's crucial to align the step timing with the previous steps or set it for a later time than the preceding step to ensure a seamless workflow. Criteria for enrolling prospects into LinkedIn Sequences 1. You must be connected on LinkedIn If you're not already connected with the prospect on LinkedIn, you'll need to send them a connection request manually first. 2. LinkedIn URL is required Make sure each prospect’s profile in Recruit CRM has their LinkedIn profile link added.

chunks.t: LinkedIn Sequencing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 3. Different LinkedIn URLs for prospect and sender The LinkedIn URL added for the prospect must not be the same as the one connected for your user account. This is to ensure the system correctly identifies the sender and receiver. 4. LinkedIn Conversation Must Be Initiated Manually First You should initiate the conversation on LinkedIn by clicking the LinkedIn tab on the prospect’s details page. This will fetch the prospect’s profile and connection status. Once this is done, you can proceed to enroll them. This step helps prevent your LinkedIn account from being temporarily blocked due to API rate limits. 1. Start by bulk selecting the prospects you want to enroll and click on Enroll.

chunks.t: LinkedIn Sequencing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 2. Then select the sequence you want to enroll them in, these could include Email , Tasks , SMS or LinkedIn steps . 3. Once they have made their selection, the system will automatically check if each selected prospect meets the necessary requirements for that sequence (like having an email ID, LinkedIn URL, etc.). Only the prospects who pass all the checks will be enrolled into the sequence. If your sequence includes LinkedIn and SMS, the system checks for A2P 10DLC (US), KYC (UK), and SMS consent before sending.

chunks.t: LinkedIn Sequencing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: If a prospect replies to your LinkedIn message, they won’t be automatically unenrolled from the LinkedIn Sequence due to technical limitations. You’ll need to manually unenroll them from the sequence. If your LinkedIn account gets disconnected from Recruit CRM, any active LinkedIn Sequences will be paused automatically . If your LinkedIn Add-On expires and you try to enroll prospects in a sequence, the system will ask you to renew the LinkedIn Integration first. If you have Recruit CRM open in two tabs, and you change the LinkedIn URL from the candidate details page in one tab, you’ll need to: Close the validation popup in the other tab

chunks.t: LinkedIn Sequencing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: This ensures the system picks up the updated LinkedIn URL. 5. Limitations in LinkedIn Sequence Analytics In LinkedIn sequencing, metrics like 'Open rate,' 'Reply rate,' and 'Unsubscribe rate' cannot be tracked. That's it, I hope this helps. Happy recruiting :) Task Sequencing in Recruit CRM: How to Create and Use Task Sequences

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Pay and Bill Rule Templates allow you to standardize how contractor working hours, overtime, breaks, pay, and billing amounts are calculated in Recruit CRM. You can create reusable templates by defining a work schedule, choosing how breaks are handled, setting the treatment of additional hours, and adding custom rules based on shifts or working hours. Standardize pay and bill calculations across contractors. Configure unpaid break hours that are automatically deducted from working hours. Configure overtime, shift-based, and time-range rules. Apply multipliers or fixed pay and bill rates.

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: Create reusable templates for different contractor work schedules. Reduce manual calculations and maintain consistency across timesheets. Please note: This feature is currently available in Beta and can be enabled upon request. Please contact your Account Manager to have it enabled for your account. Who can manage Pay and Bill Rule Templates? Account Owners , Admins , and users with custom roles that have access to Pay and Bill Templates can access Pay and Bill Template Settings . Users with Team Member and Restricted Team Member roles cannot access these settings. How to create a Pay and Bill Rule Template? Navigate to Admin Settings → Pay and Bill Settings → Pay and Bill Rule Template .

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: Under Work Schedule , enter a name for the template and select the method you want to use for defining the contractor's work schedule. Choose one of the following methods to configure the contractor's work schedule. Select at least one working day and define the Start Time and End Time for each day. Unselected days are treated as days off. You can use Copy to All to apply the first day's schedule to all working days. The configured schedule is treated as Regular Hours and calculated at the standard 1× rate.

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: Please note: The Start Time and End Time must be different, and 00:00 cannot be used as the End Time. To represent the end of the day, use 24:00 (or 12:00 AM in 12-hour format) instead of 23:59 (or 11:59 PM). Select the working days and enter the number of working hours for each day. You can use Copy to All to apply the first day's hours to all working days. Please note: You can enter up to 24 working hours per day, and the working hours cannot be 0. Use Unpaid break hours per day to define the break duration deducted from scheduled hours when calculating actual payable working hours and overtime thresholds. Please note: The break duration cannot exceed the scheduled working hours for a day.

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: Example: If the work schedule is 9:00 AM–5:30 PM with a 30-minute excluded break , the actual working hours are 8 hours . If the contractor logs 9:00 AM–6:00 PM , the system calculates 1 hour of overtime . Please note: Overtime hours are displayed only when a custom overtime rule is configured. Use the Round time entries automatically toggle in the Rule Template to automatically round time entries based on a selected interval. You can choose from the following rounding intervals: You can also choose how the time entries should be rounded: Round Up: Rounds the time entry up to the next selected interval. Round Down: Rounds the time entry down to the previous selected interval.

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: Nearest Interval: Rounds the time entry to whichever selected interval is closest. For example, if the selected interval is 15 minutes : With Round Down , 8:14 is rounded to 8:00. With Nearest Interval , 8:04 is rounded to 8:00, while 8:06 is rounded to 8:15. For bulk entries, rounding is applied according to each contractor's individual timesheet settings. If contractors have different rounding configurations, each entry is rounded according to the settings configured for that contractor. Configure the standard rate for extra hours Use the Apply standard rate (1X) for extra hours toggle to control how hours outside the defined work schedule or custom rules are handled.

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: Enabled: Extra hours are paid and billed at the standard 1× rate . Disabled: Only hours covered by the work schedule or custom rules are considered for pay and bill calculations. Any additional hours are not payable or billable. Custom rules allow you to configure shift-based, overtime, and time-based pay and bill calculations. Enter a name for the rule, select the applicable days, choose the Rule Type , and configure the required time range or threshold. The working days configured in the Work Schedule are selected by default. Define the pay and bill rates using either a Multiplier or a Fixed Rate . Fixed rates use the currency configured in the Timesheet Settings .

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: Please note: The same time range cannot be applied to multiple rules on the same day. If logged time falls outside all configured rules, the Apply standard rate (1X) for extra hours setting determines whether those hours are paid and billed. You can click the Delete icon to remove a rule or Add Rule to create additional rules. You can apply a "Before Shift" rule on selected days, specifying a time range that occurs before the regular shift start time. ‘Before shift’ for the same day cannot be applied twice. A Before Shift rule cannot start at 00:00, as it is considered an invalid start time for this rule type.

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: You can apply an "After Shift" rule on selected days, specifying a time range that occurs after the regular shift start time. This is applicable only if the method is set to "Shift." ‘After shift’ for the same day cannot be applied twice. The After shift rule cannot start at 00:00, as it is considered an invalid start time for this rule type. The Specific Range rule allows you to define a specific time window by specifying a start and end time, and applying a multiplier for that range. This rule can be applied to multiple ranges on the same day.

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: The Daily Overtime rule lets users decide after how many hours overtime should be paid on a given day. The threshold must be equal to or more than the regular working hours defined for that day. For example, if Monday’s regular hours are 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM (8 hours), then the Daily Overtime threshold must be at least 8. If it’s set below 8, the system will show an error. If the total hours worked on that day go beyond this threshold, the extra hours will be paid and billed (given that those hours are not covered by other rules). The Daily Working Hours rule can be applied twice for the same day to support multiple overtime thresholds.

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: The same threshold (e.g., “above 8 hours”) cannot be applied more than once. Each rule must define a unique threshold. The Weekly Overtime rule applies to all days in the week and is only available for weekly and biweekly timesheets. You can set a weekly threshold (e.g., 40 hours). If the total hours worked in a week go beyond this threshold, the extra hours will be counted as overtime (given those hours are not covered by other rules). The threshold must be equal to or more than the total regular hours in that week.

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: Monday to Thursday: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM (8 hours/day) Friday: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM (7 hours) Then your total regular hours = (4 × 8) + (1 × 7) = 39 hours So, the weekly overtime threshold must be at least 39 hours . You cannot set the threshold lower than the total regular hours for the week. Breaks are excluded, they are subtracted from the working hours. This means the break duration will not be considered for pay or bill calculations. Breaks are always deducted from the time slot entered on the timesheet. ​ Example: In this case, the 1-hour break will be deducted from the regular hours (9:00 AM to 5:00 PM), not the after-shift time. So the system will calculate:

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: Regular Time: 7 hours (after removing 1-hour break) The Daily Overtime functionality will work the same as the Shift Rule. The minimum hours, overtime multipliers, and all other related functionality will remain consistent with the shift rule behavior. The Weekly Overtime functionality will work the same as the Shift Rule. The minimum hours, overtime multipliers, and all other related functionality will remain consistent with the shift rule behavior. As breaks are excluded, the break hours will be subtracted from the work hours

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: Note: When rules are applied, the Specific Range rule is applied first, followed by Daily Overtime, and finally Weekly Overtime for calculations in the Start and End method. For the Working Hours method, Daily Overtime is applied first, followed by Weekly Overtime. Weekly overtime rules do not apply to monthly timesheets. If a contractor is on a monthly frequency, the weekly overtime rule will not be applied. How to edit, clone, delete, or set a default Pay and Bill Rule Template? Click the three-dot menu under the Action column of the required template to manage it.

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: Edit: Update an existing template. Changes made to the template don't affect candidates who already have a copy of that template applied. Clone: Create an exact copy of the template's current configuration. You can modify the cloned template and save it as a new template. Delete: Delete the template from Pay and Bill Template Settings. Candidates who already have the template applied will retain their copy in their Timesheet Settings. Set as Default: Set a template as the default option when enabling timesheets. You can change the default template or clear the default selection whenever needed. Problem: I can't configure a Weekly Overtime rule.

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: Likely Cause: The timesheet frequency is Monthly, a Weekly Overtime rule already exists, or the configured threshold is below the total regular working hours. What to Check: Review the timesheet frequency, existing rules, and weekly threshold. Resolution: Use Weekly or Biweekly frequency, configure only one Weekly Overtime rule, and set the threshold equal to or greater than the total regular working hours. 1. What is the difference between the two Work Schedule methods? The Work Start and End Time method defines specific shift start and end times, while the Enter Work Hours method defines the total number of working hours expected for each day.

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: 2. Can I configure more than one Daily Overtime rule? Yes. You can configure up to two Daily Overtime rules for the same day, provided each rule uses a unique overtime threshold. 3. What happens when I edit a template that's already applied to a candidate? Changes made to the original template don't affect candidates who already have a copy of the template applied. 4. What happens when I delete an applied template? The template is deleted from the Pay and Bill Template Settings, but candidates who already have the template applied retain their copy in Timesheet Settings. 5. Do Weekly Overtime rules apply to Monthly timesheets?

chunks.t: Timesheets - Create Pay and Bill Rule templates with work schedule and custom rules (Beta)
chunks.x: No. Weekly Overtime rules are available only for Weekly and Biweekly timesheets. Pay and Bill Rule Templates help standardize contractor pay and billing calculations by allowing you to configure work schedules, break calculations, additional hours, overtime thresholds, multipliers, and fixed rates. By creating reusable templates, you can reduce manual calculations, maintain consistent rules across contractors, and manage complex contract staffing workflows more efficiently. chunks.t: Candidate Source Tracking in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: The Candidate Source Tracking feature automatically captures where each applicant applied from, whether it’s from LinkedIn, job boards, or your website. This allows for smarter and more informed sourcing decisions based on data. The source is recorded automatically during the application or sign-up process. To track where your candidates are coming from, you can manually add the ?source= tag at the end of your job application or Candidate Portal links. In this case, “Promotion” will be recorded as the candidate’s source.

chunks.t: Candidate Source Tracking in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: You can customize the value to match any platform you're using, like Facebook , EmailCampaign , CareersPage , or even a recruiter’s name. Just make sure the value is clear and easy to identify. This method is especially useful when sharing job links across multiple channels, so you can track which ones bring in the most candidates. Tracks the candidate's source using the ?source= parameter in the job application and Candidate Portal sign-up links. If the ?source= parameter is missing, the system uses the browser’s referrer (the previous webpage the user was on) to identify the source.

chunks.t: Candidate Source Tracking in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: Referrer domains like linkedin.com or indeed.com are automatically mapped to user-friendly names like “LinkedIn” or “Indeed.” The source is saved in the "Source" field of each candidate’s profile, which is very useful for filtering and reporting. Depending on how the candidate enters, the source is tagged as either: From a job application: Apply Page – [SourceName] From the Candidate Portal: Candidate Portal – [SourceName] Once the source is recorded, it won’t change—even if the candidate returns through a different link. What if a candidate uses a link without ?source= and there’s no browser referrer? The system will still tag the context as "Apply Page" or "Candidate Portal."

chunks.t: Candidate Source Tracking in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: No. The source is captured only once during the first visit and remains unchanged. Why use both URL parameters and referrer data? URL parameters provide more accurate tracking, especially for campaigns. Referrer data acts as a reliable backup. What if the referrer is blocked or unavailable? The system will still log the context (Apply Page or Candidate Portal), even without the source name. Will the source be retained across multi-page forms? Yes. The system preserves the source throughout the entire session. Track the Source of Applicants from Multiple Platforms Using the Job Application URL/Talent Pool Page.

You can link Contract and Contract to Permanent jobs to Deals, automatically associate placed candidates, enable timesheets, and manage timesheet activities directly from the Deal. Track contract placements and associated contractors in one place. Link Contract or Contract to Permanent jobs with Deals. Automatically associate placed candidates with a Deal. Build and save unlimited personalized email templates for faster communication. Audit Logs Track all user activities for the past 30 days, including action types and timestamps. LinkedIn Messages Integration View and respond to LinkedIn messages within Recruit CRM. How do record limits compare between Pro Plan and Business Plan?

chunks.t: Pro Plan vs Business Plan
chunks.x: In the Pro Plan, record limits are 10,000 candidates per user, 10,000 contacts per user, and 10,000 companies per user. In the Business Plan, these limits are 20,000 candidates per user, 20,000 contacts per user, and 20,000 companies per user. Which plan should I choose for advanced automation and integrations? Choose the Business Plan if you need sequences for automated outreach, API access for custom integrations and workflows, and job board integrations like LogicMelon and Broadbean. The Pro Plan does not include these advanced automation and integration features. Which plan is better for security and access control?

chunks.t: Pro Plan vs Business Plan
chunks.x: The Business Plan is better for advanced security and access control. It includes whitelist IPs, single sign-on (SSO) via providers like Google, Microsoft Azure, or Okta, audit logs for the past 30 days, and custom roles and teams to control user access. The Pro Plan includes two-factor or multi-factor authentication but does not include IP whitelisting, SSO, audit logs, or custom roles and teams.

chunks.t: Pro Plan vs Business Plan
chunks.x: Choosing between the Pro Plan and Business Plan in Recruit CRM comes down to your agency’s scale, security needs, customization requirements, and client-facing expectations. Use this comparison to match your current and future workflows to the right plan, and adjust as your team and data volumes grow.

chunks.t: Customizable Job Application URL
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? With this Custom Job Application Form URL feature, you can define a custom domain and URL pattern for job application forms, perfect for seamless branding and candidate experience. The custom URL replaces the default Recruit CRM job application form URL across multiple touchpoints, ensuring consistency and professionalism. ​ This feature is particularly helpful for users using Recruit Craft, custom APIs for career pages/site, and for directing applicants via job boards and XML feeds. Note: Only the Account Owner, Admins, and users with custom permissions can set up the custom URL. Choosing the Right URL Based on Your Setup

chunks.t: Customizable Job Application URL
chunks.x: Depending on how your organization hosts job pages: For this feature to work accurately, you need to use our API-built or RecruitCraft-powered pages under your company domain as the base URL. If you have integrated Recruit CRM’s job listings using an iframe on your website, this feature will not apply directly. If your company has built a custom career site using the Recruit CRM API , you can use that URL here. These pages are considered part of your own domain and fully support job slugs. Example: https://careers.yourcompany.com/ ​ ❌ Do not use any Recruit CRM hosted links , for example: https://jobs.recruitcrm.io/job/software-engineer https://yourcompany.recruitcrm.io/job/...

chunks.t: Customizable Job Application URL
chunks.x: These URLs are generated by Recruit CRM’s own hosting service and cannot be reused as custom URLs. Users who don’t have their own API-based job listings site cannot use this feature. Once set, the custom URL will replace Recruit CRM’s default link in: Job boards such as Broadbean, CV Library, and TotalJobs API endpoints like Find Job by Slug, Search for Jobs, Get Job Application Form, Show All Jobs The "Copy Job Application Form URL" button in the job details page. Note: As of now, this functionality is not available for free job boards. How to set up a Custom Job Application URL? The example in this article demonstrates the setup using a sample site built with RecruitCraft.

chunks.t: Customizable Job Application URL
chunks.x: Know more about integrating RCRM with Recruit Craft 1. Go to Admin Settings . Under Job Settings click on Public Job Page Settings ​ 2. Open the Job Page Integration section scroll down to Custom Job Application URLs and toggle the setting ON ​ 3. In the Configure Custom Branded URL field, enter your company’s base career site link for example in this case: https://recruitcraft.io/site/product ​ Recruit CRM will automatically append each job’s slug to this path. (You don’t need to type {job_slug} manually.) ​ The system immediately shows an example job URL below using the latest updated job’s data, confirming how it will appear for candidates. ​

chunks.t: Customizable Job Application URL
chunks.x: 4. You can turn on the "Append a job field to the end of the URL" option to add one more job field as a placeholder (only text or dropdown fields are supported). Note: You can append the job field only if you have the same appended field in your base job application form URL on your careers page. This is a global setting that applies to all jobs in your account. ​ {job_slug} will be added mandatorily in the job application link once you configure it and only one additional job field can be added. A slug is a unique identifier for an entity in Recruit CRM, found in the URL after the last “/” on its profile page. ​

chunks.t: Customizable Job Application URL
chunks.x: Spaces in placeholder values will be converted to hyphens (for example Marketing Manager becomes Marketing-Manager). ​ When you turn the toggle off, the system will revert to using Recruit CRM’s default application links, but your previous domain and configuration will be saved in case you toggle it back on. ​ The system checks for correct URL format before saving. ​ Recruit CRM does not validate the authenticity or correctness of the custom URL entered by the user.

chunks.t: Customizable Job Application URL
chunks.x: 6. Once the toggle is enabled and a URL is configured, the system will automatically replace Recruit CRM’s default job application form URL with the custom URL across all applicable locations, regardless of whether the target URL leads to a valid destination or contains a valid job. ​ It is entirely the user's responsibility to ensure the configured URL is functional, secure, and aligned with their job application URL flow. ​ Error Message for Incorrect Custom Job Application URL If the URL entered in the custom job application field is incorrect, candidates will see a "404 error: This page could not be found" when they try to open the job application form. ​

chunks.t: Customizable Job Application URL
chunks.x: Turn the Custom Job Application Form URL toggle OFF to immediately go back to Recruit CRM’s default job application links. ​ What happens if I don’t configure a custom URL? No, currently only one additional job field (text or dropdown) can be used with the required {job_slug}. Can I add more than one additional placeholder in the URL? No, currently only one additional job field (text or dropdown) can be used with the required {job_slug}. Does the feature work for jobs accessed via APIs or XML feeds? Yes, once configured, the custom URL will reflect across all supported APIs and feeds. Can I set different URLs for different jobs?

chunks.t: Customizable Job Application URL
chunks.x: No, this is a global setting and applies account-wide to all jobs. What happens if a placeholder field is blank or has spaces? If a field is blank, the URL will still be generated but that portion may be empty. If it contains spaces, they’ll be automatically converted to hyphens (e.g., “Marketing Manager” → “Marketing-Manager”). Does Recruit CRM verify the URL I configure? No. Recruit CRM does not validate or check the availability, correctness, or security of the custom URL you enter. The system assumes the URL is valid and will use it as-is. Make sure your destination page is live, functional, and supports your application process.

chunks.t: Customizable Job Application URL
chunks.x: Can I use this with a career site built using the Recruit CRM API? Yes! You can use any API-built or RecruitCraft-powered page under your company domain as the base URL. The Custom Job Application URL feature helps you provide a consistent and branded application experience by replacing Recruit CRM’s default job links with URLs based on your Recruit Craft-powered or API-based career site. Once configured, the custom URL is automatically used across supported channels, while Recruit CRM handles job slugs and optional job fields based on your settings. chunks.t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Organic Posting Network (OPN) , powered by VONQ , allows you to publish jobs from Recruit CRM to a network of 20+ free job boards through a single XML feed integration. Instead of manually posting jobs to multiple platforms, eligible jobs can be automatically distributed across participating job boards, helping you increase job visibility, reach a broader audience, and attract more candidates with minimal effort.

chunks.t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
chunks.x: Applications received through these job boards are captured directly in Recruit CRM, making it easier to track and manage applicants from a centralised location. Candidates who apply through the Organic Posting Network are identified within Recruit CRM, with the Source field displaying Organic Posting along with the associated job information. • You want to publish jobs to multiple free job boards at the same time. • You want to increase the visibility of your open roles without paying for individual job board postings. Note: 1 Job posting credit or 25 Recruit CRM Credits will be consumed if you post the job through the organic posting network.

chunks.t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
chunks.x: You can buy Job Posting credits on a monthly or annual basis, irrespective of your subscription plan , directly from the job advertising module. Click here to know more about how to purchase credits Here is the list of all the job boards offered under OPN (going further, more job boards will be added): Please note that the job might not get posted on all the job boards mentioned in the list. ​ VONQ does not guarantee the jobs to be posted on all job boards. The jobs will go on selective job boards only based on the parameters defined by the job boards. Example location, industry, specification, etc and filtering the jobs is Vonq’s discretion. ✅ How to get a job posted on the OPN job boards?

chunks.t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
chunks.x: The first step is to make sure all the necessary criteria are met for the jobs to be visible on the XML Feed and posted on the OPN job boards. Before you create a new job in Recruit CRM, please make sure you have ticked the job posting box inside Job Fields in Admin settings . This will help post your open jobs on your website and other job boards. The "Post On Job Boards" option should be selected inside Admin Settings >> Job Custom Fields ; ❌ Please note that if you untick the checkbox, none of your jobs will be posted. The job application form should be enabled. The Updated On date should be within the last 30 days;

chunks.t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
chunks.x: All the fields where you see the message "Required To Post On Partner Job Boards" (City, State, Country, Maximum Salary, Job Description, Currency, Salary Type) and "Required to post on Organic Job Boards" (Postal code, Job Function, Job Industry) need to have a value. You may enter either the full name or just the initials in the required fields (necessary for posting on job boards), as both options are acceptable. As LinkedIn Limited Listings is available as one of the OPN job boards, in order to post jobs on the company's LinkedIn page, the default 'LinkedIn Company ID' field needs to be filled with the LinkedIn company ID. Here is an article on how to find the LinkedIn Company ID.

chunks.t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
chunks.x: 'Note for candidates' should be filled in (only if the Job Description is uploaded as a file); ​ The job status should not be 'closed', 'on hold' or 'cancelled'; ​ Select "Organic Job Boards" under the XML Feeds section ⬇️⬇️⬇️ While creating a new job or editing an existing one, make sure you select "Organic Job Boards" in the XML Feeds section to get your jobs posted on the correct XML Feed. By selecting the appropriate XML feed, you can ensure that your jobs reach the intended audience through the most relevant job boards. You also have the option to preselect the XML feeds in the Build Job Feed XML page. This means the XML Feed will automatically be selected for all new jobs created. ​

chunks.t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
chunks.x: If you don't want a job to be automatically posted on the Free Job Boards XML Feed you can simply disable the preselection on the Build Job Feed XML or uncheck the XML Feed while creating/editing the job: The jobs will be indexed to the external boards only if the requirements given above are met. Once you add details to these fields, the job goes through the review process. If everything is fine, Vonq will publish your jobs on Organic job boards instantly.

chunks.t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
chunks.x: Note: If the "organic job boards" option is selected from the XML fields section, you will be prompted to fill the required fields before you can save the job. This is to ensure your jobs are published through the feed. Please make sure all the required fields are filled in this step is essential for the job to go live. And that's it! You'll start receiving applications for those jobs in Recruit CRM! 1. You can check the list of jobs eligible to be pushed to the free job boards' feed by going to Admin Settings >>> Build Job Feed XML . Here you can click on "View Listed Jobs" to get a list of all the jobs in your account that currently meet the required criteria:

chunks.t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
chunks.x: If one of your jobs is not on the list, one of the necessary criteria is not being met. 2. You can search the job boards' websites to check if the job was posted. When your job is posted on the partner job boards, it will look something like this: The view will vary depending on the job board. 3. Another way to verify if the job was posted or not is to look for applicant candidates in your database. You can do this by enabling the Source field in Candidate Fields : ​ With the Source field, you'll be able to track the origin of how the candidate was added to the system. If the candidate applies, it will be mentioned in the field as 'Organic Posting Network' along with the Job ID. ​

chunks.t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
chunks.x: You can even run an Advanced Search on the Source field as well. Problem: A job is not appearing on any organic job board Likely cause : One or more required criteria for OPN posting have not been met. Verify that all OPN posting requirements outlined above have been met. Confirm the job is assigned to the Organic Job Boards XML Feed. Re-save the job after making any corrections. Correct any missing or invalid field values, set the appropriate job status, re-save the job, and allow time for VONQ to process and publish it. Problem: The job is not visible on a specific job board in the OPN list Likely cause: VONQ’s filtering rules did not match the job to that particular board.

chunks.t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
chunks.x: Confirm that the job is otherwise eligible and visible on at least some other boards. Review whether the job’s location, industry, or specification might not align with that board’s parameters. Adjust job parameters where appropriate (for example, industry or location), then save the job and monitor posting again. Keep in mind that VONQ does not guarantee posting to every job board in the list. Does posting to OPN consume job posting credits?

chunks.t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
chunks.x: Yes. One job posting credit or 25 Recruit CRM Credits is consumed each time you post a job through the Organic Posting Network. Job Posting Credits can be purchased on a monthly or annual basis directly from the Job Advertising module, regardless of your subscription plan. Will my job appear on every job board in the OPN list? No. VONQ does not guarantee posting on all job boards. Jobs are published on selective boards based on parameters defined by each job board, such as location, industry, and specification, and filtering is at VONQ’s discretion. How can I verify if a job posted via OPN is generating candidates?

chunks.t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
chunks.x: Enable the Source field on the Candidate List page and review candidate records. Candidates who applied via Organic Posting will show “Organic Posting” along with the job ID in the Source field, and you can run an advanced search on this field. Using the Organic Posting Network (OPN) in Recruit CRM, you can efficiently publish jobs to multiple free job boards and track resulting candidates directly in your database. chunks.t: Using Direct Apply/Easy Apply while Posting Jobs from Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Direct Apply is a feature offered by some job boards that makes it easier for candidates to apply with just one click . Instead of being redirected to another website, the job board directly shares the applicant’s information with your ATS (Recruit CRM) through a secure webhook. This keeps the process quick and smooth, allowing more candidates to complete their applications. Depending on the Job board, the candidate is stored within both the job board and the ATS. Different job boards may use terms like Easy Apply, Optimised Apply, or Quick Apply, but they all mean the same thing — Direct Apply.

chunks.t: Using Direct Apply/Easy Apply while Posting Jobs from Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Currently, LinkedIn and Naukri support Direct Apply in Recruit CRM. Note: LinkedIn Easy Apply works only for LinkedIn Recruiter accounts . How do I know if a job is posted with Direct Apply or with a redirect link? When reviewing your job posting details (after selecting a contracted job board), you’ll see a field with two options: Link Out → This redirects candidates to another page. What kind of data is shared with Recruit CRM when the job board sends an applicant via Direct Apply? When a candidate applies via Direct Apply, the following details can be sent to Recruit CRM (depending on the job board): Does LinkedIn Easy Apply work with all LinkedIn accounts?

chunks.t: Using Direct Apply/Easy Apply while Posting Jobs from Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Please note, LinkedIn Easy Apply works only for the LinkedIn Recruiter accounts. Direct Apply (also known as Easy Apply, Optimized Apply, or Quick Apply) lets candidates apply to your jobs with just one click while the job board securely shares their information directly with Recruit CRM. This keeps the process quick and smooth, allowing candidates to complete their applications. Feel free to reach out anytime if you have any further questions. chunks.t: Mark Email Conversations as Public/Private
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Public/Private Email feature allows you to control the visibility of individual emails in Recruit CRM. It will be hidden from the Related Emails tab in the Candidate or Contact record. It will not be visible to your team members. You can still access it from your Private Emails folder in your Mailbox. Marking an email as Public makes it visible to your team wherever related emails are displayed in the system. This feature is particularly useful when you need to: Keep sensitive candidate or client email conversations private. Hide specific emails without disabling email sharing for all emails.

chunks.t: Mark Email Conversations as Public/Private
chunks.x: Control which email conversations are visible to your team. By default, this feature is available to Admins and the Account Owner. Business Plan users can also create a custom role and grant permission to users in that role to Make an email conversation private in the related email tab. ​ Only the sender (email owner) can mark their emails as private or public. Select the email(s) you would like to make private by checking the box next to each email. You can also use the checkbox at the top to select all visible emails. The selected emails will be hidden from other team members. They will no longer appear in the Related Emails tab of linked candidate or contact records.

chunks.t: Mark Email Conversations as Public/Private
chunks.x: They will remain visible to you in your mailbox, including the Private Email tab and the All Email section. Additionally, if you'd like to make private emails visible to your team again, simply select the desired emails in your mailbox and click Make Email Public . The emails will then reappear in the Related Emails tab of the associated candidate and contact records. Open the relevant Candidate or Contact profile. Navigate to the Related Emails tab and open the email conversation you want to manage. Click the lock icon in the top-right corner of the email and select Make This Conversation Private .

chunks.t: Mark Email Conversations as Public/Private
chunks.x: Please note: After the conversation is marked as private, the conversation will remain accessible only to you and the email recipients, including anyone added in CC or BCC . To make the conversation visible to your team again, click the lock icon and select Make This Conversation Public . Who can mark an email conversation as private or public? Only the email sender (email owner) can change the visibility of their email conversations by marking them as private or public.

chunks.t: Mark Email Conversations as Public/Private
chunks.x: Using the public/private email controls in Recruit CRM, you can keep sensitive or internal conversations hidden while still collaborating effectively with your team. If you need more help with email visibility, you can reach out to support using the blue chat box at the bottom-right of your Recruit CRM screen. chunks.t: How to Enable Timesheets for Contract Staffing Jobs in Recruit CRM (Beta)
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM's Timesheets feature helps you track, manage, and approve contractors' working hours. Once enabled, contractors can submit timesheets for approval, making payroll and client billing more accurate and efficient. Configure pay rates, bill rates, and approval workflows. Automate pay and bill calculations using rule templates. Process payroll and client billing more accurately. This feature is currently in Beta and can be enabled upon request. Please get in touch with your Account Manager to enable it for your account. Timesheets can only be enabled for Contract and Contract-to-Permanent jobs.

chunks.t: How to Enable Timesheets for Contract Staffing Jobs in Recruit CRM (Beta)
chunks.x: Candidates in the Applied stage cannot have timesheets enabled. How to enable timesheets for an individual candidate 1. Go to Jobs and open a job with the Contract or Contract-to-Permanent job type. 2. Scroll to the Candidate Pipeline and click Enable Timesheet on the candidate's card. 3. In the Enable Timesheet window, enter the required details to configure timesheet tracking for the candidate. Choose whether the contractor is paid and billed Per Hour or Per Day . Per Hour is selected by default. Choose how often timesheets should be submitted: Weekly – The contractor submits a timesheet once every week. Bi-Weekly – The contractor submits a timesheet once every two weeks.

chunks.t: How to Enable Timesheets for Contract Staffing Jobs in Recruit CRM (Beta)
chunks.x: Monthly – The contractor submits a timesheet once every month. You can choose any day from Monday to Sunday if the timesheet frequency is set to weekly or bi-weekly, / select any date of the month if the frequency is set to monthly. Person responsible for reviewing and approving submitted timesheets. The rate paid to the candidate, per hour or per day depending on the selected Rate Type The rate you’ll bill your client per hour of the candidate’s work. When Margin or Markup is selected, the Bill Rate is calculated automatically based on the selected value. Choose how the Bill Rate should be calculated: Fixed Rate, Margin, or Markup .

chunks.t: How to Enable Timesheets for Contract Staffing Jobs in Recruit CRM (Beta)
chunks.x: The desired profit margin used to automatically calculate the Bill Rate. The desired markup on the Pay Rate used to automatically calculate the Bill Rate. Select the contractor's working days. Any day not selected is treated as a day off. Used when creating and managing day-based timesheets. Only applicable when Rate Type is set to Per Day. Per Day timesheets don't use a Pay and Bill Rule Template. Only the Work Schedule shown above applies. If Rate Type is set to Per Hour, continue configuring a Rule Template as described below. Fixed Rate: Enter the Pay Rate and Bill Rate directly.

chunks.t: How to Enable Timesheets for Contract Staffing Jobs in Recruit CRM (Beta)
chunks.x: Margin: Enter the desired profit margin, and Recruit CRM automatically calculates the Bill Rate. The value can be between 0% and 99% and cannot be a negative value. Markup: Enter the desired markup on the Pay Rate, and Recruit CRM automatically calculates the Bill Rate. The value can be between 0% and 10,000% and cannot be a negative value. Please note: The Margin and Markup fields are used based on the option selected under Calculate Charge By . When Fixed Rate is selected, the Pay Rate and Bill Rate can be entered directly. ​ Make Remark Mandatory on Timesheet – Enable this option to require a remark for every time entry logged in a timesheet.

chunks.t: How to Enable Timesheets for Contract Staffing Jobs in Recruit CRM (Beta)
chunks.x: Enable Expense Claim – Enable this option to allow contractors to submit expense claims through the Contractor Portal for reimbursement. Learn How to Manage Contractor Reimbursements If pay and bill rates are already configured for the job, they'll be pre-filled. The previously selected approver, frequency, and start day/date will also be pre-populated and can be updated if needed. Existing jobs will continue to use Fixed Rate , so existing rate configurations will not be changed.

chunks.t: How to Enable Timesheets for Contract Staffing Jobs in Recruit CRM (Beta)
chunks.x: Margin, Markup, and Calculate Charge By are also available in relevant job and timesheet workflows, including the Job Add/Edit form, Job Details, Job List, Timesheet views, exports, filters, APIs, Workato, and Zapier integrations . Rate Type is also available in relevant Job views, filters, exports, imports, and APIs. Changing the Rate Type after timesheets have been created only affects newly created timesheets going forward, existing timesheets keep using the Rate Type they were created with. 3. If you are enabling the timesheet for Per Day Rate Type, then you can next select the working days under the Working Schedule section.

chunks.t: How to Enable Timesheets for Contract Staffing Jobs in Recruit CRM (Beta)
chunks.x: If you are enabling the timesheet for Per Hour Rate Type, click Insert Pay and Bill Template , then select an existing template from the dropdown. You can also click Create New Template directly from the Rule Template dropdown to create a new template without navigating to Admin Settings . This option is available based on your role and permissions. 4. Once selected, review the automatically populated rules. You can modify the template or add custom rules, such as overtime or shift rules, without affecting the original template. 5. Click Enable to activate timesheets for the candidate.

chunks.t: How to Enable Timesheets for Contract Staffing Jobs in Recruit CRM (Beta)
chunks.x: 6. Once enabled, the Timesheet icon next to the candidate turns green , indicating that timesheets are active. How to enable timesheets for multiple candidates 1. Open the required Contract or Contract-to-Permanent job. Scroll to the Candidate Pipeline and click View All Candidates . 2. Select the candidates you want to enable timesheets for. 3. Click Enable Timesheet from the bulk actions menu. 4. Complete the required details, insert a Pay and Bill Template , make any necessary changes, and click Enable . Timesheets can also be enabled through Deals: Learn how to enable and manage timesheets through deals How to verify that timesheets are enabled

chunks.t: How to Enable Timesheets for Contract Staffing Jobs in Recruit CRM (Beta)
chunks.x: Once timesheets are enabled, the Timesheet icon next to the candidate's name turns green, indicating they are active. You can view this icon on the Candidate List page for the job. If it's not visible, enable the Timesheet field from your view settings. If any selected candidates are not eligible for timesheet activation, you will see an error message before proceeding. Candidate is in applied stage – Timesheets can only be enabled for candidates who are not in the applied stage. Timesheet is already enabled – This indicates that a timesheet is already active for the selected candidate. Problem: The Enable Timesheet option isn't available.

chunks.t: How to Enable Timesheets for Contract Staffing Jobs in Recruit CRM (Beta)
chunks.x: Likely Cause: The job isn't configured as a Contract or Contract-to-Permanent job, or the candidate is in the Applied stage. What to Check: Verify the job type and the candidate's current pipeline stage. Resolution: Update the job type if required and move the candidate beyond the Applied stage before enabling timesheets. What is the difference between Margin and Markup? Markup is the percentage added to the Pay Rate to calculate the Bill Rate. For example, a $10 Pay Rate with a 50% markup results in a $15 Bill Rate . Margin represents the percentage of the Bill Rate that is profit. For example, a $10 Pay Rate with a 50% margin requires a $20 Bill Rate .

chunks.x: The Timesheets feature makes it easy to manage contractor time tracking by enabling timesheets individually or in bulk, configuring approval workflows, and automating pay and billing calculations through reusable rule templates. chunks.t: Pricing and Billing in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: 💸 How Billing and Pricing work in Recruit Craft Recruit Craft’s pricing is designed to be simple and flexible, so you only pay for what you need. Plans are based on the maximum number of jobs you can post on your website through Recruit Craft. The plans will be automatically updated to match your current increased job posting needs. This ensures you’ll always be on a plan that supports the number of jobs you want to display, providing a smooth experience without interruptions.

chunks.t: Pricing and Billing in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: When you first sign up for Recruit Craft, you’re automatically placed on a free trial account . With the free plan, you can connect your Recruit CRM account using your API key and preview your jobs in real time. The preview gives you a clear view of exactly how your jobs will appear once published, helping you set everything up just the way you want before going live. When you’re ready to post jobs publicly, upgrading is quick and effortless. Now, follow along to upgrade your plan from the Free plan. 1. Look to the top right corner of your screen and click Upgrade Now . You can also click your profile icon , go to Settings , and select Plans and Billing from the left-hand panel.

chunks.t: Pricing and Billing in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: 2. You’ll now see a list of plans tailored to your needs. The options will automatically adjust based on the number of open jobs in your Recruit CRM account. For example, if you have 20 open jobs, only plans that support 20 or more jobs will be shown. You can also switch between Annual and Monthly billing at the top of the page, depending on your preference. 3. Choose the plan that works best for your hiring needs and click Get Started . 4. A summary page will display all the choices you’ve made. If needed, you can still adjust the plan from the dropdown menu before moving forward. 5. Once you’ve confirmed everything looks correct, click Proceed to Purchase.

chunks.t: Pricing and Billing in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: 6. The system will ask you to check your details one final time. When you’re ready, click Confirm and Pay . The payment will be processed through the card on file that’s registered in your Recruit CRM account. 7. The charge will be processed through your Recruit CRM Stripe account. ⚠️ Important: If your Recruit CRM account is currently on the FREE plan , you’ll need to upgrade your Recruit CRM account first before completing the Recruit Craft upgrade.

chunks.t: Pricing and Billing in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: Recruit Craft uses a dynamic billing system that adjusts plans based on how many jobs you have published. This ensures that your plan always aligns with your usage, without interrupting your hiring process. Additionally, you’ll receive email notifications whenever your job limit is crossed, keeping you informed and alert so you can take timely action. Automatic Upgrade If your job count exceeds the limit of your current plan for two consecutive days , Recruit Craft will automatically upgrade you to the next available tier .

chunks.t: Pricing and Billing in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: Proration of Fees – You won’t be billed the full amount for the new plan immediately. Instead, Recruit Craft calculates a prorated fee based on the number of days left in your billing cycle. This charge begins from the day your job count exceeds your plan’s limit. Invoice Update – The prorated charge is added to your card on file, and you’ll see this adjustment reflected in your next invoice.

chunks.t: Pricing and Billing in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: Example of Automatic Upgrade Imagine you are on the 6 to 15 Jobs plan and have 15 jobs published. If you publish a 16th job and maintain 16 jobs for two days in a row, the system will automatically upgrade you to the 16 to 50 Jobs plan. You will only be charged the prorated amount for the remaining days of your billing cycle at the new plan rate. Manual Upgrade Option If you prefer, you can manually upgrade your account at any time by following the same steps outlined for upgrading from a free trial. Just head to your profile, go to Settings , select Plans and Billing , and choose the new plan that suits your needs.

chunks.t: Pricing and Billing in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: If your hiring needs change and you’re managing fewer jobs, Recruit Craft gives you the flexibility to downgrade your plan to something more suitable. 1. Click on your profile icon in the top right corner of your screen and go to Settings . 2. Once inside the Profile Settings, navigate to the left-hand panel, and select Plans and Billing . 3. You’ll now be able to see your current plan along with other plans you can move to. If the plan you want is available, simply click Get Started on that option.

chunks.t: Pricing and Billing in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: You can only downgrade if your open jobs are less than the limit of the plan you’re moving to. If your published or open jobs are more than that limit, the option to downgrade will be greyed out. The job count must also be below the starting limit of your current plan at the time of the request, if it’s equal to or higher, the downgrade won’t go through. For example: If you’re on the 16 to 50 Jobs plan and your job count drops to 13, you can request a downgrade to the 6 to 15 Jobs plan. Once validated, the downgrade will take effect at the start of the next billing cycle . 4. After selecting your new plan, review the details and note the effective date. Click Proceed to Purchase to continue.

chunks.t: Pricing and Billing in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: 5. Review everything carefully and click Confirm Downgrade. You’ve now successfully downgraded your account! The new plan will take effect from the start of your next billing cycle, whether you’re on a monthly or annual subscription. Once a downgrade has been initiated, if your job count increases beyond the limit of the selected downgraded plan, the downgrade will automatically be cancelled. Recruit Craft’s pricing and billing system is designed to keep things simple and flexible, so you can focus on hiring while we handle the details. Whether you’re upgrading, downgrading, or just exploring your options, the process is straightforward and transparent.

chunks.t: Pricing and Billing in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: If you ever have questions or need a little extra guidance, don’t hesitate to reach out to our chat support team. We’re always here to help you every step of the way! chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? AI Sourcing helps you find new candidates from Recruit CRM's Global Database , which contains 800 million+ external candidate profiles. You can search this database using either a natural-language description or manually selected search filters, without requiring the candidates to already exist in your Recruit CRM database.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Recruit CRM first narrows the Global Database using Search Filters and then, for AI Search, evaluates and ranks the resulting candidates using AI-generated Matching Criteria. This allows you to either describe the candidates you need in natural language or start from a Job Description and let Recruit CRM generate the search requirements for you. You can use this feature when you want to: Find candidates who are not already in your database. Get an AI-ranked shortlist based on a natural-language description. Quickly find a list of candidates using specific filters. Search a large external candidate pool instead of only your existing records.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You can start an AI Sourcing search in several ways: - Natural-language-based AI Search : Describe the type of candidate you are looking for in plain language. - Job-based Search : Select a recent job and use its Job Description as the basis for the search. - Filter Search : Manually configure search filters to find candidates from the Global Database without AI ranking. The AI search feature within AI Sourcing allows you to describe the type of candidate you are looking for using a plain-language description. Recruit CRM uses the information in your query to create relevant search filters and rank the resulting candidates.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Go to the Candidates list page and click on the AI Sourcing button at the top. In the Search tab, describe the type of candidate you are looking for using natural language. Include details such as the job title, skills, experience, location, and any other requirements that are important for the role. ​ You can also start the search using the Job Description from a recent job . Select a recent job to use its Job Description as the basis for the search. Recruit CRM will extract relevant Search Filters and Matching Criteria from the description. When you start an AI Sourcing search from a Job, Recruit CRM uses the job description from the selected job to generate the search requirements.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: The job-selection screen displays your most recently added jobs, and you can search for additional jobs by job name, company name, city, or Job ID. Only jobs you have permission to view are available for selection. Please note: The jobs that are on the 'Closed' job status will not be visible for selection. If the selected job does not have a Job Description, you will be prompted to add one before continuing.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Review the AI Clarifying Questions displayed after you enter your search. Recruit CRM uses these questions to identify missing or ambiguous information that could affect the search results. For example, it may ask you to clarify an experience range, location, or another requirement. Clarifying the requirement helps produce more relevant results. You can select from the available answers, provide additional information where applicable, or skip the questions if you do not want to provide the suggested information. ​ Click Continue to proceed to the Search Filters and Matching Criteria.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Review the Search Filters and Matching Criteria to see the parameters Recruit CRM will use to search and evaluate candidates. To make changes to the search filters, click Edit Filters . The Filters panel will open on the right, where you can configure filters such as Employment Information, Skills and Keywords, Location, and Education . You can also add other filters based on your requirements using the option at the bottom of the panel. For Job Title and Company , you can enable the Current Only toggle to limit the search to candidates whose current job title or company matches the selected criteria. Once these filters are configured, click on Save.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Next, review the Matching Criteria generated from your query. These criteria help evaluate and rank candidates based on how well their profiles match the requirements of the role. Each criterion contributes to the candidate’s overall match score. You can adjust the weight of each criterion based on its importance to the role. Criteria with a higher weight will have a greater influence on the ranking, helping the most suitable candidates appear higher in the results. You can also add a new criterion based on your requirements by clicking Add Criterion . Enter the criterion you want Recruit CRM to consider, then adjust its weight according to its importance in the search. ​

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: As you adjust the filters, a live count of the total matching candidates will be displayed at the bottom of the page. This count updates based on the filters currently applied, helping you understand the size of the matching candidate pool before running the search. Click Find Candidates to run the search. The search usually takes 2–3 minutes to complete. Once the search results are available, Recruit CRM displays 100 candidates per page . From the results page, you can review the matched candidates and take action directly such as: Add the selected candidates to your Recruit CRM database.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Select individual candidates or use the bulk selection option to select multiple candidates. Bulk selection from the AI Sourcing Search Results is limited to 100 candidates at a time , corresponding to one full page of results. When you select a candidate, the panel on the right provides a detailed view of the candidate’s profile , along with the Matching Criteria that contributed to the candidate’s match score. This helps you understand why the candidate was ranked for the search and how well their profile matches the requirements. ​ How does the Job-based AI search work in AI Sourcing?

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: While using the job-based AI search in AI Sourcing, it extracts relevant Search Filters from your query or Job Description and uses the Matching Criteria to evaluate candidates. Each candidate is ranked and scored from 0–100 based on how closely they match the defined criteria, with reasoning provided for each score. You can review and customize the Matching Criteria before running the search. ​ Search for candidates using filters from the Filter Search section in AI Sourcing Filter search allows you to manually define the criteria used to search the Global Database . Go to the Candidates list page and click AI Sourcing at the top.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Enter the values for the fields you want to use as search criteria. Review the selected filters and click Search . Title searches the candidate’s current role and previous roles they have held in the past. To search for only the current roles, you need to enable/turn on the 'Current Only' toggle. Set a minimum and/or maximum number of years of experience. Searches for skills across the candidate’s entire profile rather than a single field. Mark specific skills as Must-have to make them require, or leave them as Good-to-have to improve ranking without making them mandatory. Set the required proficiency level and optionally mark a language as Must-have .

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Matches any of the locations you enter. You can enter a city, locality, state, or country. Location matching is based on the candidate's current profile location rather than their employer's location. Recruit CRM can recognize known location synonyms in natural-language searches. Use Boolean search operators such as AND, OR, and NOT , including grouped searches, across the candidate’s full profile. University, Graduation Year, Degree, Name These fields are also available for searching.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Limits results to candidates who currently hold the searched Job Title or currently work at the selected Company , rather than candidates who held the title or worked at the company in the past. Recruit CRM may automatically enable this option when it is relevant to the search. Only Skills and Language Skills allow Must-have and Good-to-have values to be combined in the same search. Other fields match any of the values entered by default. For stricter matching, use Boolean search with AND logic.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: When using Filter Search in AI Sourcing , Recruit CRM does not automatically treat different names for the same location, such as Los Angeles and LA , as equivalent. However, when a location is included in a natural-language query or job description, Recruit CRM may automatically recognize and add known synonyms to the filters. Filter Search in AI Sourcing returns candidates who match the selected filters but does not rank them based on suitability. No AI scoring is applied, so the order of the results does not represent a best-to-worst ranking.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: For most fields, selecting multiple values returns candidates matching at least one of the selected values. For stricter combinations, you can use AND/OR/NOT Boolean logic in the Keywords search. Skills and Language Skills are exceptions because they allow requirements to be marked as Must-have or Good-to-have . AI Sourcing uses credits based on the type of search performed. 1 credit per page, which returns up to 100 results. (Since Filter Search does not use AI ranking/reasoning, it consumes only 1 credit compared to AI Search/Job-based AI Search). 3 credits per page, which returns up to 100 results, charged per page 3 credits per new page, which returns up to 100 results.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 3 credits per new page, which returns up to 100 results. Since it will be a totally new search when filters/matching criteria are refined, it will consume 3 credits. Reopening a search from Search History does not consume any credits. For Natural-language-based AI Search and Job-based AI Search, unlocking a new page of results consumes an additional 3 credits for that page. Using Refine Matches to adjust the search and generate updated results consumes another 3 credits .

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Previously unlocked result pages can be revisited from Search History without any credit consumption . However, loading another page of AI-ranked results from Search History consumes 3 credits for that page, and using Refine Matches consumes 3 credits because the AI matching process is run again. Recruit CRM saves previously unlocked AI Sourcing results in Search History , allowing you to return to result pages you have already viewed without consuming additional credits. Open the History tab by clicking the clock icon at the top of the page. The Search History panel will open on the left side of the screen. ​ Select any previously unlocked search to return to its results.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Previously unlocked result pages can be revisited without consuming additional credits. ​ You can manage your saved searches directly from the Search History panel. Hover over the search you want to manage. Click the three-dot menu that appears on the left side of the search. Pin: Keeps the search easily accessible in your Search History. Delete: Remove the search from your Search History. Natural-language-based AI Search and Filter Search history is specific to the user who created the search. Job-based search history is shared between users who have access to the same job. Natural-language-based AI Search and Filter searches can be renamed with a custom name of up to 500 characters.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Refining a search creates a new AI run and consumes credits. In AI Sourcing , Filter Search does not use AI ranking. It only filters candidates based on the criteria you specify, so the order of the results does not represent a suitability ranking. AI Matching Criteria and explanations are currently generated in English, regardless of the language used in the Job Description. Bulk selection from AI Sourcing results is limited to 100 candidates at a time.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: When you add a candidate from AI Sourcing results to your Recruit CRM database, Recruit CRM imports their name, location, skills, summary, total experience (in years), job title, current organization, and work and education history. The candidate's LinkedIn profile PDF isn't imported through AI Sourcing. What's the difference between Filter Search and AI Search while using AI Sourcing? In AI Sourcing , Filter Search returns candidates who match the filters you specify without AI ranking. AI Search uses AI to interpret your query, score the candidates, and rank them based on how well they match your requirements.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Can I edit the filters and Matching Criteria generated by AI while using AI Sourcing? Yes, while using AI Sourcing, you can edit, add, or remove Search Filters and Matching Criteria before running an AI Search. You can also adjust the weight of each Matching Criterion based on how important it is to the role. Does Filter Search rank candidates based on suitability in AI Sourcing? No, in AI Sourcing, Filter Search only applies the selected filters and does not use AI scoring or ranking. The order of candidates in the results does not represent a best-to-worst ranking.

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Recruit CRM uses a combination of large language models, including Google's Gemini , to generate matching criteria and score candidates in AI Sourcing. In AI Sourcing, where are the candidate profiles in the Global Database sourced from? In AI Sourcing, candidate profiles in the Global Database are sourced from publicly available profiles provided by third-party data partners . Does Recruit CRM add candidate data from a customer’s Recruit CRM database to the Global Database?

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: No. Recruit CRM never aggregates or adds data from a customer’s Recruit CRM database to the Global Database . Your Recruit CRM database belongs exclusively to your company or agency and is not made available to other customers. Can data from one customer’s Recruit CRM database be made available to other customers through the Global Database? No. Data from one customer’s Recruit CRM database is never made available to other customers through the Global Database .

chunks.t: AI Sourcing in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: AI Sourcing gives you 3 ways to find new candidates from Recruit CRM's Global Database: use Filter Search to quickly find candidates matching specific filters, use Natural-language-based AI Search to describe your search in plain language and receive an AI-ranked shortlist, or use Job-based Search to use the job description from a selected job to define the search criteria and find, rank, and score matching candidates.
