The option to Create Invoice will appear if there are any other existing linked invoices. ​ 3. The invoice will automatically link to that company. ​ Option 2: From the Placements & Invoices tab 1. Go to Placements & Invoices → Invoices . Click " + New Invoice". ​ 2. Select a template (Recruit CRM provides default templates that you can edit or clone. You can also create a new template ). ​

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 3. Choose the template and record from the options below (candidate, contact, company, jobs or deal you’d like to associate this Invoice with). ​ 4. Once the form opens, you’ll see a live preview on the right showing your template and real-time calculations. ​ 5. Filling Invoice Details : ​ Entering Invoice Details (Left-hand Side): ​ While creating the invoice, you can enter values like salary, placement fee, a start and due date. You’ll see the total amount update automatically based on your formulas and fields. ​

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: ​ ​ Customizing the Invoice Layout (Right-hand Side): ​ On the right-hand side of the invoice creation screen, you will see a live preview of the invoice template . This preview is fully customizable and allows you to edit the layout and formatting of the invoice directly from the editor. ​ At the top of the editor, you will find several formatting and editing tools that allow you to structure and customize the invoice document. ​ Use Undo and Redo options to revert or reapply changes Upload or insert images (for example, a company logo) directly from your computer Insert tables by specifying the number of rows and columns Add hyperlinks within the invoice content

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Insert a Table of Contents for structured documents Add headers and footers to organize the layout Insert page numbers to structure multi-page invoices Add page breaks to control how content flows across pages Configure Page Setup and layout settings to adjust how the invoice appears in the final document Use Find to quickly locate text within the document Modify text formatting , including font type, font size, and other styling options​ The options allow you to format and structure the invoice document directly within the preview editor, similar to working in a standard document editor. ​ Once done, click on "Save" to keep it as a draft or "Save & Send" to email it to your client. ​

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: ​ Note: The invoice number is auto-generated but can be customized anytime from your billing settings. Option 3: Creating Invoices from the Hiring Pipeline You can also create an invoice automatically when updating candidate stages in the hiring pipeline. ​ Go to a specific Job and click View All to see all the candidates assigned to that job. ​ Select the candidate(s) whose hiring stage you want to update and create an invoice for. You can do this from either the List View or the Kanban View , and click Update Hiring Stage from the top. ​ Change the Hiring Stage as required. Below the Remark box , enable the Create Invoice option and click Submit. ​

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Choose an invoice template and click Create Invoice. The system will automatically generate invoices and associate them with the relevant records. ​ You can also generate invoice directly by changing the candidate's hiring stage, simply update the Hiring Stage and make sure to check the Create Invoice option at the bottom. ​ You can add your own fields to capture extra billing details like “Project Code,” “Tax Category,” or “Payment Type.” 1. Go to Admin Settings → Invoice Fields and templates . ​ 3. Choose the type of field (Text, Long Text, Date, Number, Dropdown, or Multi-select). Name the field and set visibility. Click "Save" . ​

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: These fields appear on your invoice creation form and can also be used inside templates. You can use Internal Custom Fields to track invoice information that is only visible to you and your team. Creating an Internal Custom Field for Invoices 1. Go to Admin Settings >> Navigate to Invoice Fields & Settings . >> Open the Invoice Fields tab. 3. Select Internal Field as the field type. Enter the required Field Name and choose the appropriate Field Type .

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: When creating a new invoice custom field, you can choose whether it should be a Template Field or an Internal Field . Template Fields are available on invoice templates and can be displayed on client-facing invoice PDFs, while Internal Fields are intended for internal tracking purposes and are never visible to clients or included in invoice PDFs. Managing Internal Custom Fields on the Invoice List Page Internal Custom Fields can be displayed as columns on the Invoice List page, allowing you to view and manage internal invoice information alongside other invoice details. These fields support standard list page actions such as sorting, filtering, resizing, reordering, pinning, and hiding.

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You can also update Internal Custom Fields in bulk directly from the Invoice List page by using the "Update Field" option, making it easier to maintain invoice data across multiple records at once. When exporting invoices, you can choose to include Internal Custom Fields in the export file, giving you greater flexibility when reporting on or sharing invoice data internally. When creating or editing an invoice, fields are organized into two sections: Invoice Details for client-facing information shown on the invoice PDF, and Internal Custom Fields for information used only for internal tracking.

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You can also access Internal Custom Fields from the Invoice Preview page through a dedicated 'Invoice Fields' tab, where internal field values can be viewed and edited as long as the invoice has not been marked as paid . Once an invoice is marked as Paid , Internal Custom Fields can no longer be edited. The invoice editor is also locked to help maintain invoice data integrity. Field dependencies can be configured between Internal Custom Fields . However, field dependencies are not supported for Template Custom Fields.

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: The maximum number of invoice custom fields allowed under your plan is shared across both Template Custom Fields and Internal Custom Fields. You can add up to 15 custom fields on the Pro Plan and up to 100 custom fields on the Business Plan. Recruit CRM provides default invoice templates that you can edit or clone. You can also create new Invoice templates. 1. Go to Admin Settings → Invoice Fields and templates . ​ 2. Click on the “ + Add Invoice Template ” button in the top-right corner under the Invoice Template section to create a new invoice template. ​

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 3. Start by adding the name of the template. Then, choose who you want to share the template with, it can be specific teammates or the entire team. ​ Next, set the due date (for example, selecting 30 days will automatically calculate the due date as 30 days from the issue date). ​ By default, the Amount field is already added. You can now add more default and custom fields such as (Description, Salary, or Placement Fee) as per your needs. ​ Once the fields are added, define formulas. ​

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You can mark Template Custom Fields as required while creating or editing an invoice template. When a field is marked as required, users must provide a value before the invoice can be saved, helping ensure that important billing information is captured consistently. 4. Once all fields and formulas are added, click on "Customize Theme". You will see a preview of your template. ​ From the top-right side, you can add placeholders and customise the layout and view of the template as desired. Finally, once everything looks good, click on "Save". ​

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: 1. From the left-hand sidebar, click on Placements & Invoices . You’ll see two tabs: Placements and Invoices. ​ Select the Invoices tab to view all invoices created by your team. Open any saved invoice. ​ 2. Click the ⚙️ (cog icon) beside the 'Create Invoice' button. ​ 3. This opens Billing Information, where you can: Change invoice number prefix (e.g., INV-001 → E-INV-001) Set a custom starting number for new invoices This helps you align invoice numbering with your organization’s preferred format, and click Save. ​ After saving an invoice, you can view and manage its status to track the progress of the billing process. ​

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You can update the status of an invoice directly from the invoice record. Locate the status column on the invoice list page. Select the appropriate status based on the current stage of the billing process. Add remarks if needed to record notes related to the status update. Each invoice also maintains a status history , allowing you to view previous status changes along with any remarks that were added. Invoices in the Overdue stage can be updated to: Invoices in the Sent to Client stage can be updated to: Invoices in the Unpaid stage can be updated to:

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Once an invoice is marked as Paid, its status cannot be changed. However, you can view the invoice status history along with any remarks added. Draft invoices cannot be moved to another stage directly. Click the pencil icon next to the Invoice ID on the left side of the invoice to open the Edit Invoice page. After editing, save the invoice , and you will then be able to move it to the required stage. Problem: Cannot edit internal custom fields on an invoice Likely cause: The invoice has been marked as paid, which locks internal custom fields and the editor. Open the invoice preview page and verify the invoice status. Confirm whether the invoice is marked as paid.

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: If the invoice is paid, understand that editing internal fields is intentionally disabled to maintain data integrity. If changes are essential, consider internal notes or additional records outside the locked invoice, according to your internal policy. Problem: A custom field does not appear on invoice templates Likely cause : The field was created as an internal field rather than a template field. In admin settings, open Invoice Fields and Templates. Check the field type (template vs internal). If you need the field on client-facing templates, create or configure it as a template field. Use internal fields only for data that should stay internal and not appear on PDFs.

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Problem: Field dependencies are not working on certain invoice fields Likely cause : Field dependencies are only supported for internal custom fields, not template custom fields. Identify whether the affected fields are internal or template custom fields. If you need dependencies, re-design the setup using internal custom fields where dependencies are allowed. Keep in mind that template fields cannot have dependencies. Can I change a field from Template Field to Internal Field later? No. Once an invoice custom field is created, its “Use field as” selection cannot be changed. This prevents accidental movement of client-facing data into internal-only areas or vice versa.

chunks.t: Creating and Managing Invoices in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Are Internal Custom Fields included in Boolean Search? Yes. Boolean Search will search across visible Internal Custom Fields on the Invoice list page. What happens to Internal Custom Fields when an invoice is marked as Paid? Once an invoice is marked as Paid, Internal Custom Fields become read-only and cannot be edited. Is the invoice custom field limit separate for Template and Internal fields? No. The limit is shared across both sections. For example, if your plan allows 100 invoice custom fields, that total includes both Template Custom Fields and Internal Custom Fields.

chunks.t: New Version Of The Company List Page
chunks.x: What does this feature do and when to use it? The new Company List Page helps you organize and manage company records more efficiently. View and manage company records in an improved layout. Perform bulk actions on multiple companies. Search and filter company records efficiently. To switch to the new version, click your Profile icon → Switch to New Version . You can switch back to the previous design at any time using the same option. The Company Quick View displays the total number of company records, along with the number of Hotlists and Saved Searches and the records within them. You can edit, pin, and delete Hotlists, as well as edit, pin, clone, and delete Saved Searches.

chunks.t: New Version Of The Company List Page
chunks.x: You can also minimize or expand the Company View , Company Hotlists , and Saved Searches sections The Company List Page uses infinite scrolling, allowing you to view company records continuously without switching between pages. The first 100 records are loaded initially. As you scroll, additional records can be selected automatically, up to a maximum of 3,000 records . You can also use Scroll to Top to quickly return to the top of the list. Recruit CRM provides multiple ways to select companies in bulk: Header checkbox: Selects the first 50 loaded records. As you continue scrolling, another 50 records are automatically selected.

chunks.t: New Version Of The Company List Page
chunks.x: Custom Record Selection: Click the arrow next to the header checkbox, enter a number between 1 and 3,000 , and click Select to select the exact number of records based on the current list order. Custom Record Selection replaces any existing manual or bulk selection. Automatic scroll-based selection is disabled after a custom selection until the selection is cleared. Only values between 1 and 3,000 are accepted. The Select All option is disabled once 3,000 records are selected. The five most commonly used bulk actions are displayed upfront by default, while the remaining actions are available under More . You can customize which actions appear upfront:

chunks.t: New Version Of The Company List Page
chunks.x: Move the required options above the dashed line. Click Save . Set a default bulk action arrangement for your account Account Owners can configure a default bulk action arrangement for all users from Others View . To prevent users from changing the arrangement, select Do not allow users of your account to edit their view . Please note: Users with an Admin role or the required custom permissions can still rearrange the actions. For a custom role, enable Allow User to Choose their Own Field Order and Visibility . You can click the arrow next to a column to manage individual column settings. Pin Column – Keep a column fixed while scrolling.

chunks.t: New Version Of The Company List Page
chunks.x: Add Column to Right/Left – Add a hidden column next to the selected column. Note : Only the hidden columns will be displayed in the list while adding a column to the left or right. Sort Ascending/Descending – Sort column values. Multi Sorting – Sort by multiple columns using the column actions or by holding Shift while selecting columns. Hide Column – Remove a column from the current view. Click Show/Hide Columns next to the Add Company button to manage which columns are displayed. You can also view the number of Visible Columns and Hidden Columns . Pinned columns can be unpinned from this section.

chunks.t: New Version Of The Company List Page
chunks.x: You can search for a field within the Show/Hide Columns section. Matching fields are highlighted, and a counter helps you move between multiple matches. You can also drag and drop columns to change their order while searching. Click the three dots next to a company under the Name column to access company-level actions: You can adjust the width of individual columns by hovering over the margin next to the column name and dragging it. You can also adjust the width of the Quick View section. Switch to Classic View in Advanced Search The new Advanced Search allows you to switch to Classic View , which displays filters in the familiar grid format. Use the grid modal to apply your filters.

chunks.t: New Version Of The Company List Page
chunks.x: Filters in Classic View are treated as independent AND conditions. Important: Classic View does not support duplicate filters, group filters, or cross-entity filters. The dropdown-based Advanced Search remains available with its existing functionality. You can switch back using Switch to Compact View . The new Company List Page makes it easier to manage company records, customize your workspace, perform bulk actions, and search through company data efficiently. Features such as infinite scroll, flexible column management, bulk selection, company-level actions, and Classic View in Advanced Search help you tailor the Company List Page to your recruitment workflow.

chunks.t: Creating Invoices for Timesheets (Beta)
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM allows you to create invoices directly from approved timesheets, making the contract billing process faster and more consistent. You can select multiple approved timesheets, generate an invoice, customize invoice details, and send it to your client directly from Recruit CRM. Create invoices directly from approved timesheets. Combine multiple eligible timesheets into a single invoice. Review and customize invoices before sending them to clients. Automatically track timesheet billing and collection statuses. Manage contract staffing invoices without relying on separate billing tools or manual exports.

chunks.t: Creating Invoices for Timesheets (Beta)
chunks.x: Please note: This feature is currently available in Beta and can be enabled upon request. Please contact your Account Manager to have it enabled for your account. Recruit CRM provides two standard templates for creating invoices from timesheets: Contract Job Template: Displays the total hours and billed amount and is suitable for summary-based invoicing or billing cycles that don't require a daily breakdown. Contract Job with Weekdays Template: Displays hours for each day from Monday to Sunday and is best suited for weekly timesheets.

chunks.t: Creating Invoices for Timesheets (Beta)
chunks.x: You can customize the theme, header, and footer of both templates. However, the table content and fields are fixed and cannot be renamed or edited. You can also reset the templates to their default format whenever needed. You can begin creating an invoice from either the C ontractor Details Page or the Timesheets section of a Deal. From the Contractor Details Page , navigate to Jobs , open a Contract or Contract to Permanent job, scroll to the Candidate Pipeline , and click View All Timesheets to view the timesheets associated with the contractor for that job

chunks.t: Creating Invoices for Timesheets (Beta)
chunks.x: Alternatively, navigate to Deals , open a Deal associated with a Contract or Contract to Permanent job, and open the Timesheets section to view the timesheets of contractors associated with the Deal. Select the approved timesheets you want to include in the invoice. Please note: Invoices can only be created from eligible, approved timesheets. Click Create an Invoice . A preview window will display the selected timesheets. Review the details and click Proceed to continue. The system automatically validates the selected timesheets before creating the invoice. The first approved timesheet selected is used as the reference for validating the company and currency.

chunks.t: Creating Invoices for Timesheets (Beta)
chunks.x: Please note- A timesheet cannot be included in the invoice if it belongs to a different company, isn't approved, has already been billed or collected, is attached to a draft invoice, or uses a different currency. Any ineligible timesheets are automatically excluded from invoice creation. Select the invoice template you want to use and, if required, add a description for internal reference. The description is visible only to recruiters and does not appear on the invoice sent to the client. You can choose between the following two templates: Contract Job: A clean, simple layout showing total hours and the billed amount.

chunks.t: Creating Invoices for Timesheets (Beta)
chunks.x: Contract Job with Weekdays: A detailed version showing daily hours and corresponding amounts. Click Create Invoice to generate the invoice. Review the complete invoice and make any required adjustments. You can edit client details, update the issue and due dates, remove timesheets, add additional line items, change the invoice template, or add Additional Notes that will appear on the final invoice. Click Show Preview to review how the invoice will appear to the client, and click Save after making any changes. Once the invoice is ready, use the dropdown beside Save to either save it as a draft or send it directly to the client via email.

chunks.t: Creating Invoices for Timesheets (Beta)
chunks.x: Once an invoice is saved, including it as a draft, it is automatically linked to the corresponding timesheets. Recruit CRM automatically updates timesheet statuses based on the actions performed on their linked invoice. When an invoice is created, the linked timesheets move to Billed . Once the invoice is marked as Paid , the timesheets move to Collected . Timesheets linked to a draft invoice remain Unbilled until the invoice is finalized. If the invoice is deleted, the invoice association is removed, and the linked timesheets return to Unbilled .

chunks.t: Creating Invoices for Timesheets (Beta)
chunks.x: You can also manually mark timesheets as Paid and add a payout number and payout details. If the timesheet status is changed back to unpaid, the payout number and payout date are automatically cleared. Problem: I can't select a timesheet for invoice creation. Likely Cause: The timesheet isn't approved or isn't eligible for invoice creation. What to Check: Confirm that the timesheet is approved and hasn't already been billed, collected, or attached to a draft invoice. Resolution: Approve the timesheet and ensure it isn't already associated with another invoice before creating a new invoice. Problem: Timesheets remain Unbilled after creating an invoice.

chunks.t: Creating Invoices for Timesheets (Beta)
chunks.x: Likely Cause: The invoice has been saved as a draft. What to Check: Check whether the associated invoice is still in draft status. Resolution: Finalize the invoice. The linked timesheets will automatically move to the appropriate billing status. 1. Can I create an invoice using timesheets with different currencies? No. All timesheets included in an invoice must use the same currency as the first approved timesheet selected. 2. Can I customize the default invoice templates? Yes. You can customize the theme, header, and footer. However, the table content and fields are fixed and cannot be renamed or edited. 3. What happens when I save an invoice as a draft?

chunks.t: Creating Invoices for Timesheets (Beta)
chunks.x: The invoice is linked to the corresponding timesheets, but the timesheets remain in the Unbilled status until the invoice is finalized. Creating invoices directly from approved timesheets simplifies contract billing by allowing you to select eligible timesheets, generate and customize invoices, send them to clients, and automatically track billing statuses in Recruit CRM. This helps maintain accurate billing records and keeps your contract staffing workflow organized. How to Create and Manage Timesheets? chunks.t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: The Contractors page is available under the Pay and Bill entity and provides a centralized view of all candidates who are working as contractors. This page helps agency users track contractor availability, active and future assignments, job duration, and related job and deal information from one place. ​ Only candidates who have timesheets enabled for at least one job are shown on this page. Currently, this feature is in beta and can be enabled upon request. Please feel free to reach out to your Account Manager to have it enabled for your account. You will see a list of all contractors that you have access to, based on your roles and permissions.

chunks.t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Open the Contractors page from the Pay and Bill entity. Review the list of contractors displayed in a single list view. Remember that a candidate appears here only if: They are assigned to at least one job where timesheets are enabled. You have permission to view that candidate’s record. Note: If you do not have permission to view a candidate, you will not be able to see that candidate listed as a contractor on the Contractors page. Look at the status column for each contractor. Note that the contractor status is automatically determined by the system and cannot be manually edited.

chunks.t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Assigned : The contractor is either currently working on an active job or is assigned to a future job that has not started yet. Green Assigned: The contractor has an active job. Yellow Assigned: The contractor has a future job that has not started yet. Available : The contractor is not working on any active jobs. All previously assigned jobs have passed their job duration (their start and end dates have ended). The Job Name and Job Duration columns provide an at-a-glance view of the contractor's current and upcoming assignments. The Job Name column displays all relevant jobs assigned to the contractor, including future job assignments.

chunks.t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: If a contractor has both active and future assignments, all relevant job names are displayed. For active jobs , the number of days remaining along with the job's end date. For future jobs , Yet to Start along with the relevant job's end date. If a contractor has multiple jobs, the Job Duration column displays the active job with the highest number of days remaining . Hover over the Job Duration value to view details of all relevant jobs, including: The remaining days are calculated based on the account's timezone . The Job Duration value is color-coded based on the percentage of the total assignment duration remaining:

chunks.t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: For example, for a 100-day assignment, 50 days remaining is shown in orange , while fewer than 30 days remaining is shown in red . You can choose which fields are displayed on the Contractors page and arrange them to suit your workflow. On the Contractors page, click Show/Hide Columns in the top right corner. Select the fields you want to display or clear the ones you want to hide. Drag and drop the selected fields to arrange them in your preferred order. Your selected columns and their order will be reflected on the Contractors page, making it easier to view the information most relevant to your workflow.

chunks.t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: The Contractors page allows you to filter the list to quickly find specific contractors. On the Contractors page, go to the top right corner of the page. Click Add filters to open the filtering options. Select a field from the Contractors field list to filter by Status, Job Name, or Deal Name. Choose the required filter values to refine the results. Apply the selected filters to quickly find specific contractors based on their status, the jobs they are assigned to, or the deals associated with those jobs. You can filter contractors using the following fields: You can select multiple contractors at once and perform bulk actions on the selected records.

chunks.t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: On the Contractors page, select contractors individually by clicking the checkbox next to each contractor. To select contractors in bulk, click the checkbox at the top of the list, which selects 50 contractors at a time . Continue scrolling down the list to select additional contractors until the desired number is selected. You can select up to 3,000 contractors at a time for bulk actions by clicking on Select All.

chunks.t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Once the desired contractors are selected, a bulk action bar will appear at the top of the list with options such as Assign to Job, Request Updated Profile, Pitch Candidate, Add to Hotlist, Enroll in Sequence, Compose Email, Add Note, Mark as Off-Limits, Update Field, Export, Enable Portal Access, Disable Portal Access, and Delete Candidate . Click More to view additional bulk action options. Select from the Bulk Action bar the action that you want to perform. Assign to Job: When Assign to Job is selected as a bulk action, the job selection is automatically limited to Contract and Contract-to-Perm jobs.

chunks.t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Contractor Portal: Upto 200 contractors can be enabled or disabled for the Contractor Portal through bulk actions. When enabling the portal, eligibility is checked automatically. Contractors are excluded if: A portal already exists with the same email address. They have reached the daily invitation limit. If you would like to learn more about this feature, you can book a quick call with our team through this link . Problem: A contractor you expect to see is missing from the Contractors page Likely cause: The candidate does not have timesheets enabled for any job, or you do not have permission to view that candidate.

chunks.t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Confirm that the candidate is assigned to at least one job where timesheets are enabled. Confirm that your user permissions allow you to view that candidate’s record. Enable timesheets for at least one job for that candidate if required. Ask an administrator to review and update your permissions if you should have access to that candidate. Problem: You cannot change a contractor’s status Likely cause: Contractor status is system-generated. Review the contractor's active and future jobs and their dates to understand how the status is being set.

chunks.t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Adjust job assignments or job dates if the status should change based on the contractor's actual assignments, rather than trying to edit the status field directly. Only candidates who are assigned to at least one job with timesheets enabled appear on the Contractors page. What happens if a contractor is unassigned from all jobs? If a contractor is unassigned from all jobs where timesheets are enabled: They are automatically removed from the Contractors page If the contractor is reassigned to a job with timesheets enabled, they will appear again on the Contractors page. Do deleted candidates appear on the Contractors page?

chunks.t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: No. Deleted candidates do not appear on the Contractors page. However, their historical timesheets remain accessible on the All Timesheets page. For active jobs, it shows the number of days remaining and the job's end date. For future jobs, it shows Yet to Start and the job's end date. What happens to the Job Duration column if a contractor has multiple jobs? The Job Duration column shows the active job with the highest number of days remaining. Hover over the value to see details for all relevant active and future jobs. What happens when a contractor has only future assignments? The contractor is shown as Assigned in yellow, and the Job Duration column shows Yet to Start .

chunks.t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
chunks.x: A contractor is shown as Available only when they have no active jobs and no future job assignments. The All Contractors page in Recruit CRM gives you a clear, centralized way to track contractors with timesheets, their availability, active jobs, and related deals. If you need this beta feature enabled or have questions about access and visibility, contact your account manager for further assistance. How to Create and Manage Timesheets? (Beta) Timesheets - Deals for Contract Staffing (Beta) Contractor Portal in Recruit CRM - Timesheets (Beta)

chunks.t: Setting up your profile section (New UI)
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The Profile section allows you to manage your personal Recruit CRM account settings, including your profile picture, registered email, time zone, time format, default currency, password, email reminders, daily email reports, email tracking, and browser notifications. Set up your Recruit CRM profile for the first time. Update your registered email, password, or time zone. Manage email reminders, daily reports, email tracking, or browser notifications. Open your Profile section: From any screen in Recruit CRM, click your avatar in the top-right corner and select Profile .

chunks.t: Setting up your profile section (New UI)
chunks.x: Change your profile picture: In the Profile section, click the existing profile image on the left side and upload the picture you want to use for your Recruit CRM account. Change your registered email ID: Click the email section, remove your existing email address, and enter the new email address you want to use for your Recruit CRM account. Set your default time zone: Select your preferred time zone from the Time Zone dropdown and click Save Profile to apply the change.

chunks.t: Setting up your profile section (New UI)
chunks.x: Choose your time format: Select either the 12-hour AM/PM or 24-hour format. Your selected format will be reflected wherever time is displayed or selected across Recruit CRM, including interviews and custom date/time fields. The same format will also be reflected in the mobile app. In 12-hour format, times will appear as: 5:00 AM, 5:00 PM. In 24-hour format, times will appear as: 05:00, 17:00 (without AM/PM) Set your default currency: Select your preferred currency from the Default Currency dropdown. Note: You can also have a separate currency for each candidate and each job. You can change that by going inside the candidate's profile or inside that job.

chunks.t: Setting up your profile section (New UI)
chunks.x: All Amount fields follow a standardized currency format: <Symbol><Amount> <Code> (e.g., $100 USD , ₹5,000 INR ). Amount values are also right-aligned across list views and tables for easier scanning. Note: This formatting does not apply to Contract Staffing/Timesheets . Change your account password: Click Change Password, enter your current password, and then enter your new password to update your account credentials. Manage email reminders and daily email reports: Turn off email reminders and the daily email report: If you don't want to receive email reminders for your tasks and appointments in Recruit CRM, here's how you can turn them off by disabling this toggle.

chunks.t: Setting up your profile section (New UI)
chunks.x: You can also disable the daily email report, which is a report you'll receive every morning between 8-10 AM, essentially a list of all your website, job boards, and talent pool applications or Recruit CRM profile submissions from the last twenty-four hours. Click here to learn more about Email Reminders! Manage the email tracking pixel: This feature will help you manage your email tracking within Recruit CRM. If it is on, Recruit CRM will add a tracking pixel in your email body, and if it is off, then the system won't add a tracking pixel.

chunks.t: Setting up your profile section (New UI)
chunks.x: If the emails that are sent from Recruit CRM are going to the spam or junk folder of your recipient, turn this tracking pixel off to avoid emails going to spam or junk. Enable browser notifications: You can also enable browser notifications for real-time updates without the need to be active on the web app. Note: Profile settings apply to your individual user account and do not change other users’ settings. Problem: Emails sent from Recruit CRM are landing in recipients’ spam or junk folders. Likely cause: Email tracking pixel is turned on and being flagged by some email providers. What to check: Check the Email Tracking Pixel setting in your profile.

chunks.t: Setting up your profile section (New UI)
chunks.x: Resolution path: Turn the tracking pixel off to avoid emails going to spam or junk. The Profile section lets you manage your personal Recruit CRM settings, preferences, and notifications in one place. How Email Open Tracking Works in Recruit CRM? Changing/Resetting Your Recruit CRM Password Requesting Updated Candidate Profiles (New UI)

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting (New UI)
chunks.x: What this features does and when to use it? Through this feature, you can generate branded, client-ready resumes directly from candidate profiles. You can apply branding elements such as headers, footers, cover letters, and watermarks to create consistent resume submissions across clients and roles. You can also redact sensitive information such as names, phone numbers, email addresses, physical addresses, and LinkedIn profiles before sharing candidate profiles externally. Once saved, the formatted resume is stored on the candidate record either in a selected file-type custom field or in the Files section. This helps you maintain a consistent, professional format across all submissions.

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting (New UI)
chunks.x: Please note - The Resume/CV Formatting feature, including Text Redaction and the ability to add custom headers, footers, and watermarks is available on the Business Plan and above. You want to add your logo, agency details, or standardised branding to every CV sent to clients. You need to hide sensitive candidate information (like contact details or LinkedIn) before sharing resumes. Your client requires resumes in a specific, uniform layout or format. You want to store multiple versions of a candidate’s resume (raw vs. formatted) in structured fields. ​ • If you want to save formatted resumes into specific fields, you will need file-type custom fields created under Candidate Fields .

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting (New UI)
chunks.x: • When converting DOC files to PDF, minor formatting limitations may occur. While the system handles most conversions accurately, complete accuracy cannot be guaranteed in all cases. 1. Use any of the following methods to access the Generate Formatted Resume tab - From within the Candidate Profile page To format a resume, go to the candidate profile and click on the three dots at the top of the profile. ​ Once you click this,in the menu that appears, select Generate Formatted Resume . ​ You can also open the candidate’s resume in Recruit CRM and scroll to the bottom of the page. From there, click on Generate Formatted Resume to proceed.

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting (New UI)
chunks.x: 2 . Configure Header, Footer, Cover Letter, and Watermark Once you open the Generate Formatted Resume tab, use the Templates section to apply headers, footers, cover letters, and watermarks. These templates allow you to standardise resume branding across clients, teams, or submission workflows. You can select an existing template or create a new one based on your requirements. 3. Use Text Redaction to Remove Sensitive Information Text redaction allows you to hide sensitive candidate information from a resume before sharing it with clients. This can include details such as name, email, phone number, address, LinkedIn profile, or any other information you do not want to disclose.

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting (New UI)
chunks.x: Text Redaction only affects the formatted resume that is generated. The original resume file and candidate profile remain unchanged. This is commonly used when sharing resumes with clients while withholding personal contact information during early recruitment stages. Keyword-based redaction Search for a specific keyword, and the system will automatically identify and select all instances of that term in the resume. For example, entering “LinkedIn” will highlight all occurrences of the word, allowing you to remove them in one go. ​

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting (New UI)
chunks.x: Manual redaction using highlighter Use the highlighter tool to manually select specific sections of the resume. Simply click and drag over the text or area you want to hide. ​ Once you’ve selected all the required sections, click Apply Redaction to remove or hide the highlighted content from the formatted resume. 4. Save the Formatted Resume and Choose Storage Location Saving creates a new formatted version of the resume. The original resume remains unchanged on the candidate record. You can choose where the formatted version is stored so it can be accessed later without regenerating it.

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting (New UI)
chunks.x: Once you’ve made all the changes to the Resume/CV, click Save . A popup will appear where you can rename the file and choose where to store the formatted resume. Enter a file name and select a file-type custom field as the storage location. If you don’t have one set up, you can create a new file-type custom field directly from this popup. ​ If no custom field is selected, the resume will automatically be saved in the Files section of the candidate profile. ​ ​ Note: Only file-type custom fields created under Candidate Fields will appear in the dropdown. 1. Problem: I cannot see the option Generate Formatted Resume on the candidate profile. Likely cause: Plan or permission limitations.

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting (New UI)
chunks.x: Confirm that your account is on the Business plan or above and that your user role has permission to view and edit candidate files. Ask your account admin to confirm your plan and adjust your role permissions if needed. 2. Problem: My file-type custom field does not appear in the save dropdown. Likely cause: The custom field is not configured under Candidate Fields or is not of file type. Go to your field settings and verify that the field is a file-type custom field under Candidate Fields . If needed, create a new file-type custom field under Candidate Fields, then return to the save popup and check again. 1. What changes after I use CV formatting on a resume?

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting (New UI)
chunks.x: The system creates a new formatted version of the candidate’s resume with your chosen header, footer, cover letter, watermark, and any applied redactions. The original resume file remains unchanged. 2. Which plans and roles can use the CV formatting feature? The resume/CV formatting feature, including text redaction and the ability to add custom headers, footers, and watermarks, is available on the Business plan and above. Users must have permission to access and edit candidate files. 3. Can I have different header and footer templates for different clients?

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting (New UI)
chunks.x: Yes. Under the Template section, you can choose from existing header and footer templates or create new ones. This allows you to maintain multiple branded templates for different clients or use cases. 4. Does text redaction permanently remove data from the candidate profile? No. Text redaction only affects the formatted resume you generate. The original candidate data and original resume file remain intact in the candidate profile. 5. Where is the formatted CV stored after I click Save?

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting (New UI)
chunks.x: If you select a file-type custom field in the popup, the formatted CV is saved in that field. If you do not select or create a custom field, the formatted CV will automatically be saved within the candidate’s Files section. 6. Does CV formatting modify the candidate's original resume? No. CV Formatting always creates a separate formatted version of the resume. The original resume file remains unchanged and available on the candidate record. 7. Can I apply multiple branding elements to the same resume?

chunks.t: Resume/CV Formatting (New UI)
chunks.x: Yes. A formatted resume can include a header, footer, cover letter, watermark, and text redactions at the same time. These elements are combined into a single formatted version when the resume is generated. CV Formatting helps you create consistent, client-ready resume submissions without editing documents manually. By combining branding templates and text redaction, you can maintain professional presentation standards while controlling what candidate information is shared.

chunks.t: Using candidate summary template (New UI)
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Candidate Summary Templates allow you to create reusable templates using candidate field placeholders. These templates help standardize candidate summaries, reduce manual effort, and ensure important candidate information is presented consistently. You can also set a default template that is automatically applied whenever a new candidate is added. Standardize candidate summaries across your team. Create reusable templates for different hiring workflows. Set a default summary template for newly added candidates. Quickly generate or update candidate summaries while editing candidate records.

chunks.t: Using candidate summary template (New UI)
chunks.x: Please note: You can create up to 100 templates on the Business plan and Enterprise plan and 1 template on the Pro plan . Create and use candidate summary templates Navigate to Admin Settings > Data Customization > Candidate Fields and click New Candidate Summary Template . Recruit CRM also provides Sample Template 1 , Sample Template 2 , and Sample Template 3 as ready-to-use templates. These templates have been added as ready-to-use starting points and can be further customized based on user requirements using the tools available directly within the editor, making them useful if you do not want to create a template completely from scratch.

chunks.t: Using candidate summary template (New UI)
chunks.x: Enter a name for your template and use the placeholders to fetch information from candidate fields to the template. You can easily write the outline summary of the candidate with the help of the placeholders. If you'd like Recruit CRM to automatically use a template for new candidates, click the three-dot menu (⋮) beside the template name and select Set as Default . Once a template is set as the default, Recruit CRM automatically generates candidate summaries for all newly added candidates, whether they're added manually or through resume parsing. Existing candidates will need to be updated manually. Next, to generate a candidate summary using a template:

chunks.t: Using candidate summary template (New UI)
chunks.x: Add a new candidate or open an existing candidate's profile and click the Pencil icon to edit the record. Navigate to the Candidate Summary section and select the required template from the dropdown. Review the generated summary and click Submit to save your changes. To view the generated summary, ensure the Candidate Summary field is added to the candidate profile, then click the File icon to open it. Problem: I can't create a new candidate summary template. Likely Cause: You've reached the template limit for your subscription plan. What to Check: Verify how many templates already exist and confirm your current Recruit CRM plan.

chunks.t: Using candidate summary template (New UI)
chunks.x: Resolution: Delete unused templates or upgrade your subscription if you need additional templates. Problem: My default template isn't being applied to new candidates. Likely Cause: The template hasn't been set as the default, or the candidate already existed before the default template was configured. What to Check: Confirm that the template is marked as Default and verify whether the candidate was created after the default template was configured. Resolution: Set the required template as the default. Please note that default templates are only applied to newly created candidates. 1. Does the default template apply to existing candidates?

chunks.t: Using candidate summary template (New UI)
chunks.x: No. Default templates are only applied to newly added candidates. Existing candidate summaries must be updated manually. 2. Can I change the template while editing a candidate? Yes. You can select a different template from the Candidate Summary dropdown whenever you edit a candidate. Candidate Summary Templates help you create consistent, professional candidate summaries while reducing manual effort. How to Create, Edit, and Manage Email Templates in Recruit CRM Creating title and candidate profile templates for executive search reports Bulk emailing candidates/contacts (New UI)

chunks.t: Entity Type Custom Fields (New UI)
chunks.x: Custom Entity-Type Fields empower recruiters to tailor their CRM and ATS to fit their unique workflows by linking key records like Candidates, Jobs, Contacts, Companies, Deals, Users, and Teams. These fields streamline data management, boost visibility across connected entities, and enhance automation and reporting capabilities across platforms. This feature brings the flexibility of creating multi-select searchable fields that connect entities, ensuring data integrity, consistency, and a major productivity boost — especially when used with automation tools like API, Zapier, and Webhooks.

chunks.t: Entity Type Custom Fields (New UI)
chunks.x: You can create and manage custom fields linking to Candidates, Contacts, Companies, Jobs, Deals, Users, and Teams. Please note that this is supported on Candidates, Jobs, Contacts, Companies, and Deals. Go to your Admin Settings . Navigate to the Data Customisation section, where custom fields are managed. In Data Customization, select the record type where you want to add the entity type custom field. (Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Deals, or Jobs.) Within the chosen record type, click New Custom Field . Enter a Field Name that explains the relationship (for example, “Key Account Contacts”, “Associated Recruiters”, or “Related Jobs”).

chunks.t: Entity Type Custom Fields (New UI)
chunks.x: From the Field Type options, choose one of the supported entities: Candidate, Contact, Companies, Job, Deals, Users, or Team. Once saved, the field becomes available on all records of that record type. You can also add those fields to the Profile View: Problem: The entity type custom field is not visible on records Likely Cause: The entity type custom field was created for a different record type than the one you are currently viewing in Recruit CRM. What to Check: Go to Settings > Custom Fields and confirm which record type (Candidates, Contacts, Jobs, etc.) the field was created under.

chunks.t: Entity Type Custom Fields (New UI)
chunks.x: Resolution Path: Open a record of the matching type, or create the same field under the correct record type if you need it elsewhere. Problem: Users can see the field, but cannot edit it Likely cause: Role or permission restrictions are preventing edits. What to check: Review user roles and permissions related to editing records and custom fields. Resolution path: Adjust user roles to grant edit access where appropriate. Ask an Admin to verify that no additional restrictions are configured on that record type. 1. Why are these fields only multi-select and not single-select?

chunks.t: Entity Type Custom Fields (New UI)
chunks.x: Multi-select ensures users can associate multiple related records (e.g., multiple candidates to a job) for richer data linking and flexibility. For User and Team fields, profile viewing is restricted for privacy and security. Clicking is disabled to avoid exposing sensitive team/user info. 3. Can I search records I don’t have access to? No, if you don't have access to view a record, you won't be able to search it. 4. Why can’t I use placeholders with these fields? Placeholder support is intentionally excluded since entity fields are structured references rather than free-text entries. 5. What happens if an imported value doesn't match any record?

chunks.t: Entity Type Custom Fields (New UI)
chunks.x: The field is skipped to maintain data accuracy. You must ensure correct slugs, email IDs, or team names are used. 6. Why aren’t these fields supported on the Talent Pool or Job Application settings? These fields are meant to track internal data and are ideally not to be exposed.

chunks.t: Entity Type Custom Fields (New UI)
chunks.x: Entity type custom fields in the new UI let you connect candidates, jobs, contacts, companies, deals, users, and teams in a structured, searchable way. By setting them up thoughtfully and adding them to your key views, you can streamline workflows, improve data integrity, and unlock more powerful reporting and automation. If you need help designing your field structure or troubleshooting a specific scenario, reach out to your admin or support team for further assistance. How to Create, Edit, and Manage Custom Fields in Recruit CRM Common drop-down values for custom fields How to Create, Edit, and Manage Custom Fields in Recruit CRM (New UI)

chunks.t: Job-Associated Fields and Files (New UI)
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Job-associated fields let you tailor the application process to the specific requirements of each job opening. Recruit CRM streamlines the process of managing candidate information by allowing you to customize fields based on the different job roles the candidate is being considered for. Job-associated files let you add, store, and share files that are specific to each job a candidate is associated with. This allows you to manage different resumes, cover letters, portfolios, or other documents for the same candidate across multiple roles. Together, these features streamline how you collect, store, and share candidate information that varies by job.

chunks.t: Job-Associated Fields and Files (New UI)
chunks.x: You need to ask job-specific questions on the job application form. You want to store different resumes, cover letters, or portfolios for each job a candidate applies to. You can easily add and share job-specific fields for candidates, and ensure you gather the most relevant information for each position. 1. Navigate to your Admin Settings -> Job Application Form Fields Settings 2. Scroll down to the “Job Associated Files” section and click on 'Add Field': 3. Enter the field name and select its type from the following options: 'Text', 'Long Text', 'Dropdown', 'Multiselect', 'Number', or 'Checkbox'. 4. Click on the green 'Save Field' button to add the field.

chunks.t: Job-Associated Fields and Files (New UI)
chunks.x: Recruit CRM lets you add 5 custom job-associated fields apart from the 5 default 'File' type job-associated fields in the system. How to make job-associated fields visible on the job application form? 1. Once you add the fields, turn the visibility 'ON' of the desired fields to make them visible on your job application form. Additionally, you can mark fields as 'Required' to make them mandatory for applicants to fill out. 2. Click the green 'Save' button to save your changes: 3. Upon saving the changes, the desired fields will become visible on the job application forms as well, ensuring that applicants can easily access and fill them out as required.

chunks.t: Job-Associated Fields and Files (New UI)
chunks.x: Any changes you make in the Job application form settings will apply to all the job application forms. However, you can also customize these fields uniquely for each job application form. Accessing job-specific details submitted by candidates 📄 On the job details page, within the "Candidate Pipeline" tab, click on the "Job Specific Details" button in the candidate details section to access job-related information for each candidate. You'll be able to access the job-associated fields that you've added, enabling you to upload files, add values to those fields, and view previous values added by yourself or submitted by candidates via the job application form.

chunks.t: Job-Associated Fields and Files (New UI)
chunks.x: Furthermore, you'll also be able to review the candidate questions that the candidate has submitted for that specific job. You might need different information from a candidate such as a different Cover Letter or Resume based on the different job roles they're being considered for. Recruit CRM makes it easy to add, store, and share job-specific files for Candidates. If one of your candidates wants to apply to 2 different jobs, say a Marketing role and a Sales role, with 2 job-specific Resumes. The candidates can now submit different CVs/ Portfolios/ Cover letters/ Other files for different jobs from the job application form.

chunks.t: Job-Associated Fields and Files (New UI)
chunks.x: 1. If you are on the Candidate’s profile, you can find the “View Files” option under the Assigned Jobs tab. (as seen in the image below): 2. On the Job profile, you’ll find the “Job Specific Details” option under Candidate Pipeline: Once you click on the “Job Specific Details” button under each Job assignment, you’ll have the option to add/ store 5 standard files such as Formatted Resume, Cover Letter, Portfolio and an additional 2 other files for each job. These can also be Resumes formatted and Cover Letters created within Recruit CRM. This article will give you more information: Resume/ CV Formatting There are two ways in which you can add a candidate file associated with the job: ​

chunks.t: Job-Associated Fields and Files (New UI)
chunks.x: 1. You can click on the “Upload file” option and upload a brand new file into the system 2. You can use the “Select file” option to choose an existing file from within the files section of the Candidate. How to share job-associated fields with clients? ✅ While submitting candidates to clients, you can share the fields/files associated with the particular job. To do that, click on the "Fields Shared with Clients" button and select the fields/files that you want to share. Click here to learn more about the Submit Candidates to Contact feature!

chunks.t: Job-Associated Fields and Files (New UI)
chunks.x: On the Assigned Candidates list within a job, you have the flexibility to display job-associated fields in the List view, run Advanced searches based on these fields, and seamlessly export them along with the candidate data. Problem: New job-associated field does not appear on the job application form Likely cause : The field’s visibility is turned off or changes were not saved. In Job Application Form Field Settings , confirm the field is listed under Job Associated Fields . Verify the Visibility toggle is turned on for that field. Confirm you clicked the green Save button after making changes.

chunks.t: Job-Associated Fields and Files (New UI)
chunks.x: Turn visibility on for the field, click Save , and refresh or reopen the job application form to verify the field now appears. Problem: Cannot add more job associated fields Likely cause : You have reached the limit of custom job associated fields. Count how many custom job associated fields are already created. Since Recruit CRM allows five custom job associated fields (in addition to five default file-type job associated fields), remove or repurpose existing custom fields if you need to create new ones. Can a candidate upload different resumes for different jobs?

chunks.t: Job-Associated Fields and Files (New UI)
chunks.x: Yes. Using job-associated files, a candidate can submit different resumes, cover letters, portfolios, or other files for each job they apply to. Can I choose which job-specific fields and files to share with clients? Yes. When submitting candidates to clients, click Field Share with Clients and select which job-associated fields and job-associated files you want to share.

chunks.t: Job-Associated Fields and Files (New UI)
chunks.x: Job-associated fields and files in Recruit CRM give you the flexibility to collect, store, and share candidate information that's specific to each job opening. Whether you're capturing job-specific answers through the application form, managing role-specific resumes and documents, or sharing relevant details with clients, these features help you keep candidate data organized and relevant across every position they're considered for. chunks.t: How to use Direct Apply for Seek

chunks.t: Adding records in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: Recruit CRM allows you to manually add Candidates, Contacts, Companies, and Jobs using the Global Add menu or directly from the respective List View . You can also add Candidates, Contacts, and Companies using the Recruit CRM Chrome Extension . When adding a Candidate, Recruit CRM also checks for potential duplicates. If a duplicate Candidate is detected and new or changed information is available, you can compare the existing and incoming information before deciding which fields to update. Manually add Candidates, Contacts, Companies, or Jobs to Recruit CRM. Review and manage new information when a duplicate Candidate is detected.

chunks.t: Adding records in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: Update selected fields or only populate empty fields on an existing Candidate. Add standardized location information using address suggestions and auto-fill. When adding a job, you must associate it with a company using the Company Name field. Your ability to add or edit records may depend on your role and permissions set by your Recruit CRM admin. The Chrome extension is an additional option and requires separate installation and setup. Click the Plus (+) / Global Add button at the top-right corner of your Recruit CRM window. Enter the Candidate's details in the Add Candidate form. Once you have entered the required information, click Submit to add the Candidate.

chunks.t: Adding records in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: What happens if a duplicate Candidate is detected? When you submit the Add Candidate form, Recruit CRM checks whether the candidate already exists. If new or changed information is available, a comparison window appears, displaying the existing and incoming values side by side. Compare existing and incoming values side by side for all changed or newly available fields. Incoming values can be edited directly within the comparison modal before updating the candidate. You can choose exactly which fields to overwrite or use Update Empty Fields Only to populate only blank fields. Required fields are validated before applying updates to prevent incomplete candidate records.

chunks.t: Adding records in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: Note: If no new information is available to update, the comparison modal is skipped, and you are taken directly to the existing candidate profile with a notification that no update was needed. Click the Candidates tab from the left-side menu to open the Candidate List View. Enter the Candidate's details in the Add Candidate form. You can also add Candidates, Contacts, and Companies to Recruit CRM using the Recruit CRM Chrome Extension . Install and open the Recruit CRM Chrome Extension. Navigate to the profile or page from which you want to add the record. Follow the prompts in the extension to capture the information and add the record to Recruit CRM.

chunks.t: Adding records in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: For detailed instructions on installing and using the extension, refer to the Recruit CRM Chrome Extension article. When adding a Job, the Company Name field is mandatory because every Job must be associated with a Company. Start typing the name of the Company in the Company Name field. Recruit CRM will display matching Companies as you type. You can select an existing Company or create a new Company if it does not already exist. Recruit CRM provides standardized location fields when adding Candidates, Contacts, Companies, and Jobs. The Postal Code field is available alongside the Full Address, Locality, City, State, and Country fields.

chunks.t: Adding records in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: You can search using a Street Address, City, State, or Postal Code to view address suggestions while adding a Candidate, Contact, Company, or Job. When you enter a Postal Code, Recruit CRM uses geocoding services to automatically populate the corresponding City, State, and Country . You can manually edit any of the populated location fields if required. Note: The address suggestion feature is available on external pages and on the Chrome Extension. Problem: The company you expect does not appear in the dropdown when adding a job Likely cause: The company has not been created yet, or the name is being typed differently.

chunks.t: Adding records in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: What to check: Check the spelling and try typing more characters of the company name. Resolution path: If no match appears, use the option offered in the dropdown to create a new company record, then associate it with the job. By using the global add menu, the List view, or the Chrome extension, you can quickly add records manually in Recruit CRM. Bulk Importing Records into Recruit CRM (New UI)

Keep the candidate profile organized according to your workflow. The Candidate Actions section lets you perform several actions directly from the top corner of the candidate profile, including:

chunks.t: New Version of Candidate Details Page
chunks.x: You can also customize these actions and keep your most frequently used actions easily accessible. Click the three dots on the candidate's details page and select Customize Options . chunks.x: Click here to know more about linking Candidate to contact The Information Overview section contains essential candidate fields in one place. chunks.t: New Version of Candidate Details Page

chunks.t: New Version of Candidate Details Page
chunks.x: Tailored Field Visibility: You can now fully customize the Information Overview section by selecting exactly how many fields you want to display. chunks.t: Customizing Fields on the Details Page
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Customizing fields on the profile page lets you reorder, replace, and add the fields shown in the Information Overview section for all record types, including candidates, companies, contacts, and jobs. This helps you display the most relevant information and customize the view based on your needs and workflows. Use this feature when you want to make record pages easier to scan and more relevant for your team to:

chunks.t: Customizing Fields on the Details Page
chunks.x: • Highlight key details like company, job title, or location for faster decision-making. • Standardize layouts across your team for consistency. • Show role-specific data such as skills or certifications. • Remove unnecessary fields to reduce clutter. • Ensure you have access to the relevant record type (candidates, companies, contacts, or jobs) • The steps below use the candidate profile as an example, but apply to all record types • Decide which fields you want to display, reorder, or hide before making changes. Step-by-step instructions to replace a field 1. From the candidate list page, open the specific candidate. 2. To replace any existing field on the profile:

chunks.t: Customizing Fields on the Details Page
chunks.x: Hover your mouse over the area next to the field name in the Information Overview section. When the pencil icon appears next to the field name, click it. 3. In the configuration box, click the Replace field option at the bottom of the box. • From the list, select the new field you want to use in place of the current one. • After selecting the desired field, click Replace . The selected field will immediately replace the existing one in the profile view Step-by-step instructions to Add/Remove or Reorder fields

chunks.t: Customizing Fields on the Details Page
chunks.x: 1. On the candidate profile page, click Customize Information Overview in the Information Overview section. You can access it by clicking the icon in the top right corner of the section. 2. Within the Customize Information Overview panel: To increase the number of fields visible , adjust the number of visible fields using the control provided. To add a new field , select any additional field you want to display from the available list. To reorder fields , drag and drop the fields into your desired order. To remove a field , simply deselect it by unchecking its checkbox.

chunks.t: Customizing Fields on the Details Page
chunks.x: After arranging the position of all fields and selecting any new fields that need to be added, click Save to apply your changes. Once saved, you will see a confirmation message indicating that your view was updated successfully. The Information Overview layout updates to reflect your selected fields and order. 1. Problem You cannot see a specific field when trying to replace, reorder, or add it. ​ ​ Likely cause The field’s visibility is turned off in Admin Settings for that record type. ​ ​ What to check • In Admin Settings , open the relevant record type (candidates, companies, contacts, or jobs). • Confirm that the field exists and that its visibility toggle is turned on.

chunks.t: Customizing Fields on the Details Page
chunks.x: • Turn the field visibility on (or toggle it off and on again). • Return to the profile page and open Customize Information Overview again to check if the field now appears. You changed the number of visible fields, but the layout doesn’t look updated. Changes were not saved after adjusting the number of visible fields or reordering. • Confirm that you clicked Save in the Customize Information Overview panel. • Check for the confirmation message that the view was updated successfully. • Reopen Customize Information Overview , verify your selections and order, and click Save again. • Refresh the profile page to confirm the updated layout.

chunks.t: Customizing Fields on the Details Page
chunks.x: After replacing a field, the information shown looks incorrect or incomplete. The new field type differs from the old one, or the data was not updated after the replacement. • Review the new field’s content on the profile page. • Confirm whether the new field expects different data (for example, text vs. date). • Add, correct, or confirm the information. • Click Save to ensure the new field stores the correct data. 1. Does customizing the candidate profile fields affect other users? No, customizing the fields and their order on the details page cannot affect how other users see that record type. However, the account can set a default view for all users.

chunks.t: Customizing Fields on the Details Page
chunks.x: 2. Can I use these steps for companies, contacts, and jobs as well? Yes. The same steps for replacing, reordering, and adding fields apply to all record types, including candidates, companies, contacts, and jobs. 3. What happens to existing data when I replace a field? When you replace a field, the new field type is applied. You should review, edit, or add information in the new field and click Save to confirm the data. 4. Can I undo changes to the field order or visibility? You can reopen Customize Information Overview at any time to change the visible fields and their order again. You can click on the Reset to Default button at the bottom to undo all your changes.

chunks.t: How to Create, Edit, and Manage Custom Fields in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: What does this feature do & when to use it? Custom fields in Recruit CRM allow you to capture and organize additional information for records such as Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Jobs & Deals. Using custom fields, you can tailor Recruit CRM to match your recruitment workflows and standardize data collection across the organization. On the Pro plan, you can create up to 15 custom fields per entity (candidates, companies, contacts, jobs, deals). On the Business plan, up to 100 custom fields per entity can be created. You need access to Admin Settings to create and manage custom fields. Deleting a custom field permanently deletes all data stored in that field.

chunks.t: How to Create, Edit, and Manage Custom Fields in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: 1. Navigate to Admin Settings in your Recruit CRM account. 2. Under Data Customization , select the entity (Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Jobs, or Deals) for which you want to add custom fields. 3. On the right side of the screen, click the + New Custom Field button. ​ 4. Create the new field by selecting the appropriate field type, entering the correct value or label, and then clicking Save Field . 5. After saving, you can find the newly created field under Additional Information (Custom Fields) in the list on the left.

chunks.t: How to Create, Edit, and Manage Custom Fields in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: Note: Once a custom field of a specific type is created, its type cannot be changed later. If you need a different type, create a new custom field and delete the old one. Deleting a custom field will permanently remove all data stored in that field. Supported Custom Field Types in Recruit CRM Text (You can add up to 2000 characters in this field) This field type is used to input the data of the "text" type. Long Text (You can add up to 5000 characters in this field.) This field type is used to add a paragraph. Client-facing summaries or internal private notes about a candidate This field type selects an option from a pre-defined set of values.

chunks.t: How to Create, Edit, and Manage Custom Fields in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: This field type is used to capture the phone number. You can click on the number to take further action. This field type selects multiple options from a pre-defined set of values. This field type is used to capture an email address. You can just click on the value inside this field and it will open a pop-up to compose an email. This field type is used to input the date. This field type is used to attach and upload files. This field type is only used to input the data of the "number" type. It will not allow any character or special characters in this field. Social Profile (You can read more about this in this article .)

chunks.t: How to Create, Edit, and Manage Custom Fields in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: This field type allows you to enter the URL for a social media app, creating an icon on the record for easy access. Clicking on the icon redirects you to the records' social media profile URL. This field type is used to capture the data of type "Yes" or "No". This field type is used to track and manage date and time details effectively and it supports MM-DD-YYYY, HH:MM format with a calendar and time picker (12-hour format). For eg, Jan 20, 2025, 12:30 PM Use dropdowns when values should remain standardized. Use multi-select fields when users may select multiple options. Use text fields only when flexible input is required. Use date fields for tracking milestones/date related data.

chunks.t: How to Create, Edit, and Manage Custom Fields in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: Use number fields to store numeric values. How to Rearrange Custom Fields and Sections 1. To customize the arrangement of fields and sections that appear when you manually add or edit candidates, contacts, companies, deals, or jobs, go to the respective field settings in Admin Settings . 2. Use drag-and-drop to reorder fields or entire sections to match your preferred layout. Now your fields will appear in the updated order when you add or edit profiles. ​ How to Replace Existing Fields with Custom Fields

chunks.t: How to Create, Edit, and Manage Custom Fields in Recruit CRM (New UI)
chunks.x: 1. On the profile layout, choose any field that you no longer want in that section. Hover over the existing field, click the pencil (edit) icon , and select Replace Field . Then select the custom field you created to replace the old one. 2. Once placed, the custom field will appear on all records for that entity, allowing users to enter and edit data directly in that field. Problem: I created a custom field, but I cannot see it on the profile page. Likely cause: The custom field is created but not added to the entity’s profile layout. ​ What to check: Confirm the field appears under Additional Information → Custom Fields for the correct entity and ensure the visibility toggle is enabled.

chunks.t: How to Create, Edit, and Manage Custom Fields in Recruit CRM (New UI)

chunks.t: Changing Hiring Stage (New UI)
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Hiring Stages help you track a candidate's progress throughout your recruitment process for each job they are assigned to. You can update hiring stages from both the Candidate Profile and the Job Details page, add remarks, create follow-up tasks, and maintain an accurate hiring history. Track a candidate's progress through your hiring pipeline. Update a candidate's hiring stage for a specific job. Add remarks or create follow-up tasks while changing a hiring stage. Bulk update hiring stages for multiple candidates. You can update a candidate's hiring stage from either the Candidate Profile/Details Page or the Job Details page.

chunks.t: Changing Hiring Stage (New UI)
chunks.x: 1. Update the hiring stage from the Candidate Profile Navigate to the Candidate entity and open the required candidate's profile. Open the Assigned Jobs tab, locate the relevant job, and click on the candidate's current Hiring Stage . Select the appropriate hiring stage from the dropdown list. The available stages are based on your Hiring Pipeline configuration, such as Shortlisted, Assigned, Interview, Rejected, Placed, and more. You can also add a remark or create a follow-up task before saving the stage update. Note: A red dot appears on the Remark icon whenever the candidate's current hiring stage includes a remark added by either you or the client.

chunks.t: Changing Hiring Stage (New UI)
chunks.x: Click the Remark icon to view the remark. When updating an individual candidate's hiring stage to Placed , you can also update the candidate's Current Salary by enabling the Update Current Salary toggle, clicking the Pencil icon, entering the updated salary, and saving the hiring stage. 2. Update the hiring stage from the Job Details page Navigate to Jobs and open the required job. Under the Candidate Pipeline tab, choose the relevant candidate and click on the candidate's current Hiring Stage . Select the appropriate stage from the dropdown menu and hit submit to save the changes You can also update hiring stages for multiple candidates; click View All from the Candidate Pipeline.

chunks.t: Changing Hiring Stage (New UI)

Open the candidate's Stage History and click the three-dot (⋮) menu beside the relevant entry. Please note: The Edit/Delete option is not available for stages or remarks added by the client, the initial Applied or Assigned stage in the candidate's current hiring history, or the latest Assigned stage created after a candidate has been unassigned and reassigned.
