chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: A CMS (Content Management System) is a tool that helps you create and manage multiple pieces of similar content without building each one as a separate page. For example, if you want to publish 50 blog posts, you do not need to design 50 individual pages. With a CMS, you design the structure once, add your content, and the website automatically uses that structure for each entry. Recruit Craft's Content Library is built directly into the Website Builder, allowing you to create, manage, customize, and publish repeatable content without using a separate CMS such as WordPress. You can use the CMS to create content such as:

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: The same content can be displayed across different pages of your website through a configurable CMS display section. 📌 Please note: The CMS is available only for Full Website projects . Career-Page-only projects do not have the CMS option. The Recruit Craft CMS is organized around four main components: Collections: Organize similar content into groups, such as Blog Posts or Team Members. Posts: Individual pieces of content within a collection. CMS display section: Displays posts from a collection on your website. Dynamic detail page: Automatically displays the full content of each post.

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: For example, you can create a Blog Posts collection, add multiple posts to it, and place a CMS section on your homepage to display those posts. Each post can also have its own automatically generated detail page. ​ Open your Full Website project in Recruit Craft. In the left sidebar, select Content Library . ​ A collection is a group of related content. Case Studies for customer success stories Open Content Library from the left-side panel once you are inside your project. Select the option to Create a collection.

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: Once the collection is created, you can start adding posts to it. Inside the Content Library, you can create and manage collections. Each collection displays its name, item count, and actions such as Rename and Delete. ​ Collection names must be unique within a project. A collection that contains posts cannot be deleted until its posts are removed. You can create up to 25 collections in a project. A post is an individual content item within a collection. For example, if you have a Blog Posts collection, each article you create within that collection is treated as a separate post. Each post can have its own content, featured image, writer, publish date, tags, excerpt, and SEO settings.

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: From the Content Library , open the collection where you want to add the content. For example, open your Blog Posts collection if you want to create a new blog article. Select the option to Create to add a post and open the post editor by entering the relevant Post Title. You can create the content manually using the rich text editor or use AI to generate an initial draft. ​ Click here to learn more about how to write and format your post Recruit Craft provides a rich text editor that lets you create and format your content directly within the post editor. You can either write the post manually or use AI to generate a first draft .

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: When generating a post with AI, you can provide details such as: Based on the information you provide, AI generates a draft and title for your post. You can then review, edit, and format the generated content directly in the post editor before publishing. This gives you the flexibility to use AI for the initial draft while retaining full control over the final content. Once you have added the main content, configure the information that will be used when the post is displayed on your website. ​ Click here to learn more about how to add post details Open the post Settings panel from the left side panel to configure details such as:

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: Featured image: Add the image that represents your post on CMS cards and other areas where the post is displayed. Alt text: Add alternative text to describe the featured image. Publish date: Set the date associated with the post. Author Name: Specify the person who wrote the post. Excerpt: Add a short preview of the post that can be displayed on content cards. Tags: Add tags to categorize or describe the post. If you leave the Excerpt field blank, Recruit Craft automatically uses the beginning of the post body as the excerpt.

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: If Writer or Tags are left blank, these fields will not be displayed on the content card. You can also control the visibility of the publish date, writer, and tags through the Website Builder settings. Each CMS post has its own SEO configuration , allowing you to configure how that specific post is represented for search engines and shared content. You can access the SEO Settings by clicking on the 3 dots under the Action panel. ​ Click here to learn more about the SEO settings You can configure the following SEO fields: Route/URL: Set the URL route for the post. Page title: Define the title used for the page. Page description: Add a description for the post.

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: Metadata: Configure additional metadata for the page. Thumbnail: Set the image used for the page's SEO/social representation. ​ Because these settings are available at the individual post level, you can configure SEO information separately for each piece of CMS content. Once you have completed the content, post details, and SEO settings, you can save the post as a Draft or Publish it. You can publish a post in either of the following ways: While creating or editing the post: Click the Publish button at the top of the post editor to publish it directly. From the collection: Locate the post in the collection and select Publish from its Actions panel.

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: The post can have one of the following statuses: Draft: Keeps the post in the CMS without displaying it on the live website. Published: Makes the post eligible to appear on your live website when the relevant CMS section is mapped to the collection. 📌 Please note: A post title is required before you can save or publish the post. Each collection has a dedicated post list where you can view and manage all the content within it. The list displays the post name, publish date, and status , with posts marked as either Draft or Published . You can also search by post name and filter posts by publish date or status to quickly find the content you need. ​

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: From the Actions menu for a post, you can publish , move a published post back to Draft by unpublishing it , pin or unpin it, rename the title, manage the SEO Settings or delete it. Pinning a post keeps it at the top of both the collection's post list and the live CMS card order , regardless of its publish date. By default, pinned posts appear first, followed by the newest posts based on publish date. Deleting a post is permanent and requires confirmation. ​ When you need to manage multiple posts at once, select the relevant posts and use bulk actions to Publish , Unpublish and move them to Draft, or delete them. ​

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: Once you have created posts, you can display them on your website using the Blog section . The Blog section is a draggable section that connects to a CMS collection and displays its posts as cards. 1. Open the page where you want to display the content. ​ 3. From the settings on the right, select the collection you want to display. 4. Configure the card layout and design . Click here to learn more about customizing Blog cards and layout The Blog section uses a shared card design for all posts in the selected collection. Cards can display the featured image, title, excerpt, writer, publish date, and tags .

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: You can control the visibility of available metadata and customize the elements displayed on the card. Any styling changes made to one card are applied across all posts in the collection, while the content remains unique to each post. Use the Blog Layout settings to control how the cards are arranged and displayed. You can configure the number of cards displayed per row and the number of posts shown at a time. The layout also adapts to mobile and tablet screens. ​ You can display up to 10 posts at a time. 5. Configure Pagination based on how you want to display your posts. Click here to learn more about using the Blog section as a teaser

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: To display a limited number of posts, such as the latest articles on your homepage, turn Pagination off . This displays a finite set of cards and allows you to direct visitors to a separate page containing the complete collection. Turn Pagination off from the Blog Layout settings. Configure the number of cards you want to display. When a visitor selects a post from a CMS card, the Read More link automatically takes them to that post's dynamic detail page. The link is generated using the post's slug , so you do not need to manually create a separate link for each post. ​ 📌 Please note: The Read More button must be linked before the section can be saved or published. ​

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: Click here to learn more about creating a full blog using pagination To create a complete blog listing page, turn Pagination on . Posts are displayed across numbered pages, with up to 10 posts per page . Set the number of posts to display per page. Customize the surrounding sections of the page as required. The Blog section itself becomes the full blog listing, so you do not need to create a separate page specifically for pagination. Each numbered page is individually reachable. ​ 📌 Please note: Recruit Craft does not provide a predefined full blog page. You create the page yourself by adding a Blog section, enabling pagination, and customizing the surrounding sections.

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: Before a collection is connected, the Blog section displays sample cards so you can preview the layout. Once you select a collection, its posts are used to populate the cards. An unmapped Blog section cannot be published to the live website. ​ When you add the first post to a collection, Recruit Craft automatically creates a dynamic detail page for that collection. The page is named after the collection and is used to display the full content of each post. ​ CMS publishing works independently from publishing the entire website. When you publish a CMS post, the post automatically becomes available on the live website, provided the CMS section is mapped to its collection.

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: You do not need to republish the entire website every time you publish a post. The post can have a Published status, but it will not appear on the live website until the website itself is published. Only posts with a Published status appear on the live website. Draft posts remain available in the editor and preview but are not displayed to visitors. If a CMS section is mapped to a collection that does not contain any published posts, the CMS content does not appear on the main website. Where can I find the CMS/ Content Library? The CMS is available in the Website Builder left sidebar as Content Library, below Pages Management . It is available only for Full Website projects .

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: What can I use the CMS/ Content Library for? You can use collections to manage any repeatable content type, such as blog posts, team members, testimonials, case studies, resources, and company news. Do I need WordPress or another external CMS? No. You can create, manage, customize, and publish your CMS content directly inside Recruit Craft. Yes. You can provide the topic, tone, word count, and preferences for images and tags. AI generates a draft and title, which you can then edit before publishing. Do I need to republish my website after publishing a CMS post?

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: No, if the website is already published. A published CMS post goes live automatically when its collection is mapped to a CMS section. If the website has not been published yet, the post will appear once you publish the website. Can I show a few posts on my homepage and have a full blog on another page? Yes. Turn Pagination off for a teaser section with a Read More button, and turn Pagination on for a full blog page with numbered pages. Do I need to create a separate page for every CMS post? No. Each collection gets a dynamic detail page that can display every post in that collection. Read More links automatically take visitors to the relevant post using its slug.

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: Can I control what information appears on a CMS card? Yes. You can customize the card and control the visibility of information such as the writer, publish date, and tags. The card styling is shared across posts in the collection. Will draft posts appear on my live website? No. Only published posts appear on the live website. Drafts remain available in the editor and preview. Yes. You can pin a post to keep it at the top of both the collection list and the live card order, regardless of its publish date. You can create up to 25 collections in a CMS project.

chunks.t: Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: The Recruit Craft CMS lets you manage repeatable website content without creating and maintaining every page individually. You can create collections, add and manage posts, write content manually or generate a first draft with AI, configure SEO for individual posts, display content through customizable CMS sections, and automatically provide dynamic detail pages for each entry. You can use these capabilities to build blogs, team directories, testimonials, resources, and other content-driven sections while keeping content and website management within Recruit Craft. Building a Custom Careers Page with the Recruit Craft Website Editor How to Create a Website Using Recruit Craft

chunks.t: How Google for Jobs Works With Your Recruit Craft Career Page
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? When you publish a job on your Recruit Craft career page, Recruit Craft automatically submits the job details to Google for Jobs , Google's job search experience. This gives candidates another way to discover your open positions when searching on Google. There is no separate setup required. Recruit Craft automatically creates the information Google needs using the details already available in Recruit CRM. How Google for Jobs works with Recruit Craft Which Recruit CRM fields are sent to Google What to check if Google reports missing information

chunks.t: How Google for Jobs Works With Your Recruit Craft Career Page
chunks.x: Google for Jobs is a feature within Google Search that collects job listings from different websites and displays them in a dedicated job search experience. Candidates can use filters such as location and job type to find relevant opportunities. To make a job available for this experience, Google reads structured information from the job's webpage. Recruit Craft automatically creates this information for jobs published on your career page using the JobPosting format defined by Schema.org . You do not need to configure or manage this structured data yourself. Recruit Craft handles the formatting and uses the information stored in your Recruit CRM job record.

chunks.t: How Google for Jobs Works With Your Recruit Craft Career Page
chunks.x: When you publish a job, Recruit Craft takes the relevant information from the job record in Recruit CRM and maps it to the fields expected by Google. Some fields are always included because they are required for a valid job listing. Other fields are included only when the required information is available, or a specific setting has been enabled in Recruit CRM.

chunks.t: How Google for Jobs Works With Your Recruit Craft Career Page
chunks.x: 📌 Please note: Having complete and valid job information does not guarantee that the job will appear in Google for Jobs. Google decides which jobs are indexed and displayed based on its own indexing and ranking process. Recruit Craft follows Google's recommended structured data practices, so keeping your job information complete gives your listing the best possible chance of being picked up accurately. The table below shows the information Recruit Craft can send to Google, where the information comes from in Recruit CRM, and when it is included. Job address including street, locality, state or province, postal code, and country Street Address, Locality, State/Province, Postal Code, Country

chunks.t: How Google for Jobs Works With Your Recruit Craft Career Page
chunks.x: Only when Job Location Type is set to Remote Country candidates must be located in for remote jobs Only when the job is Remote and a Country is set Employment type such as full time or part time Only when the Job Type can be matched to a type recognized by Google Salary Currency, Minimum Annual Salary, Maximum Annual Salary Only when the salary range is visible on the job card in Recruit Craft and the relevant value is available Your company's identifying name on Recruit Craft Whether candidates can apply directly from Google Only when available on the job card in Recruit Craft

chunks.t: How Google for Jobs Works With Your Recruit Craft Career Page
chunks.x: Always. When company information is configured and visible on the job, Google uses the job's Company Name. Otherwise, it uses the Recruit Craft Company Name. When company information is configured and visible on the job, and a Company Logo is available. When company information is configured and visible on the job, and a Company Website is available. Company information is available to Google when either of these fields is configured and visible on the job: When either field is configured and visible, Google uses the Company Name from that job. If the job also has a Company Logo or Company Website, those details are included as well.

chunks.t: How Google for Jobs Works With Your Recruit Craft Career Page
chunks.x: If neither field is configured and visible, Google uses the Recruit Craft Company Name instead. The Company Logo and Company Website are not included in this case. ​ Will my job definitely appear in Google for Jobs if every required field is filled in? No. Google decides which jobs are indexed and displayed through its own indexing and ranking process. Recruit Craft cannot guarantee that a particular job will appear. Keeping the job information complete and valid gives it the best possible chance of being picked up by Google. What happens if an optional field is missing?

chunks.t: How Google for Jobs Works With Your Recruit Craft Career Page
chunks.x: The job can still be submitted to Google for Jobs. If an optional field does not have the required information, that field is simply left out of the listing. Why does my company name sometimes look different on Google compared to my career page? This depends on the company field mapping on the job. If a Company Image or Company Text field is mapped, Google uses the company information associated with that job. If neither is mapped, Google uses your Recruit Craft Company Name . Can I choose which jobs are sent to Google for Jobs?

chunks.t: How Google for Jobs Works With Your Recruit Craft Career Page
chunks.x: Jobs published on your Recruit Craft career page are submitted automatically. The information included in the Google listing depends on how complete the job details are in Recruit CRM. Recruit Craft automatically prepares your published jobs for Google for Jobs using the information stored in Recruit CRM. Keeping your job records complete, especially details such as location, salary, employment type, and company information, helps ensure that your listings are prepared with the information Google expects and gives them the best possible chance of appearing accurately in Google for Jobs. Recruit Craft: No-Code Career Page & Candidate Portal Builder

chunks.t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
chunks.x: This article explains how to connect a domain managed through Cloudflare to your Recruit Craft career page. You can connect either your full domain, such as yourcompany.com , or a subdomain, such as careers.yourcompany.com . You will first generate the required DNS records in Recruit Craft, add them to Cloudflare, and then wait for the domain to be verified. A subdomain uses CNAME records throughout. A full domain uses a CNAME for SSL verification and one or more A records to point your domain to your Website. Access to the Cloudflare account that manages your domain. Your domain set up with Cloudflare's Full DNS setup , meaning its nameservers point to Cloudflare.

chunks.t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
chunks.x: The domain or subdomain you want to use for your career page. ​ Generate your DNS records in Recruit Craft Before adding anything to Cloudflare, generate the DNS records required for your custom domain in Recruit Craft. In Recruit Craft, go to Custom Domain from the panel on the left. Under Default Project URL , set a unique name for your project and click Save . For a full domain setup, this name must match the domain you want to connect. Under Custom Domain , enter your domain in both fields to confirm it, then click Connect . In Recruit Craft, go to Custom Domain from the panel on the left.

chunks.t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
chunks.x: Under Custom Domain , enter your preferred career page subdomain in both fields to confirm it, then click Connect . Make sure the subdomain matches the name of your Default Project URL . For a subdomain, Recruit Craft generates two CNAME records. A CNAME (Canonical Name) record is a type of DNS record that directs a domain or subdomain to another address. Copy the Name and Value for both records. Record 1: Used to verify your SSL certificate and secure your career page connection. Record 2: Used to point your subdomain to your Recruit Craft career page. ​

chunks.t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
chunks.x: For a full domain, Recruit Craft generates a CNAME record for SSL verification, plus one or more A records with static IP addresses to point your domain to your career page. Please note: Keep both CNAME records handy before moving to Cloudflare. You will need to add both records. ​ Once you have your records from Recruit Craft, add them to your domain's DNS settings in Cloudflare. Log in to Cloudflare and select your domain. Go to DNS > Records from the panel on your left. Click Add record and select CNAME as the record Type . ​ In the Name field, enter the Name provided by Recruit Craft exactly as shown, including the domain. ​

chunks.t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
chunks.x: In the Target field, enter the Value provided by Recruit Craft. ​ For the second record, click Add record again and select A as the record Type instead of CNAME. In the Name field, enter your root domain, for example, yourcompany.com. In the IPv4 address field, enter the static IP address Recruit Craft provided. Set Proxy status to DNS only. Click Save. ​ If Recruit Craft provided a second static IP address, repeat this step with the same Name and the second IP address.

chunks.t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
chunks.x: Please note: A CNAME record can't normally be set on a root domain, since it can't share a name with the NS and SOA records already there. Recruit Craft avoids this by pointing your root domain directly at one or more static IP addresses using A records instead. If two IP addresses are provided, both A records share the same Name — this is a standard DNS pattern called round robin, distributing traffic across multiple IP addresses serving identical content. Log in to Cloudflare and select your domain. ​ Click Add record and select CNAME as the record Type . ​ In the Name field, enter the Name provided by Recruit Craft exactly as shown, including the domain. ​

chunks.t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
chunks.x: In the Target field, enter the Value provided by Recruit Craft. ​ Repeat steps 3 to 7 for the second CNAME record. For this record, use your subdomain as the Name , for example, careers.yourcompany.com . Please note: Set both CNAME records to DNS only . Do not enable Cloudflare's proxy for these records. Cloudflare does not automatically add your domain to the Name field. Enter the Name exactly as it appears in Recruit Craft for both CNAME records. For example, if Recruit Craft provides a Name that includes your complete domain, copy the complete value into Cloudflare. After saving the CNAME records, the DNS changes need some time to become available.

chunks.t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
chunks.x: Since Cloudflare is the authoritative DNS provider when your domain uses its Full DNS setup, the changes typically take effect within five minutes or less . If your custom domain does not work immediately, wait a few minutes and check again. Once the DNS records have propagated, return to Recruit Craft to continue or verify your custom domain setup. Recruit Craft may take up to 5 hours to verify the records after they become available. Problem: Recruit Craft is asking you to add CAA records before you can continue with custom domain setup.

chunks.t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
chunks.x: Why this is required: Recruit Craft uses AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue the SSL certificate for your custom domain. The CAA record authorizes Amazon to issue a certificate for your domain. If Recruit Craft displays CAA records during the custom domain setup, you must add those records to your DNS provider and verify them before you can proceed to the CNAME records. ​ ​ Resolution: If Recruit Craft provides a CAA record, add the record to Cloudflare exactly as shown in the Recruit Craft custom domain setup.

chunks.t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
chunks.x: To add the record in Cloudflare: 1. Log in to Cloudflare and select your domain. 2. Go to DNS > Records . 3. Select Add record and choose CAA as the record type. 4. In Name , enter the name provided by Recruit Craft. 5. Cloudflare separates the CAA value into multiple fields. If Recruit Craft provides: ​ 0 issue " amazon.com " enter the values as: ​ Flags: 0 ​ Tag: Issue ​ CA domain name: amazon.com 6. Leave TTL set to Auto . 7. Select Save . 8. Return to Recruit Craft and select Verify . ​ Do not enter 0 issue " amazon.com " as a single value in Cloudflare. Cloudflare requires the CAA value to be entered separately as Flags , Tag , and CA domain name .

chunks.t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
chunks.x: Once the CAA record has been successfully verified, Recruit Craft will allow you to continue with the CNAME record setup. If Recruit Craft provides a CAA record, use the values provided there rather than creating a different CAA record. If you already have CAA records for other certificate authorities, do not remove them unless you understand the impact of doing so. Can I connect my root domain, like yourcompany.com? Yes. Full domain setup uses A records rather than CNAME for the record that points your domain to your career page. A records work at the root domain on every provider, Cloudflare included, so this covers full domain setups directly with static IP addresses.

chunks.t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
chunks.x: Should I use Proxy or DNS only for these records? Use DNS only for both CNAME records. Cloudflare proxying is not required for this setup. What if Cloudflare says the name is already in use? This usually means another DNS record already exists with the same name. Check your existing DNS records and edit or remove the conflicting record before adding the CNAME provided by Recruit Craft. How long does it take for my custom domain to work? DNS changes on Cloudflare typically take effect within a few minutes. After the records are live, Recruit Craft may take up to 5 hours to verify the connection.

chunks.t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
chunks.x: Adding the DNS records provided by Recruit Craft to your Cloudflare DNS settings connects your custom domain or subdomain to your Recruit Craft career page. A subdomain uses CNAME records throughout; a full domain uses a CNAME for SSL verification plus one or more A records. Once the DNS changes have propagated, return to Recruit Craft to complete or verify the connection. chunks.t: WhatsApp Integration: Message Candidates & Contacts Right Inside Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? The WhatsApp Integration helps recruiters manage candidate and contact communication without switching between Recruit CRM and WhatsApp. Communicate with Candidates and Contacts directly from Recruit CRM. Manage WhatsApp and LinkedIn conversations from one place. Send attachments and voice messages during conversations. Keep conversations accessible while working on other Recruit CRM pages. Control who can view your WhatsApp conversations. Please note: This feature is currently in Beta and will be gradually rolled out to all users. You can connect your WhatsApp account from Profile Settings → WhatsApp Integration .

chunks.t: WhatsApp Integration: Message Candidates & Contacts Right Inside Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Go to Profile Settings → WhatsApp Integration and click Connect . A QR code will be displayed. Open WhatsApp, go to Linked Devices , and scan the QR code to connect your account. You can also use the pairing code method. Once WhatsApp is connected, you can communicate with Candidates and Contacts directly from their Recruit CRM profiles. To start a WhatsApp conversation, the Candidate or Contact must have a WhatsApp-linked phone number saved in the default phone number field .

chunks.t: WhatsApp Integration: Message Candidates & Contacts Right Inside Recruit CRM
chunks.x: If no phone number is available, Recruit CRM prompts you to add one. If the saved number is not associated with a WhatsApp account, Recruit CRM informs you that a WhatsApp conversation cannot be started with that number. View conversations from other team members, depending on message privacy settings. Use AI Assist to draft WhatsApp and LinkedIn messages. WhatsApp, LinkedIn Classic, and LinkedIn InMail conversations are available through a common Messaging interface.

chunks.t: WhatsApp Integration: Message Candidates & Contacts Right Inside Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You can search conversations and filter them by messaging channel. All Chats is selected by default. From the conversation screen, you can also switch between available messaging channels without leaving the Candidate or Contact profile. If both LinkedIn and WhatsApp are connected, LinkedIn is shown as the default channel . Recruit CRM remembers your selected messaging channel, so your preference is retained when you return to the Messaging widget. You can send attachments directly from WhatsApp conversations in Recruit CRM. Files received from Candidates or Contacts can also be opened or downloaded from the conversation.

chunks.t: WhatsApp Integration: Message Candidates & Contacts Right Inside Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You can record and send WhatsApp audio messages directly from Recruit CRM. This provides a similar experience to sending voice messages directly from WhatsApp. Delivery status is displayed directly on sent WhatsApp messages: Single tick: Message sent but not delivered. Double tick: Message delivered but not seen. Blue double tick: Message delivered and seen. Please note: Read status updates may take slightly longer to appear in Recruit CRM than in WhatsApp.

chunks.t: WhatsApp Integration: Message Candidates & Contacts Right Inside Recruit CRM
chunks.x: If a user selects Delete for Me/Delete for Everyone in WhatsApp, the message will not remain visible in the corresponding conversation in Recruit CRM, as the deletion is not synced to Recruit CRM. The 'Deleted for Everyone ' tag message that we get in WhatsApp will not be synced as well. Recruiters also receive an in-app notification when a new WhatsApp reply is received. WhatsApp conversations can be docked at the bottom of Recruit CRM, allowing you to continue chatting while working on other pages.

chunks.t: WhatsApp Integration: Message Candidates & Contacts Right Inside Recruit CRM
chunks.x: You can keep up to two conversations docked at the same time. Docked conversations can be minimized, maximized, closed, or dragged horizontally to change their position. If a third conversation is opened, it replaces the oldest docked conversation. Control who can see your WhatsApp messages The Hide my messages setting is available for connected WhatsApp accounts under Messaging Integration . You can continue viewing your own conversations. You can continue viewing teammates' conversations where permitted. Other teammates cannot view your WhatsApp conversations. When disabled, teammates can view the conversations through Team Chats under the specific profile.

chunks.t: WhatsApp Integration: Message Candidates & Contacts Right Inside Recruit CRM
chunks.x: WhatsApp Integration uses a credit-based model. The cost is 100 Recruit CRM Credits per connected user for 30 days. WhatsApp access remains active for 30 days. Access automatically renews after 30 days if the option remains enabled. If disabled before renewal, no additional credits are deducted, and access ends at the end of the current period. You can track deductions through WhatsApp Credit History in RCRM Credits . If Recruit CRM cannot process the required credits, the connected user receives an in-app notification with an option to add more credits.

chunks.t: WhatsApp Integration: Message Candidates & Contacts Right Inside Recruit CRM
chunks.x: Likely cause: The Candidate or Contact does not have a WhatsApp-linked number saved in the default phone number field, or the saved number is not associated with WhatsApp. What to check: Confirm that the correct phone number is saved in the default phone number field and that the number is linked to WhatsApp. Resolution: Update the phone number if needed and try starting the conversation again. Recruit CRM will indicate when the saved number is not available on WhatsApp. Teammates cannot see WhatsApp conversations Likely Cause: The Hide my messages setting is enabled under Messaging Integration, which restricts other teammates from viewing the user's WhatsApp conversations.

chunks.t: WhatsApp Integration: Message Candidates & Contacts Right Inside Recruit CRM
chunks.x: What to check: Review the Hide my messages setting under Messaging Integration. Resolution: If the setting is enabled, disable it to allow the conversations to be visible to permitted teammates through Team Chats . WhatsApp Integration brings candidate and contact communication directly into Recruit CRM, making it easier to manage WhatsApp and LinkedIn conversations from one place. With support for attachments, audio messages, delivery statuses, message privacy, notifications, and docked conversations, recruiters can keep their communication workflow within Recruit CRM. chunks.t: Contractor Invoices
chunks.x: What does this feature do and when to use it? Contractor Invoices helps agencies and contractors manage the invoicing process directly from approved timesheets. Generate invoices from approved contractor timesheets. Allow contractors to generate their own invoices. View, download, and delete generated invoices. Access invoices directly from their related timesheets. Contractor Invoicing must be enabled from the Timesheet form . The timesheet must be approved before a contractor invoice can be generated. Please note: The invoice setting is based on its state at the time the timesheet is approved. Changes made to the setting after approval do not affect previously approved timesheets.

chunks.t: Contractor Invoices
chunks.x: 1. Generate an invoice from the Contractor Portal Contractors can generate an invoice directly from an approved timesheet in the Contractor Portal . Open the desired approved timesheet . Click Generate in the top-right corner. The contractor invoice will be generated automatically. The generated invoice includes the relevant timesheet and payment information, such as: Work hours, overtime hours, and total hours for hourly timesheets Generate an invoice from the Agency Portal Agency users can generate contractor invoices from the Agency Portal for either a single timesheet or multiple timesheets in bulk.

chunks.t: Contractor Invoices
chunks.x: Go to the specific Job and, from the candidate pipeline, click View Timesheets for the contractor. Open the timesheet for which you want to generate an invoice. On the timesheet details page, under Contractor Invoice , click Generate . Select the timesheets for which you want to generate invoices. Click the dropdown arrow beside Create Invoice and select Create for Contractor. You can generate up to 15 invoices at a time . Before generating invoices, Recruit CRM checks whether each timesheet is eligible. An invoice will not be generated if: Contractor Invoicing is not enabled for the contractor. A contractor invoice has already been generated.

chunks.t: Contractor Invoices
chunks.x: The invoice will be generated for the selected timesheet and automatically linked to it. The contractor receives an email and an in-app notification when an agency user generates an invoice on their behalf. Contractors and agency users can manage generated invoices from the respective portal. Access an invoice directly from the related timesheet using the invoice link Recruit CRM sends notifications based on who generates the contractor invoice: Agency user generates an invoice: The contractor receives an email and an in-app notification. Contractor generates an invoice: The designated agency approver receives an email notification.

chunks.t: Contractor Invoices
chunks.x: Please note: Contractor invoices are not available on the Client Portal . 1. Can I enable Contractor Invoicing after a timesheet has already been approved? No. Enabling the setting after approval will not update previously approved timesheets. The setting is captured based on its status at the time of approval and will only apply to timesheets approved after it is enabled. 2. What happens if the contractor has already generated the invoice? The invoice will automatically be linked to the timesheet. Agency users can view and download the invoice from the relevant timesheet. 3. Can expenses be updated after a Contractor Invoice is generated?

chunks.t: Contractor Invoices
chunks.x: No. Once a Contractor Invoice has been generated, expense claims cannot be updated for that timesheet. Contractor Invoices simplifies the invoicing process by allowing agencies and 1099 contractors to generate invoices directly from approved timesheets. With individual and bulk invoice generation, invoice management, automatic timesheet linking, and notifications, agencies can manage contractor invoicing more efficiently. chunks.t: How to Delete a Custom Domain in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit Craft lets you delete a custom domain connection for your career page at any stage, whether you are still setting it up or it is already fully connected and live. Start over if you run into a problem while connecting a domain. Remove a custom domain you no longer want to use for your career page. Free up a domain or subdomain so you can connect a different one. You can delete a custom domain connection at any point during the setup process or after it has been fully connected. During setup: If you run into a problem while configuring the domain, you can delete the connection without completing the setup first and start again.

chunks.t: How to Delete a Custom Domain in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: After setup: Even after a domain has been fully connected and verified, you can delete it at any time. ​ When you delete a custom domain, Recruit Craft removes the domain connection from your account. This does not affect the DNS records configured with your domain provider. In Recruit Craft, go to Custom Domain from the panel on the left. Locate the custom domain integration you want to remove on the page, then click the Delete button in the bottom corner of the integration. A confirmation prompt will appear asking you to enter the domain name you want to delete.

chunks.t: How to Delete a Custom Domain in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: Select Delete Domain . You'll see a message confirming that the deletion process has begun. Please do not refresh the page while the domain is being deleted. The deletion may take a few seconds to process. Once it is complete, you'll see a Domain deleted successfully message to confirm. ​ Deleting a domain in Recruit Craft removes the connection on the Recruit Craft side only . It does not remove the CNAME records you added with your domain provider. If you no longer need those records, you must remove them separately from your domain provider.

chunks.t: How to Delete a Custom Domain in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: After the custom domain is deleted, your career page will no longer be available at that custom domain. It will remain accessible through its default Recruit Craft URL until you connect another custom domain. You can start the custom domain connection process again at any time, either with the same domain or with a different one. Can I delete a domain before it's fully verified? Yes. You can delete a custom domain at any stage of the setup process. If you run into a problem while configuring it, you can delete the connection and start again. What happens to my career page after I delete a custom domain?

chunks.t: How to Delete a Custom Domain in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: Your career page remains available at its default Recruit Craft URL . It will no longer be accessible through the custom domain you deleted. Do I need to remove the DNS records at my domain provider too? Recruit Craft only removes the custom domain connection from its side. The CNAME records you added at your domain provider remain there. If you no longer need them, remove them separately from your provider. Can I connect a new domain after deleting the old one? Yes. You can start the custom domain connection process again at any time, either for the same domain or for a different one.

chunks.t: How to Delete a Custom Domain in Recruit Craft
chunks.x: You can delete a custom domain from Recruit Craft at any stage, whether you are restarting an incomplete setup or removing a domain that you no longer need. Deleting the connection does not affect your career page itself, which remains available through its default Recruit Craft URL. If needed, you can connect the same domain again or set up a different custom domain at any time. chunks.t: Daily Timesheets
chunks.x: What this feature does and when to use it The Per Day Rate Type lets you pay and bill contractors based on the number of days worked instead of hours worked and create Daily Timesheets. You can select Per Hour or Per Day for Contract and Contract-to-Perm jobs. The selected Rate Type determines how Pay Rate, Bill Rate, timesheet entries, invoicing, and reporting are calculated. ​ You pay or bill contractors based on a daily rate. You want to track attendance as Full Day, Half Day, or No Show instead of hours. You want timesheets, invoices, exports, and reports to reflect days worked. Per Hour is selected by default. Select Per Day when you want to manage the contractor based on days worked.

chunks.t: Daily Timesheets
chunks.x: The Rate Type and Work Schedule are captured when a timesheet is created. Changes made afterward apply only to newly created timesheets. Existing timesheets continue to use the settings they were created with. Per Day timesheets do not require a Rule Template . Instead, you configure the contractor's Work Schedule directly in the Enable Timesheet form. Go to Jobs and open a Contract or Contract-to-Perm job, or create a new one. Per Hour : Contractors are paid and billed based on hours worked. Per Day : Contractors are paid and billed based on days worked. ​ Enabling Per Day timesheets for a candidate

chunks.t: Daily Timesheets
chunks.x: Once you select Per Day as the Rate Type for the job, you can enable a Per Day timesheet for individual candidates in the Candidate Pipeline. When enabling the timesheet, define the contractor's Work Schedule, Pay Rate, and Bill Rate so the timesheet can calculate daily pay and billing correctly. Open the job and scroll to the Candidate Pipeline . ​ Click Enable Timesheet on the candidate's card. In the Enable Timesheet window, select Per Day as the Rate Type. ​ Under Work Schedule , select the days the contractor is expected to work. Any day you do not select is treated as a day off. Enter the contractor's Pay Rate and Bill Rate . ​

chunks.t: Daily Timesheets
chunks.x: Please note: Per Day timesheets do not use a Rule Template . You only need to select the Work Schedule that applies to the contractor. ​ After the timesheet is enabled, you can record the contractor's attendance for each scheduled working day. Instead of entering the number of hours worked, select the attendance status that applies to each day. For each working day, select the appropriate attendance type: Full Day: Counts as 1 day and applies the full daily Pay Rate and Bill Rate. Half Day: Counts as 0.5 day and applies 0.5x the daily Pay Rate and Bill Rate. No Show: Counts as 0 days and applies 0x the daily Pay Rate and Bill Rate. ​

chunks.t: Daily Timesheets
chunks.x: For example, if the daily rate is $100 , a Full Day is $100 , a Half Day is $50 , and a No Show is $0 . ​ ​ Total Work Days are calculated automatically based on the attendance entries. For example, 4 Full Days + 1 Half Day = 4.5 Total Work Days . ​ Click Submit once all entries are complete. ​ Rate Type and Total Work Days are available as columns on the Timesheets page . You can also filter timesheets by Rate Type and select: If you need to update multiple Per Day timesheets at once, you can use the bulk time entry options from supported Timesheet views. The selected timesheets must use the same Rate Type for the bulk action to work. Select the timesheets you want to update in bulk. ​

chunks.t: Daily Timesheets
chunks.x: Make sure the selected timesheets use the same Rate Type . The Rate Type of the first selected timesheet is used as the reference. ​ If the selected timesheets use different Rate Types, you'll see "Timesheet setting is different." Enter Full Day, Half Day, or No Show for the relevant dates. Use Copy to All or Copy to Period to apply entries across the selected timesheets. ​ Here is how you can bulk update timesheets on the Timesheets Page- Here is how you can bulk update timesheets from the Job- Total Work Days is displayed for the selected Per Day timesheets.

chunks.t: Daily Timesheets
chunks.x: Approved Per Day timesheets can be used to create invoices based on the total number of billable days. When creating the invoice, make sure the selected timesheets use the same work schedule type so the appropriate invoice template can be applied. Select the approved Per Day timesheets you want to invoice. The selected timesheets must use the same work schedule type. Then click the Create Invoice button at the top. You can see that the invoice template has been by defualt selected as the Per Day invoice template. The template includes Description, Number of Days, and Amount . Here, enter the description details and click on Create Invoice. ​

chunks.t: Daily Timesheets
chunks.x: Number of Days represents the total billable units: For example, 4 Full Days + 1 Half Day = 4.5 days on the invoice. Review and save the invoice as you would for other timesheet invoices. Viewing Per Day data in Billing and Revenue Report Go to Reports and open the Billing & Revenue Report . In the KPIs dropdown, select Total Billable & Payable Days . The KPI is calculated from approved Per Day timesheets, including half days. For example, 43 Full Days + 0.5 Day = 43.5 days . You can generate the report for Overall, Company, Job, and Contractor report types. ​ Rate Type and Total Days are available as export fields for Per Day timesheets.

chunks.t: Daily Timesheets
chunks.x: Day-wise exports show whether each day was logged as a Full Day or Half Day . Hour-based fields remain empty for Per Day timesheets, while Per Day-specific fields remain empty for Per Hour timesheets. Per Day timesheets in the Contractor and Client Portals Per Day timesheets are also supported in the Contractor Portal and Client Portal . Timesheets created through these portals follow the Rate Type configured for the contractor . Contractors configured with Per Day can submit Full Day, Half Day, or No Show entries through the portal. Per Day allows you to pay and bill contractors based on the number of days worked instead of hours worked.

chunks.t: Daily Timesheets
chunks.x: A Full Day counts as 1 day and applies the full daily Pay Rate and Bill Rate. A Half Day counts as 0.5 day and applies half of the daily Pay Rate and Bill Rate. Full Days count as 1 and Half Days count as 0.5 . For example, 5 Full Days + 2 Half Days = 6 Total Days . Can I change the Rate Type after timesheets have already been created? Yes. However, the change applies only to newly created timesheets . Existing timesheets continue to use the Rate Type that was configured when they were created. Do Per Day timesheets require a Rule Template?

chunks.t: Daily Timesheets
chunks.x: No. Per Day timesheets do not require a Rule Template . You only need to select Per Day as the Rate Type and configure the required Work Schedule in the Enable Timesheet form. The Per Day Rate Type lets you manage contractor pay and billing based on days worked rather than hours. With Full Day, Half Day, and No Show entries, the selected rate type carries through timesheets, bulk actions, invoicing, exports, reporting, and the Contractor and Client Portals.
